title.en: Chapter One: Ruins in the Rain

zh: 南城的秋雨，从来都下得黏腻而绵长。
从入夜开始，细密冷雨就没停过，层层叠叠的水雾压在城市上空，把整座城的灯火泡得朦胧昏沉。空气里裹挟着泥土潮湿的腥气，混着深秋草木腐烂的味道，闷得人胸口发紧。
夜里十点四十分。
城郊，三年前停工的锦绣澜庭烂尾工地。
这片占地极广的废弃工地早已被荒草和藤蔓侵占，数栋未完工的毛坯高楼骨架嶙峋，突兀刺破雨雾，在暗沉夜色里像几具死寂的骸骨。四周没有路灯，没有行人，远离居民区，是整片南城最荒芜、最僻静的死角。
警车的红蓝爆闪灯光，是这片死寂区域唯一的亮色。
三辆刑侦警车依次停在工地入口的土路旁，车轮碾过泥泞，压出深深的辙印。雨刷器不停摆动，却始终刷不净挡风玻璃上朦胧的雨雾。
警戒线已经拉起，明黄色的带子在风雨里轻轻晃动，隔绝出一片封闭的案发现场。辖区派出所的民警守在警戒线外，身姿挺拔，神色肃穆，将所有试图靠近的闲杂人等尽数拦在外面。
“市局重案组到。”
低声的通报穿透雨声。
车门被推开，冷凉的风雨瞬间灌了进来。
几道身影依次下车，没有人说话，没有多余的动作，默契得近乎本能。
最先落地的男人穿着深色通勤警服，身姿挺拔笔直，肩线利落。夜色压沉了他的眉眼，整张脸线条冷硬凌厉，周身带着一种久经大案沉淀下来的沉肃气场。他抬手拢了下领口，目光抬眼，直直穿透朦胧雨雾，落向深处漆黑的烂尾楼群，视线沉稳锐利，一瞬扫过整片荒芜工地。
“陸隊”
他没有多余问话，只沉声道了一句：“情况。”
守在一旁的辖区民警立刻上前汇报，声音压得很低，带着难以掩饰的紧绷：“十分钟前接到匿名报警，工地三号楼北侧空地发现人体残肢。我们到场确认，是碎尸现场，初步判定遇害者为一名成年男性，残肢散落范围大概二十平米，雨水冲刷严重，现场破坏度极高。”
“匿名报警？”
问话的人音色冷冽，没有起伏，是重案组队长，陆峥。
“是，号码查不到实名，拨完报警电话直接关机，追踪不到任何信号源。”辖区民警点头，“现场目前没有发现完整尸体，只有零碎骨块、皮肉组织，散落得很散。雨太大，很多痕迹已经被冲没了。”
话音落，身后几道身影已然行动起来。
身形利落的青年拎着沉重的现场勘查箱、物证收纳设备，快步踏入泥泞。他动作干脆迅捷，开箱、架设临时冷光源、固定现场点位，一气呵成，是组里负责痕迹物证勘查的苏晚。
另有一道高挑身影绕着警戒线外围快步绕行，脚步轻而稳，目光锐利扫过周边荒草、泥路、围墙死角，排查所有外来脚印、车辆停留痕迹，负责外勤摸排与现场布控，江驰。
还有一人靠在警车旁，手里捏着空白卷宗本，指尖悬在纸面上方，安静沉着，全程沉默梳理案件逻辑，负责侧写与线索整合，许砚。
最后走在队尾的人，一身干净无菌防护服，眉眼温顺清淡，待人永远温和耐心，哪怕面对最血腥的现场，情绪也从无波动，是组里的专职法医，沈予安。
沈予安戴好双层乳胶手套与防护口罩，眉眼温顺平静，哪怕即将面对血腥残酷的碎尸现场，神色里也没有半分紧绷和抵触，只有极致的耐心与审慎。
他抬手整理好防护服的袖口，确保没有一寸肌肤外露，动作细致周全，妥帖得让人安心。
“我先进场。”
他的声音很轻，温温软软，穿透嘈杂雨声，清晰落在几人耳中，“雨夜现场易二次破坏，我先固定尸块位置，初步筛查遗体残损特征，你们晚点再进，避免踩踏物证。”
陆峥微微颔首，语气简短沉稳：“注意脚下，优先固定残损痕迹，雨势还在变大。”
沈予安轻轻应了一声，转身踏入警戒线内。
雨丝落在他洁白的防护服上，晕开细小的湿痕。他走得很慢，步子极稳，每一步都精准落在裸露的硬土上，刻意避开所有松软泥泞、疑似残留痕迹的区域，专业细致到了极致。
工地深处，三号楼北侧空地，一片狼藉。
荒草被碾压倒伏，泥泞的地面遍布深浅不一的水洼，浑浊的积水之下，隐约能看见一块块颜色暗沉的碎块。
哪怕早已做好心理准备，近距离直面景象时，依旧让人头皮发紧。
不是完整尸体。
是被彻底分割、拆解、零碎到极致的人体残肢。
皮肉、碎骨、软组织零零散散分布在二十多平的空地上，被雨水泡得发胀发白，暗红色的血水混在泥水之中，被不断冲刷、稀释、流淌，几乎要彻底融进泥土里。
没有规整的摆放，没有刻意的遮掩，也没有粗暴胡乱的劈砍痕迹。
所有残肢的切割断面，平整得近乎诡异。
哪怕经过雨水长时间浸泡腐烂，依旧能清晰看见每一处切口都笔直、均匀、角度统一，没有丝毫崩裂、参差、毛刺，完全不像是普通刀具劈砍能够形成的痕迹。
沈予安蹲在满地残肢之前，单膝跪地，动作轻柔至极，小心翼翼避开每一块散落的人体组织。
他手里拿着小巧的强光冷光源勘查灯，光线调至柔和不刺眼的档位，一寸寸扫过地面。灯光掠过碎骨断面，清晰照出骨骼被平滑切开的整齐切面。
他眼底平静无波，没有惊惧，厌恶，只有纯粹的审慎与专注。
指尖悬空“切口统一垂直，骨质切面无崩口、无挤压损伤、无撕扯痕迹。”
“分割工具极其精密，不是普通砍刀、菜刀、斧头、锯子。大概率是高精密医用骨科切割器械，转速稳定，刀口极薄。”
他一边观察，一边轻声梳理线索，条理清晰，逻辑缜密。
“分割手法极度规范，下刀精准，避开所有骨节硬阻，完全贴合人体解剖结构。凶手熟知人体肌理、骨骼分布、软组织走向，具备极高的专业解剖知识，绝非普通仇杀、激情犯罪。”
风雨呼啸，现场死寂。
远处，苏晚已经架好勘查灯光，调好设备参数，拿着痕迹刷和微量物证收集器，一寸寸清扫地面水洼与泥土表层。她做事极快，专注力极强，眼里只有物证，不受周遭血腥氛围影响。
“陆队。”苏晚抬头出声，声音清亮冷静，“表层泥土全部被雨水重度冲刷，足迹、车辙、指纹、皮屑全部无留存。现场地表干净得过分，不像是自然冲刷，更像人为大面积清水冲洗过。”
陆峥迈步走入现场，站在灯光边缘，目光沉沉扫过整片空地：“人为清理现场？”
“是。”苏晚点头，“普通雨水冲不掉缝隙里的微量血迹，这里砖缝、草根缝隙里全部无残留，明显是刻意清洗灭迹。”
江驰排查完外围，快步折返，裤脚沾满泥水，神色严肃：“外围无闯入痕迹，无车辆停靠痕迹，围墙内外没有攀爬脚印，工地出入口近期没有监控留存，这片区域的摄像头半年前就坏了，一直没维修。”
许砚站在卷宗灯光旁，笔尖快速划过纸面，淡淡开口：“无监控、无路人、无住户、现场可人为清洗灭迹。凶手提前踩点，熟悉这片区域所有死角，预谋作案，不是临时起意。”
四人在外围汇总线索，唯有沈予安始终蹲在尸块之间，一点点规整、分类、标记每一处残肢位置。
他动作极轻，对待每一块破碎的人体组织，都带着近乎悲悯的慎重。
“受害者是男性。”
片刻后，沈予安抬头，温软的声音穿透雨幕，传到几人耳中。
“从骨盆骨形态、骨骺发育程度判断，年龄在二十八到三十五岁之间，骨骼肌肉密度偏高，生前大概率从事体力劳动或长期运动。”
“初步筛查，致命伤不在肢解创口。残肢断面无生活反应，出血痕迹极少。”
一句话，瞬间让在场所有人神色一凛。
陆峥眼神骤沉：“死后分尸。”
“对。”沈予安点头，语气依旧平和温柔，没有半分波澜，“受害者先死亡，死后被精密拆解分尸，抛尸此处。真正致命伤不在残肢里，大概率在未找到的躯干和头颅部分。”
他抬手，轻轻拂开灯影下的一块细小软组织：“肢解只是抛尸手段，不是致死手段。凶手杀人、分尸、抛尸、清场，全程冷静、有序、无错漏、无情绪化痕迹。”
“心理极其稳定，反侦察能力顶级。”
许砚垂眸记录，轻声补充：“无情绪化犯罪特征，无泄愤、无炫耀、无遗留物证。这类凶手最难抓，没有软肋，没有破绽。”
沈予安低头，继续规整物证，声音轻轻的，带着天然的善意与惋惜：“无论死者生前是什么身份，这样的死状太过惨烈。凶手心性太冷，视人命如草芥。”
他说这句话时，眉眼干净柔软，眼底是真切的悲悯与不解。
是全队所有人都熟悉的模样。
永远见不得无辜惨死，永远会为受害者惋惜，永远对罪恶抱有最纯粹的抵触。
陆峥看着场内温顺专注的身影，心底微松。
每次面对这种极致黑暗血腥的案子，也只有沈予安的沉稳温柔，能稳住所有人紧绷到极致的情绪。
“继续查。”陆峥沉声下令，“苏晚全面提取微量泥土、水草、孢子样本，带回实验室筛查。江驰走访周边荒地、近郊小路，查近期夜间通行车辆。许砚整理同类完美犯罪悬案卷宗，做串案比对。”
“收到。”
三人应声，立刻分头行动。
雨还在下，冲刷着满地残骨，洗去最后一丝温热的血腥，只剩冰冷死寂的泥土味。
沈予安依旧蹲在原地，低头整理着散落的尸块，白色防护服在昏暗灯影里干净得近乎刺眼。
他指尖轻轻捏起一枚极小的骨屑，放进证物袋。
温顺低垂的眉眼之间，在无人看见的阴影里，掠过一丝极淡、极冷、毫无温度的漠然。
转瞬即逝。
雨势没有减弱的迹象，豆大的雨点砸在临时架设的勘查灯防护罩上，噼啪作响，灯光被水雾揉得一片朦胧。
沈予安把最后一块骨片封进透明证物袋，袋口捏紧，贴上临时编号标签。他动作缓慢，每一个证物袋都摆放得整整齐齐，依次放进专用保温物证箱。做完这一切，他撑着膝盖缓缓站起身，长时间蹲跪让小腿微微发麻，他轻轻活动了一下脚踝。
“尸块全部标记完毕。”沈予安隔着口罩，声音温温的传到陆峥耳里，“我这边建议，现场所有泥土分层取样。雨水虽然冲刷表层，但下层泥土或许能留住一些被溶解的微量物质，带回实验室做理化检测。”
陆峥点头，侧头看向苏晚：“听见了？按他说的做，分层取土，分袋标注深度。”
“明白。”苏晚手里的毛刷没有停下，她半跪在泥泞里，小心翼翼扫开一块沾着腐液的草根，“我这边在草根缝隙找到一小片织物残片，很薄，不是普通衣服面料，像是某种工业隔离布料，颜色是深灰，已经泡得发朽。”
她用镊子小心夹起残片，举到灯光下。布料边缘切割整齐，没有撕裂痕迹。
江驰刚好从外围折返，裤脚沾满黄泥，靴底沾着杂草碎叶。“周边两公里全部排查完。这片烂尾工地有两条土路出入口，北面那条连通城郊国道，路边没有民用监控，只有国道卡口的测速摄像头，我已经联系交管，申请调取近七十二小时的车辆记录。南面是成片荒山，没有通路，人很难背着重物从山里进出。”
许砚坐在折叠小马扎上，手里的钢笔在卷宗本上不停滑动，纸上密密麻麻写满了推演要点。“凶手选择这里抛尸，是精心挑选的。远离居民区，降雨多，便于掩盖痕迹。而且工地停工许久，平时根本没人过来，匿名报警，等警方到场，大部分痕迹已经被雨水毁掉。”
他顿了顿，抬眼看向众人，目光冷静：“报警的人，要么是凶手本人，要么是组织内部的人。故意引导我们发现尸体，时间卡得很巧妙，早一点，雨还没冲掉痕迹；晚一点，残肢会被野兽拖走。”
沈予安站在一旁，静静听着几人的讨论，轻轻蹙了蹙眉：“如果是凶手主动报警，目的是什么？单纯炫耀？还是想引导我们往错误方向查？”
“现在还判断不了。”陆峥低声回应，目光扫过漆黑的工地高楼，“先把物证全部带回局里。尸体残肢送解剖室连夜检验，许砚，你回去检索档案，看看近五年南城有没有类似手法的分尸案件，切口一致的优先筛选。江驰，明天一早，去国道卡口调取录像，排查可疑车辆。苏晚，实验室那边，织物残片、泥土样本优先检测。”
分工明确，没有人提出异议。
几人开始收尾工作。拍照组从不同角度拍摄现场全景，标记点位，将一箱箱证物小心搬运，贴上封条。
沈予安脱下外层防护服，折叠整齐放进垃圾袋，手套按规范密封处理。深秋夜风一吹，他微微缩了缩肩。
江驰留意到这个小动作，随口开口：“沈哥，夜里冷，等下回去路上把空调开高点。一晚上泡在这种现场，小心着凉。”
“多谢，我没事。”沈予安弯了弯眼，笑容温和，“倒是你们，跑前跑后，辛苦了。”
苏晚一边核对证物清单，头也不抬地接话：“每次大案，最熬人的就是你。解剖室估计又要通宵了。”
“本职工作而已。”沈予安淡淡一笑，“早点查清，死者才能安息。”
陆峥站在最前面，看着他们收拾现场，低声叮嘱：“所有人注意，今晚现场的事，不要对外泄露。媒体那边暂时封锁消息，避免恐慌，也防止惊动凶手。”
“收到。”
一行人陆续撤出警戒线，黄色带子在风雨里飘摇。坐回车里，车门关上，隔绝了外面潮湿阴冷的空气。车厢里一时安静，只剩下雨刷来回摆动的声响。
许砚翻看着刚记录的笔记，低声开口：“我有个疑问。凶手懂得精密解剖，拥有专业器械，熟悉人体结构。大概率是医疗相关从业者，医生、医学生，或者有解剖相关工作经历。”
江驰靠在车窗上，揉了揉眉心：“南城从事医疗行业的人太多，范围太大。全市大小医院、私人诊所，还有一些生物实验室，挨个排查，工作量大到离谱。”
“先不急着大范围排查。”陆峥握着方向盘，目视前方，“等沈予安完成解剖，拿到更多线索，苏晚那边织物和泥土检测报告出来，再缩小范围。盲目的大面积走访，只会浪费时间。”
车子驶入城区，街道两侧路灯次第亮起，把路面照成一片水光。
回到市局大院的时候，已经凌晨一点多。大楼大部分办公室已经熄灯，只有刑侦支队、法医室和化验室的灯依旧亮着。
几人下车，分头行动。
苏晚抱着证物箱直奔化验室，立刻安排样本登记。江驰去资料室，预约调取国道监控录像。许砚抱着卷宗，回到自己的工位，翻找历年悬案档案。陆峥去办公室，准备向上级汇报今夜发现的碎尸案。
沈予安独自走向解剖室。
消毒水的气味扑面而来，冰冷，清冽。他换上解剖服，将保温箱内的残肢一件件取出，摆放在解剖台上。无影灯亮起，惨白的光线铺满台面。
他拿起测量尺，一点点记录骨骼尺寸，检查每一处软组织。动作从容，有条不紊。
解剖室里只有仪器轻微的嗡鸣，安静得可怕。
天亮的时候，第一份初步尸检报告打印完成。
沈予安拿着纸质报告，走到陆峥的办公室门口，抬手轻轻叩门。
陆峥眼底布满红血丝，桌上堆着厚厚的卷宗，烟灰缸里塞满烟蒂。一夜没合眼。
“陆队，初步尸检报告。”沈予安推门走进来，将文件放在办公桌，语气依旧温和，“我熬了一整夜，把所有残肢全部检验完毕。”
陆峥立刻拿起报告翻看，目光快速扫过文字。
“死者男性，31岁。死亡时间预估在四到五天前。致命伤在胸口，单一致命锐器贯穿心脏，当场死亡。死后十二小时左右，凶手开始分尸。”沈予安站在一旁，缓缓讲解，“残肢里没有找到头颅和躯干的大部分组织，这两部分被凶手带走，没有抛在工地。”
陆峥眉头紧锁：“带走躯干和头颅？为什么？”
“猜测两种可能。”沈予安耐心解释，“第一，头颅和躯干上留有能够直接锁定凶手身份的痕迹，必须单独处理销毁。第二，这是凶手的习惯，保留部分遗体，作为某种纪念。后者在连环犯罪里并不少见。”
他顿了顿，补充一句：“另外，在一小块皮下组织上，发现了非常微量的油脂，不属于人体，也不是普通动植物油脂，成分特殊，已经取样交给苏晚那边化验。”
“很好。”陆峥抬眼看向他，语气带着一丝疲惫的赞许，“辛苦了，沈予安。你先去休息室歇一会，后面有新发现，我再叫你。”
“好。”沈予安微微颔首，转身离开办公室。
走廊光线偏暗，他缓步往前走。
另一边，化验室内，苏晚正盯着显微镜，仔细观察昨夜带回的泥土样本。
“这泥土里面，有少量人造合成纤维，还有微量的油脂残留。”苏晚对着通讯耳麦，轻声汇报，“和沈法医提取到的油脂样本一致，正在做成分比对，需要一点时间。”
江驰已经拿到交管部门发来的监控视频，坐在电脑前，拖动进度条，一帧一帧查看国道卡口来往车辆。屏幕光映在他脸上，神情专注。
许砚摊开厚厚一叠旧案卷，一页一页翻阅，试图寻找和本次分尸手法相似的旧案子。
en: Autumn rain in Nancheng was always clammy and unrelenting.

Since nightfall, the fine, cold drizzle had not let up. Layers of mist hung over the city, blurring its lights into a dull haze. The air carried the damp smell of earth and the rot of late-autumn vegetation, heavy enough to tighten the chest.
On the outskirts of the city: the unfinished Jin Xiu Lan Ting development, abandoned three years earlier.

Weeds and vines had overrun the vast construction site. The bare frames of several unfinished towers thrust through the rain like skeletal remains. There were no streetlights, no pedestrians. Far from any residential neighborhood, this was one of Nancheng’s most desolate corners.
The flashing red and blue of police lights provided the only color.

Three criminal investigation vehicles pulled up in succession beside the dirt road at the entrance, their tires cutting deep ruts through the mud. Windshield wipers swept back and forth without ever quite clearing the wet haze.

A cordon was already in place. Bright yellow tape stirred in the wind and rain, sealing off the scene. Officers from the local police station stood watch outside it, straight-backed and solemn, turning away anyone who tried to approach.
“The municipal bureau’s major crime team is here.”
The low announcement cut through the rain.
A car door opened. Cold wind and rain rushed inside.
The team stepped out one after another. No one spoke. No one wasted a movement. Their coordination was almost instinctive.

The first man out wore a dark police uniform. He stood tall, his shoulders square. The night deepened the shadows around his eyes and sharpened the hard lines of his face. He carried the quiet gravity of someone who had worked too many major cases. Adjusting his collar, he looked through the mist toward the black towers, his steady gaze taking in the entire abandoned site.
“Team Leader Lu.”
He asked only one question, his voice low. “What have we got?”

An officer from the local station stepped forward. His voice was hushed but tight. “An anonymous call came in ten minutes ago. Human remains on the open ground north of Building Three. We confirmed a dismemberment scene on arrival. Preliminary assessment: an adult male. The remains are scattered over roughly twenty square meters. Heavy rain has washed through the site. The scene is badly compromised.”
“Anonymous?”
The question came in a cold, level voice. This was Lu Zheng, leader of the major crime team.

“Yes. We couldn’t find a registered identity for the number. The phone was switched off immediately after the call. No signal to trace.” The officer nodded. “We haven’t found an intact body. Just scattered bone fragments and soft tissue. A lot of the traces have already washed away.”
Before he had finished, the others were moving.

A slight young figure strode into the mud with a heavy scene-examination case and evidence containers. Opening the case, setting up portable lighting, fixing reference points: each movement followed cleanly into the next. This was Su Wan, responsible for trace evidence and scene examination.

Jiang Chi, tall and light on his feet, made a quick circuit outside the cordon. His sharp gaze searched the weeds, muddy paths, and blind corners along the walls for footprints and signs of parked vehicles. Field inquiries and scene security were his responsibility.

Xu Yan remained beside a police car with a blank case notebook, his fingertips poised over the paper. Quiet and composed, he was already working through the logic of the case. He handled profiling and the integration of leads.

Last came Shen Yu’an, the team’s forensic physician, in clean, sterile protective clothing. His features were mild, his manner unfailingly gentle and patient. Even the bloodiest scene never seemed to disturb him.
Shen Yu’an put on two pairs of latex gloves and a protective mask. Faced with the prospect of a brutal dismemberment scene, he showed neither tension nor reluctance. Only patience and care.
He adjusted the cuffs of his protective suit until no skin was exposed. There was something reassuring about the thoroughness of his movements.
“I’ll go in first.”

His voice was soft, but it carried clearly through the rain. “A scene like this is easy to disturb further. I’ll document the positions of the remains and make a preliminary examination of the injuries. Give me a little time before you come in. We don’t want to tread on evidence.”
Lu Zheng nodded. “Watch your footing. Record the damage first. The rain is getting heavier.”
“All right.”
Shen Yu’an answered quietly and stepped inside the cordon.

Fine rain darkened the white fabric of his suit. He moved slowly and with absolute steadiness, placing each foot on exposed patches of firm ground. He avoided the soft mud and every area that might hold a trace. His care was meticulous.
Deep inside the site, the ground north of Building Three was a wreck.
Weeds had been crushed flat. Puddles of different depths covered the mud. Beneath the murky water, dark fragments were just visible.
Even prepared for it, one could not face the scene at close range without a tightening of the scalp.
There was no intact body.
There were human remains, divided and dismantled into fragments.

Flesh, broken bone, and soft tissue lay scattered across more than twenty square meters, swollen and pale from the rain. Dark blood mingled with the muddy water, washing away, thinning, running into the soil.
Nothing had been arranged neatly. Nothing had been deliberately hidden. Nor was there any sign of crude, haphazard hacking.
The cut surfaces were almost unnaturally smooth.

Even after prolonged soaking and decay, each cut remained visibly straight, even, and consistent in angle. No splintering, ragged edges, or burrs. These were not marks an ordinary blade would leave when used to hack through a body.
Shen Yu’an lowered himself onto one knee among the remains, taking care not to touch a single scattered piece of tissue.

He held a small, powerful examination light, adjusted to a soft setting. He swept it over the ground inch by inch. As the beam passed across the bone fragments, it revealed clean, smoothly severed surfaces.
His eyes were calm. No fear or disgust. Only attention and caution.
His fingertips hovered above a fragment. “The cuts are consistently perpendicular. No chipping of the bone, no compression damage, no tearing.”

“The instrument was extremely precise. Not an ordinary cleaver, kitchen knife, axe, or saw. Most likely a high-precision orthopedic cutting instrument, with a steady rotational speed and a very thin blade.”
He spoke quietly as he worked through the evidence, each observation following the last.

“The dismemberment is highly systematic. Precise cuts, avoiding resistance at the joints, closely following the anatomy. Whoever did this understands tissue structure, skeletal distribution, and the alignment of soft tissue. They have considerable anatomical training. This is no ordinary revenge killing or crime of passion.”
Wind and rain filled the silence.

Farther off, Su Wan had set up the lights and adjusted the equipment. With a trace brush and a collection tool, she worked over the puddles and surface soil inch by inch. She was fast and intensely focused, seeing only the evidence, undistracted by the bloodshed around her.

“Team Leader Lu.” Her voice was clear and calm. “The surface soil has been heavily washed. No footprints, tire impressions, fingerprints, or skin flakes remain. It’s too clean. This doesn’t look like rain alone. It looks as though someone flushed a large area with clean water.”
Lu Zheng stepped into the scene and stopped at the edge of the light. His gaze swept the open ground. “Someone cleaned it?”
“Yes.” Su Wan nodded. “Ordinary rainfall wouldn’t remove trace blood from the crevices. There’s nothing between the bricks or around the roots. Someone deliberately washed the evidence away.”

Jiang Chi returned from the perimeter, mud coating his trouser legs. His expression was grave. “No signs of forced entry. No indication of a parked vehicle. No climbing marks on either side of the wall. There’s no recent surveillance footage from the entrances. The cameras here stopped working six months ago and were never repaired.”

Xu Yan stood beside the light illuminating his notebook, his pen moving quickly. “No cameras, no passersby, no residents. A scene that can be washed clean. The killer scouted this place and knew its blind spots. Premeditated. Not impulsive.”
While the four of them pooled their findings at the edge of the scene, Shen Yu’an remained among the remains, sorting, classifying, and marking the position of each piece.
He handled every fragment with a care that was almost tender.
“The victim was male.”
He looked up after a moment. His gentle voice reached them through the curtain of rain.
“Judging by the pelvis and epiphyseal development, between twenty-eight and thirty-five. Relatively high bone and muscle density. He probably did physical work or exercised regularly.”
“On preliminary examination, the dismemberment wounds weren’t the cause of death. There’s no vital reaction at the cut surfaces, and very little bleeding.”
Everyone grew still.
Lu Zheng’s gaze hardened. “Dismembered after death.”

“Yes.” Shen Yu’an nodded, his tone as even and gentle as before. “The victim died first. The body was then precisely dismembered and dumped here. The fatal injury isn’t on the parts we’ve found. It’s probably on the torso or head, both still missing.”

He lightly moved aside a small piece of soft tissue beneath the lamp. “The dismemberment was a means of disposal, not the cause of death. Killing, dismemberment, dumping, cleanup. All calm, orderly, without mistakes or any sign of emotional excess.”
“Exceptionally stable psychologically. Highly skilled at avoiding detection.”
Xu Yan looked down and wrote. “No emotional hallmarks. No venting of anger, no showing off, no physical evidence left behind. This kind is the hardest to catch. No weakness. No opening.”

Shen Yu’an lowered his head and continued arranging the evidence. His voice was quiet, naturally kind and regretful. “Whoever he was in life, no one should end like this. The killer is cold. Human life means nothing to them.”
His face was gentle as he spoke, his eyes full of genuine pity and incomprehension.
It was an expression the whole team knew.
He could never bear the violent death of an innocent person. He always grieved for the victims. His revulsion toward cruelty was instinctive and uncomplicated.
Watching that quiet, attentive figure inside the cordon, Lu Zheng felt some of the tension ease.
In cases this dark and bloody, Shen Yu’an’s steady gentleness was often the only thing that kept everyone else from breaking.

“Keep working,” Lu Zheng ordered. “Su Wan, collect soil, aquatic vegetation, and spore samples. Take them back for screening. Jiang Chi, make inquiries around the wasteland and the outlying roads. Check vehicles passing through at night. Xu Yan, pull unsolved cases with comparable methods. Look for links.”
“Understood.”
The three of them moved off at once.
Rain continued to wash over the broken bones, taking away the last warm trace of blood until only the cold smell of earth remained.
Shen Yu’an was still crouching where he had been, his head lowered over the remains. Under the dim lamps, his white suit looked almost painfully clean.
With his fingertips, he picked up a tiny splinter of bone and placed it in an evidence bag.
In the shadow beneath his lowered eyes, where no one could see, a trace of indifference passed over his face. Faint. Cold. Utterly without warmth.
Then it was gone.
The rain showed no sign of easing. Large drops crackled against the protective covers of the portable lamps, their light blurred by mist.

Shen Yu’an sealed the last bone fragment in a transparent bag, pressed the closure tight, and attached a temporary identification label. He worked slowly, arranging each bag neatly before placing it in the insulated evidence container. When he finished, he braced his hands on his knees and rose. His calves had gone numb from crouching. He gently moved his ankles.

“All the remains have been marked.” His voice reached Lu Zheng softly through the mask. “I recommend taking soil samples at different depths. The rain has washed the surface, but lower layers may still contain traces of dissolved substances. We can run physical and chemical tests back at the lab.”
Lu Zheng nodded and turned to Su Wan. “You heard him. Separate layers. Bag them individually and record the depth.”

“Understood.” Her brush kept moving. Half-kneeling in the mud, she carefully cleared a root stained with decomposition fluid. “I’ve found a small textile fragment caught between the roots. Very thin. Not ordinary clothing material. Possibly some kind of industrial barrier fabric. Dark gray, badly deteriorated from soaking.”
She lifted it carefully with tweezers and held it to the light. The edge had been cut cleanly. There was no tearing.

Jiang Chi returned from the perimeter, yellow mud on his trouser legs and crushed weeds clinging to his boots. “We’ve checked a two-kilometer radius. There are two dirt-road entrances. The northern one connects to the national highway outside the city. No private cameras along that stretch, only the highway checkpoint’s speed cameras. I’ve contacted traffic police and requested the last seventy-two hours of vehicle records. To the south it’s all uncultivated hills, no road. Carrying anything heavy in or out that way would be difficult.”

Xu Yan sat on a folding stool, his fountain pen moving over pages crowded with deductions. “The dump site was carefully chosen. Far from housing. Plenty of rain to conceal traces. Construction stopped years ago; normally no one comes here. An anonymous call, and by the time the police arrive, most of the evidence has washed away.”

He paused and looked up. “The caller was either the killer or someone inside the organization. They wanted us to find the body. The timing was exact. Any earlier and the rain wouldn’t have erased the traces. Any later and animals might have carried the remains away.”
Shen Yu’an listened quietly, a slight crease forming between his brows. “If the killer made the call, why? Just to show off? Or to send us in the wrong direction?”

“Too early to say.” Lu Zheng looked toward the dark towers. “Bring all the evidence back to the bureau. The remains go to the autopsy room for examination tonight. Xu Yan, search the files for dismemberment cases in Nancheng over the past five years. Prioritize matching cut patterns. Jiang Chi, get that highway footage first thing tomorrow. Look for suspicious vehicles. Su Wan, have the lab prioritize the fabric and soil.”
The assignments were clear. No one objected.
They began closing the scene. The photography team took wide shots from multiple angles and recorded reference points. Evidence containers were carried out with care and sealed.

Shen Yu’an removed his outer protective suit, folded it neatly into a waste bag, and sealed his gloves for disposal according to procedure. A gust of late-autumn wind made him draw his shoulders in slightly.
Jiang Chi noticed. “Shen, it’s cold out. Turn the heater up on the way back. A whole night in this weather—you’ll catch a chill.”
“Thanks. I’m fine.” Shen Yu’an smiled, his eyes softening. “You’re the ones who’ve been running around all night. You’ve worked hard.”
Still checking the evidence inventory, Su Wan spoke without looking up. “Every major case takes the most out of you. Another all-nighter in the autopsy room, I suppose.”
“It’s my job.” He gave a faint smile. “The sooner we find out what happened, the sooner he can rest.”

Lu Zheng stood ahead of them, watching the cleanup. “One thing. Nothing about tonight’s scene goes outside the team. No information to the media for now. We don’t want panic, and we don’t want to alert the killer.”
“Understood.”
They left the cordon one by one, the yellow tape fluttering in the rain. Back inside the vehicles, the doors closed out the damp cold. For a while there was only the sweep of the wipers.

Xu Yan looked through his notes. “One question. The killer understands precise anatomical dissection, has specialist instruments, knows the human body. Most likely someone connected to medicine. A doctor, a medical student, or someone with dissection experience.”

Jiang Chi leaned against the window and rubbed the bridge of his nose. “That covers too many people in Nancheng. Every hospital, every private clinic, some of the biological labs as well. Checking them one by one would be an enormous job.”

“We’re not casting that wide a net yet.” Lu Zheng kept his eyes on the road. “Let Shen Yu’an finish the examination. Wait for Su Wan’s fabric and soil reports. Then we narrow it down. Knocking on every door without direction will only waste time.”
They entered the city. Streetlights appeared one after another, turning the wet road to silver.

It was past one in the morning when they reached the municipal public security bureau compound. Most offices were dark. Only the Criminal Investigation Detachment, the forensic medicine unit, and the laboratory still had their lights on.
They got out and went their separate ways.

Su Wan took the evidence container straight to the lab and arranged for the samples to be logged. Jiang Chi went to the records room to organize retrieval of the highway footage. Xu Yan returned to his desk with the files and began searching old unsolved cases. Lu Zheng went to his office to prepare a report for his superiors on the night’s discovery.
Shen Yu’an walked alone toward the autopsy room.

The sharp, cold smell of disinfectant met him at the door. He changed into autopsy clothing, took the remains from the insulated container one by one, and laid them on the table. The surgical lamp came on, flooding the surface with white light.
He picked up a measuring rule and began recording the bone dimensions and examining each piece of soft tissue. His movements were unhurried and methodical.
Only the faint hum of equipment broke the terrible stillness.
At daybreak, the first preliminary autopsy report came off the printer.
Shen Yu’an carried it to Lu Zheng’s office and knocked lightly.
“Come in.”
Lu Zheng’s eyes were bloodshot. Thick files covered his desk, and cigarette ends filled the ashtray. He had not slept.
“Team Leader Lu. The preliminary report.” Shen Yu’an entered and placed it on the desk, his tone as gentle as ever. “I’ve finished examining all the remains. It took the whole night.”
Lu Zheng picked up the report immediately, his eyes moving quickly over the text.

“Male, thirty-one. Estimated time of death: four to five days ago. The fatal injury was a single sharp-force wound penetrating the heart. Death was immediate. Dismemberment began roughly twelve hours afterward.” Shen Yu’an stood beside the desk and explained each finding. “We haven’t recovered the head or most of the torso. The killer took those away rather than leaving them at the site.”
Lu Zheng frowned. “The head and torso. Why?”

“Two possibilities.” Shen Yu’an explained patiently. “First, they carry evidence that could directly identify the killer, so they had to be disposed of separately. Second, keeping part of a victim is a habit. A kind of souvenir. That isn’t uncommon in serial crime.”

He paused. “There’s one other thing. A minute trace of grease on a small piece of subcutaneous tissue. Not human fat, and not an ordinary animal or vegetable oil. The composition is unusual. I’ve sent a sample to Su Wan for analysis.”
“Good.” Lu Zheng looked up with weary approval. “Thank you, Shen Yu’an. Get some rest in the break room. I’ll call you if anything new comes in.”
“All right.” Shen Yu’an inclined his head and left.
The corridor was dim. He walked slowly along it.
In the laboratory, Su Wan was studying the soil samples from the previous night under a microscope.

“There are small quantities of synthetic fibers in the soil, and traces of grease.” She spoke quietly into her headset. “Consistent with the sample Dr. Shen recovered. We’re comparing the compositions now. It’ll take a little time.”

Jiang Chi had received the footage from traffic police. He sat at a computer, moving through it frame by frame, studying the vehicles passing the highway checkpoint. The light of the screen caught his concentrated face.
Xu Yan spread a thick stack of old case files across his desk and turned the pages one by one, searching for an earlier case with the same dismemberment method.

zh: 上午九点整。
市局刑侦支队会议室的百叶窗半合，细碎的晨光透过缝隙落进来，切割出明暗交错的线条。桌上铺满昨夜整理完毕的尸检报告、物证化验单、监控截图、走访笔录，厚厚一叠文件压得整齐规整。
一夜连轴转，所有人眼底都带着熬出来的红血丝，但精神高度集中，没有一人松懈。
陆峥坐在主位，指尖轻轻叩击桌面，声音沉稳冷静，开启今日案情复盘：
“目前所有线索统一汇总，重新梳理一遍，把那些無用的除掉，缩小范围。”
他抬眼扫过众人。
“先说物证。苏晚。”
苏晚应声起身，走到投屏前，调出后台化验数据。
“泥土样本、草屑附着物、残肢附带微量油脂，三组物证溯源结果完全统一。”
“第一，润滑脂属于高端精密器械专用油，市面零售店无售卖，只对精密器械维修工坊、私人改装工作室小批量定向供货。南城范围内，登记在册的采购方一共三家。”
“第二，现场发现的超细纤维隔离布，防水、防尘、防碎屑，不属于医院手术室耗材，是精密器械操作专用防尘擦拭布。”
“第三，所有微量附着物，无任何实验室试剂残留，排除正规科研单位、公立医院实验室作案可能。”
她关掉数据页，画面定格在三家采购单位名单上。
“筛查后，两家正规生物实验室可以直接排除。他们耗材出入库登记完整，人员轮岗透明，监控全覆盖，近一月所有设备使用、物料消耗全部可溯源，无任何空白时间。”
“仅剩最后一家——城郊私人精密器械改装工作室。”
会议室空气微微一沉。
许砚顺势接话，指尖点着手里的筛查名单：
“我做了人员筛查。该工作室法人陈默，四十二岁，本地人，无犯罪前科，社会关系简单，已婚，育有一子，日常对外形象老实、勤恳、技术口碑良好。”
“工作室规模小，全职人员只有陈默一人，偶尔招短期学徒，无固定员工，符合单人独立作案条件。”
江驰靠着椅背，接过话头：
“我这边监控筛查也出结果了。”
他点开国道卡口修复后的高清截图，画面跳出一辆深色小型商务车。
“案发当晚凌晨一点零七分，这辆车从城郊烂尾工地方向驶出，正是我们推算的抛尸窗口期。画质修复后确认车牌，车主就是陈默。”
“当晚只有他一台私人车辆吻合时间、路线、区域。其余车辆全部排除嫌疑。”
三条独立线索——物证溯源、人员条件、行动轨迹。
全部精准收拢到同一个人身上。
嫌疑链，完整闭环。
沈予安坐在侧边，安静听着所有人的推论，视线落在投屏上陈默的证件照上。
照片里的男人眉眼普通，面相憨厚，看着就是常年伏案做工的手艺人，没有半分凶戾之气。
他微微开口，语气严谨：
“结合尸检结果补充。”
“凶手手法看似规整，但肢解细节有明显生疏感，属于照着固定流程模仿操作，不是常年解剖的专业人员。”
“陈默的精密器械改装工作，需要熟悉人体仿生器械结构，具备基础肌理认知，完全吻合凶手的技术层级。”
“不高不低，刚好对上。”
几句补充，彻底堵死了所有偏差可能。
陆峥点头，沉声定论：
“目前所有客观线索，全部指向陈默。无第二嫌疑人，无其他分支线索。”
“但现在只有轨迹物证，缺少死者身份、作案动机、人证口供。暂时不定性结案，先落地核查人际关系。”
他快速分派任务，条理清晰、层层落地。
“江驰，立刻带队二次外勤。前往陈默工作室周边走访邻居、街坊、往期学徒，查他近期情绪状态、人际矛盾、是否有隐秘仇怨。”
“许砚，深挖陈默私人社交、借贷、私下纠纷，查近期是否有大额收支、隐秘往来人员。”
“苏晚，继续比对工作室物料样本，做百分百同源匹配，固定铁证。”
所有人应声领命，迅速散开，各司其职。
上午十点，刑侦组外勤车再次驶出市局。
江驰带队直奔城郊工坊聚集区。
陈默的工作室就在国道旁一排临街小平房，独门独院，门口挂着不起眼的锈迹招牌，平时门庭冷清，几乎无人往来。
周边都是做五金、维修、小加工的个体户。
江驰分头走访左右邻里、隔壁店铺老板、路口小卖部。
排查推进极快。
隔壁五金店老板回忆得很清楚：
“陈默啊？这人看着老实，话少，天天闷头干活，平时不惹事。不过……这半个月有点不对劲。”
“以前他每天准时开门收工，最近夜夜熬到两三点，院子里机器半夜还响。前几天我半夜起夜，看见他院子车灯亮着，车子脏兮兮的，全是黄泥，问他去哪了，他说进山拉材料。”
另一位开店的老板娘补充：
“他前段时间跟一个陌生男人吵过架，就在店门口，吵得特别凶，脸红脖子粗的。那人看着挺壮，不是本地人，来了两次，每次都鬼鬼祟祟，没进店，就在门口跟他私聊。”
线索瞬间多出关键缺口。
隐秘人际矛盾！
江驰立刻追问：“什么时候的事？大概样貌、身高、特征？”
“大概五六天前，刚好就是案发前后那几天。”老板娘仔细回想，“一米七多，挺结实，看着不好惹，穿黑衣服，戴帽子，看不清脸。两人吵完之后，那人就再也没来过。”
线索瞬间咬合。
许砚远程同步筛查，立刻传回消息：
“查到了。陈默半年前私下参与过高息民间借贷，近期债务到期，被催债多次。他近期账户有不明资金往来，小额频繁入账，来源无法追溯。”
“同时查到，他三个月前和一名外地务工人员产生过工程纠纷，闹得很僵，对方多次上门扯皮。”
所有碎片瞬间拼合。
私怨、纠纷、隐秘人际、夜间反常行动、物证匹配、轨迹锁定。
嫌疑人彻底锁死。
中午十二点，所有外勤信息汇总回市局。
临时小会议室里，几人快速复盘。
“可以确定。”江驰语气笃定，“陈默有作案时间、作案空间、作案工具、作案动机。所有外部条件全部吻合。”
苏晚拿着最新的比对报告走进来，轻轻放在桌上：
“最终同源检测完成。”
“案发现场的润滑油脂、隔离布纤维，与陈默工作室库存物料，分子结构完全一致，属于同一批次耗材。”
铁证落地。
至此，人、物、时间、空间、动机，五条链路全部锁死。
陆峥抬眼，目光锐利果决：
“申请传唤令、搜查令。”
“即刻，抓捕陈默。”
沈予安站在窗边，看着楼下警车陆续出车，眉眼温顺，轻声说了一句：
“希望能尽快查清真相，给死者一个交代。”
午后一点半，烈日悬在南城上空，空气闷得发烫，柏油路面微微泛着热浪。
两辆没有标识的民用警车，缓缓停靠在城郊工坊街的路口，隔着几十米，远远对着陈默那间私人器械工作室。
院墙不高，红砖砌成，院子里停着那辆深色商务车，正是国道监控里拍到的车辆。院门虚掩，里面隐约传来金属打磨的嗡鸣，断断续续飘到街上。
江驰坐在前车副驾，手里捏着搜查令与传唤文书，低声跟陆峥汇报。
“四周已经布控完毕，两个队员守后侧围墙，防止翻墙逃跑。前后两条通路全部盯死，他跑不掉。”
陆峥微微颔首，目光落在小院门口：“注意，目标手里有精密加工刀具，存在持械反抗风险。行动尽量平稳，不要激化冲突。”
许砚留在车上，拿着平板实时调取工作室周边监控，随时留意院内动静。苏晚带着物证采集箱，跟在队伍后面，准备一旦入户搜查，立刻固定现场物证。
“行动。”
陆峥一声低令。
江驰带着两名便衣，缓步走向院门。他抬手，轻轻敲了敲木门。
院内打磨机的声响停下。
“谁？”男人的声音隔着院墙传出来，带着一丝警惕。
“警察，麻烦开下门，有案子需要向你核实情况。”江驰声音平稳，没有刻意压迫。
沉寂几秒，院门向内拉开一道缝隙。
陈默出现在门后，身上穿着沾金属碎屑的工装，脸上还沾着一点灰。看见门外的便衣，他瞳孔猛地收缩，下意识往后退了半步，手指悄悄攥紧了身侧工作台边缘一把狭长的美工刻刀。
“警察？找我干什么？”他的声音有点干涩，强装镇定。
“陈默，我们持有搜查令和传唤文书，请配合我们回市局接受讯问，同时我们要对你的工作室进行搜查。”陆峥上前一步，出示证件，目光牢牢锁在陈默身上。
陈默脸色瞬间发白，嘴唇哆嗦，目光飞快扫向院子后侧围墙，心里盘算着逃跑路线。可余光一瞥，围墙两头已经站了人，退路彻底封死。
“我……我没犯法。”他喉咙发紧，握着刻刀的手越收越紧。
“放下手里的工具。”江驰上前半步，语气严肃，“不要做多余动作。”
陈默的精神绷到极限，突然猛地转身，想要冲进屋内。江驰反应极快，跨步上前伸手扣住他的胳膊，微微发力，直接将人按压在工作台面上。金属刀具“哐当”一声掉落在水泥地面，发出刺耳的撞击声。
“别动！”
冰冷的手铐咔嗒一声，锁死陈默的手腕。
他剧烈挣扎了几下，力气快速耗尽，肩膀起伏，大口喘着粗气，垂着头，不再反抗，只有肩膀不停发抖。
“带走。”陆峥吩咐。
两名队员押着陈默走到车前，将他安置在后排座位。
另一边，苏晚带着勘查人员进入工作室，开始全面搜查。
屋子不大，一半空间堆满金属原料、打磨设备，货架上整齐摆放着各类耗材，其中就有那一款精密合成润滑脂，还有一叠超细纤维隔离布，和案发现场提取到的纤维完全一致。
工作台台面缝隙里，还残留着一点点淡褐色干涸痕迹。苏晚拿出棉签小心取样，密封保存。
“陆队，这里发现疑似血迹残留，还有同款耗材。”
许砚走进屋内，环顾四周。房间角落放着一个简易储物柜，打开之后，里面有一本笔记本。本子上面记录着器械调试参数，但是后半部分，写着零散的文字，像是记录操作步骤。
“像是照着一套流程写下来的操作要点。”许砚翻了两页，眉头微蹙，“文字很生硬，不像是他自己思考写下的，更像是抄写。”
陆峥走过来翻看笔记本，指尖划过纸面。
“先全部打包带回，作为物证。”
沈予安这时才缓步走进工作室。他目光慢慢扫过工作台、地面，最后落在那本笔记本上，只是简单扫了一眼，没有多言。他弯腰看了看苏晚采集的痕迹样本，轻声开口：“台面残留的痕迹，需要尽快做DNA比对，确认是不是死者的。”
“明白。”苏晚点头。
整个搜查持续了一个半小时。所有可疑物证全部封存装箱，一一登记。
太阳渐渐向西倾斜，热浪稍稍褪去。车队押着嫌疑人，带着满满一箱物证，启程返回市局。
车厢里，陈默低着头，一言不发，浑身紧绷。
江驰坐在他旁边，偶尔侧头观察他的神态。陈默一直沉默，问一句答一句，回避关键问题，整个人像一只受惊的困兽。
回到市局，陈默直接被带进审讯室。
陆峥、江驰准备开始审讯，许砚在观察室等候，随时分析嫌疑人的心理变化。苏晚带着刚采集的样本，立刻送去化验室加急比对。
陆峥拿起对讲机，声音低沉：“开始审讯。”
审讯室的冷白光直直打在陈默脸上，墙面吸音，空间闷得让人喘不过气。
金属审讯椅将他固定住，手铐扣在桌沿，他垂着头，额前的碎发挡着眼睛，肩膀一直微微发抖。
江驰坐在桌子对面，面前摊开笔录本，录音笔已经启动。陆峥坐在江驰身侧，没有急着开口，只是安静看着陈默，压迫感无声漫开。
单向玻璃后的观察室里，许砚握着平板，实时记录嫌疑人的微表情。沈予安站在一旁，双手自然垂在身前，目光平静落在玻璃后的人身上，神态像是单纯旁观，没有半分异样。
“陈默，再问一次。锦绣澜庭烂尾工地，那具被肢解的男尸，是不是你做的。”江驰率先开口，声音平稳，不带情绪。
陈默脑袋埋得更低，声音闷闷的：“不是我，我都说了，我那天晚上在工作室干活。”
“我们在你工作室，找到了同款润滑脂、隔离布，工作台缝隙检出疑似血痕。”江驰把物证照片推到桌子中间，“国道监控拍到你的车，案发凌晨从烂尾工地方向驶出，你怎么解释？”
陈默身体猛地一颤，嘴唇反复抿动，依旧死咬说辞：“那些東西很多地方都能买到！那条国道那么多车经过，凭什么说我去过工地？你們說的什麼鬼痕跡是加工金属锈迹，不是人血！”
他的回答反应很快，每一句辩解，都像是提前在心里演练过无数遍。
陆峥往前微微倾身，目光锁定他：“你工作室柜子里找到的笔记本，上面抄写的肢解操作步骤，怎么回事？”
这话一出，陈默的肩膀骤然一僵，眼神慌乱地飘向一旁。
“那……那是我网上随便找的资料，只是好奇，我没有用来害人。”
“哪个网站，链接呢？作者是谁？”陆峥紧跟着追问。
陈默卡住了，支支吾吾半天，答不上来。“我……记不清了，好久之前浏览的，找不到了。”
许砚在观察室低声跟沈予安说道：“他的心理防线已经开始松动，核心信息全部回避，编造的说辞没有办法交叉验证。”
审讯室内，江驰继续抛出证据。“我们提取了你工作台缝隙的样本，苏晚那边加急检测，结果很快就会出来。一旦确认是死者的DNA，所有辩解都没有意义。”
陈默呼吸越来越急促，胸口大幅度起伏，指尖死死抠着掌心，指甲几乎嵌进肉里。
几分钟之后，观察室的通讯器响起，苏晚的声音传过来：“陆队，DNA比对完成。工作台上面的残留，确认为本次死者的血液组织。”
铁证彻底砸实。
陆峥拿起对讲机，淡淡开口：“告诉他。”
江驰把检测报告复印件摊在桌上，推到陈默眼前。“DNA匹配。你工作台上面的血迹，就是被害人的。现在，还要继续否认吗？”
陈默盯着纸上的文字，瞳孔骤然放大，整个人瞬间垮了下去。刚刚硬撑起来的伪装，轰然碎裂。
他把头埋进臂弯，肩膀剧烈抖动，压抑的呜咽声从喉咙里挤出来。
“是……是我做的。”
声音沙哑微弱，断断续续。
“人是我杀的。”
江驰拿起笔，准备记录口供：“死者是谁，你们之間什麼關係？”
“他叫赵强，之前跟我合伙做工程，欠了我一大笔钱，一直拖着不还。”陈默声音颤抖，“我找他很多次，每次都被他耍，他还威胁我，说要砸了我的工作室。”
“那天晚上，我约他到工作室谈还钱的事。我们吵起来，情绪上头，我拿起器械刀刺中了他胸口。”
他顿了顿，眼神涣散，继续交代。
“人死之后，我慌了。不知道该怎么处理尸体。我想起之前看到的那套处理尸体的步骤，就照着上面写的，把尸体肢解，连夜开车运到烂尾工地抛掉。”
“为什么要选那处工地？”陆峥追问。
“那边偏僻，很少有人去，下雨能冲掉痕迹。我想着雨水一泡，很多东西就查不出来。”
陈默一五一十，交代了行凶、分尸、抛尸的完整过程。作案动机、行凶过程、抛尸路线全部对上。
问到笔记本的来源，陈默说是在一个小众论坛偶然看到的帖子，保存抄写下来。发帖人是匿名账号，他根本不知道对方是谁，只是当时觉得写得很细致，就随手抄了。
“那个人，你线下见过吗？”陆峥抓住这个点。
“没有，完全没见过。网上聊过几句，对方话很少，只留下那些文字。”陈默摇着头，“我当时只是随便看看，后来出事，脑子里就想起了这份东西，照着做了。”
观察室里，许砚整理着口供要点：“动机是债务纠纷，激情杀人，事后参考网上教程处理尸体，单人作案。所有线索闭环。”
沈予安安静听完，缓缓开口：“口供和物证、现场痕迹基本吻合。可以继续核实死者身份，确认债务纠纷的真实性。”
陆峥安排江驰继续审讯，确认口供细节，核对时间线。
另一边，许砚立刻检索赵强的身份信息，核查他和陈默之间的债务往来记录。苏晚继续完善物证链，把所有检测报告整理归档。
傍晚，审讯结束。陈默被带回留置室暂时关押。
几人回到会议室汇总全部口供与证据。
“死者赵强身份确认，确实和陈默存在工程欠款纠纷，欠条、转账记录都查到了。”许砚把资料投屏，“两人多次发生争吵，周边邻居证词也能佐证。”
江驰揉了揉发酸的肩膀：“他交代的作案细节，和现场尸检、物证情况全部对上。抛尸时间、车辆路线，没有矛盾。”
陆峥扫视一圈众人：“案件基本事实清楚，证据链完整。等所有文书补齐，就可以准备结案。”
沈予安翻看着口供笔录，指尖轻轻划过陈默描述的网上匿名教程那段文字，淡淡说了一句：“网上偶尔会有这种猎奇帖子，只是没想到，真的会有人照着实施犯罪。”
语气平淡，仿佛只是感慨网络乱象。
天色彻底暗下来，窗外城市灯火亮起。
这桩恶性分尸案，走到了收尾阶段。所有人都觉得，案子马上画上句号。
en: Nine in the morning.

The blinds in the municipal bureau’s Criminal Investigation Detachment conference room were half closed. Slivers of morning light cut the room into alternating bands of light and shade. Autopsy reports, laboratory results, surveillance stills, and interview notes from the night before covered the table in neat, thick stacks.
After a night of nonstop work, everyone’s eyes were bloodshot. Their attention, however, remained sharp. No one had relaxed.
Lu Zheng sat at the head of the table, tapping it lightly with his fingertips. His voice was steady as he opened the case review.
“Bring everything together. We go through it again, discard what gets us nowhere, and narrow the field.”
He looked around the room.
“Physical evidence first. Su Wan.”
Su Wan stood and went to the screen, bringing up the laboratory data.
“The soil samples, deposits on the grass fragments, and trace grease on the remains all point to the same source.”

“First, the grease is a specialist lubricant for high-end precision instruments. It isn’t sold in ordinary retail shops. Small batches go directly to precision-equipment repair workshops and private modification studios. There are three registered purchasers in Nancheng.”

“Second, the microfiber barrier cloth found at the scene is resistant to water, dust, and debris. It isn’t a hospital operating-room consumable. It’s a dust-control wiping cloth used in precision-equipment work.”
“Third, none of the trace deposits contains laboratory reagent residue. That rules out an established research facility or a public hospital laboratory as the crime scene.”
She closed the data page, leaving the three purchasers’ names on the screen.

“We can eliminate the two established biological laboratories after screening. Both keep complete inventory records. Staff rotations are documented, surveillance coverage is comprehensive, and every use of equipment and materials over the past month can be accounted for. No gaps.”
“That leaves one: a private precision-equipment modification workshop on the outskirts.”
The atmosphere in the room grew heavier.
Xu Yan picked up the thread, touching a name on the list in his hand.

“I’ve checked the personnel. The workshop’s legal representative is Chen Mo. Forty-two, local, no criminal record. Simple social ties. Married, one son. His public reputation is honest, hardworking, and technically competent.”
“It’s a small operation. Chen Mo is the only full-time worker. He occasionally takes on short-term apprentices, but has no permanent employees. He could have acted alone.”
Jiang Chi leaned back in his chair and spoke.
“The surveillance review has come through too.”
He opened an enhanced high-resolution still from the highway checkpoint. A small, dark minivan appeared on the screen.

“At 1:07 a.m. on the night in question, this vehicle came from the direction of the unfinished development. That falls within our estimated disposal window. Image enhancement confirmed the plate. The registered owner is Chen Mo.”
“His was the only private vehicle matching the time, route, and area. We’ve ruled out the others.”
Three independent lines of inquiry: the source of the evidence, the suspect’s circumstances, and his movements.
All converged on one man.
The chain linking him to the crime was complete.
Shen Yu’an sat to one side, quietly listening to the deductions. His gaze rested on Chen Mo’s identification photograph on the screen.
The man in the picture was unremarkable, with an earnest face. He looked like a craftsman who spent his days bent over a workbench. There was nothing overtly vicious about him.
Shen Yu’an spoke, his tone precise.
“One addition from the autopsy findings.”
“The method looks systematic, but the details of the dismemberment show a distinct lack of practice. Someone following and imitating a fixed procedure, not a professional accustomed to dissection.”

“Chen Mo’s work modifying precision equipment requires familiarity with the structure of devices modeled on the human body, and a basic understanding of tissue structure. That fits the killer’s level of technical knowledge.”
“Neither more nor less skilled than we would expect.”
Those few observations closed off the remaining room for doubt.
Lu Zheng nodded and summed up in a low voice.
“All the objective evidence currently points to Chen Mo. No second suspect. No separate line of inquiry.”

“But so far we have his movements and physical evidence. We still lack the victim’s identity, a motive, witness accounts, and a statement. We’re not drawing final conclusions or closing anything yet. Verify his personal connections first.”
He assigned the work quickly, each task clear and specific.

“Jiang Chi, take a team back out. Speak to the neighbors, shopkeepers, and former apprentices around Chen Mo’s workshop. Find out about his recent state of mind, any disputes, any grudges he’s kept quiet.”
“Xu Yan, dig into his private contacts, loans, and personal disputes. Look for recent large transactions or people he’s been meeting discreetly.”
“Su Wan, keep comparing the workshop’s material samples. Establish a conclusive common-source match. Make the evidence solid.”
They acknowledged their assignments and dispersed.
At ten, the investigation team’s vehicles left the municipal bureau again.
Jiang Chi led the team straight to the workshop district on the outskirts.

Chen Mo’s studio occupied one of a row of single-story roadside buildings beside the national highway. It had its own entrance and courtyard, with an inconspicuous, rusting sign above the gate. Usually, hardly anyone came or went.
The neighboring businesses were small hardware shops, repair shops, and processing workshops.
Jiang Chi divided the inquiries among the nearby residents, neighboring shop owners, and the little store at the intersection.
The canvass moved quickly.
The hardware shop owner next door remembered clearly.
“Chen Mo? Seems honest enough. Doesn’t talk much. Keeps his head down and works. Never causes trouble. Though… something’s been off these past couple of weeks.”

“He used to open and close on time every day. Lately he’s been there until two or three every night. You can hear the machinery in the yard after midnight. A few days ago I got up in the night and saw his headlights on. The van was filthy, covered in yellow mud. I asked where he’d been. He said he’d gone into the hills to collect materials.”
A woman who ran another shop added something else.

“He argued with a man I didn’t recognize a little while ago. Right outside the shop. A terrible row, both of them red in the face. The man was quite solidly built. Not local. Came twice, acting furtive both times. Never went inside. Just talked to him privately at the gate.”
A crucial gap in the evidence suddenly opened up.
A concealed personal conflict.
Jiang Chi pressed her at once. “When was this? What did he look like? Height? Anything distinctive?”

“Five or six days ago, I think. Around the time this happened.” She considered it carefully. “Somewhere over one meter seventy. Sturdy. Looked like trouble. Black clothes and a hat, so I couldn’t see his face properly. After that argument, he never came back.”
The lead clicked into place.
Xu Yan, screening records remotely as the inquiries came in, sent a message almost immediately.

“Found something. Six months ago Chen Mo became involved in private high-interest borrowing. The debt recently fell due, and he’s been pressed for repayment several times. There are unexplained transactions in his account: frequent small deposits whose source we can’t trace.”
“He also had a serious dispute over a job three months ago with a worker from outside the area. The man came to his workshop repeatedly to argue.”
The fragments fitted together.
Grievances, disputes, concealed relationships, unusual activity at night, matching physical evidence, and confirmed movements.
The suspicion against him tightened.
At noon, all the field reports reached the municipal bureau.
The team gathered in a small meeting room for a quick review.
“We can establish it,” Jiang Chi said firmly. “Chen Mo had the time, the space, the tools, and a motive. All the external circumstances fit.”
Su Wan entered with the latest comparison report and set it on the table.
“The final source comparison is complete.”
“The lubricant and barrier-cloth fibers from the scene have the same molecular structure as the stock in Chen Mo’s workshop. They belong to the same production batch.”
Now there was hard evidence.
The person, the materials, the time, the place, the motive: all five lines were in place.
Lu Zheng looked up, decisive.
“Apply for the summons and the search warrant.”
“Bring Chen Mo in. Now.”
Shen Yu’an stood by the window, watching the police vehicles leave below. His expression was mild when he spoke.
“I hope we can establish the truth quickly. Give the victim an answer.”
At half past one, the sun hung fiercely over Nancheng. The air was stifling, and heat shimmered above the asphalt.
Two unmarked police cars eased to a stop at the entrance to the workshop street. A few dozen meters away stood Chen Mo’s private equipment studio.
The courtyard wall was low and built of red brick. Inside sat the dark minivan from the highway footage. The gate was ajar. The intermittent hum of metal grinding drifted into the street.
Jiang Chi sat in the front passenger seat of the leading car, holding the search warrant and summons documents. He briefed Lu Zheng quietly.
“The perimeter is covered. Two officers at the rear wall in case he tries to climb out. Both access routes are watched. He won’t get away.”
Lu Zheng nodded, his eyes on the gate. “Remember, he has precision cutting tools. There’s a risk of armed resistance. Keep it calm. Don’t escalate unless you have to.”

Xu Yan stayed in the car with a tablet, pulling up surveillance around the workshop and watching for movement in the yard. Su Wan followed behind the others with her collection kit, ready to secure physical evidence as soon as the search began.
“Move.”
Lu Zheng gave the order quietly.
Jiang Chi approached the gate with two plainclothes officers. He raised his hand and knocked lightly on the wood.
The grinder stopped.
“Who is it?” The man’s voice came from inside, edged with suspicion.
“Police. Please open the gate. We need to check some details with you about a case.” Jiang Chi’s voice was steady, without deliberate pressure.
Several seconds passed. Then the gate opened inward a crack.

Chen Mo stood behind it in work clothes dusted with metal shavings. A smear of grime marked his face. At the sight of the plainclothes officers, his pupils contracted. He took an involuntary half-step back. His fingers quietly closed around a long, narrow craft knife on the edge of the workbench beside him.
“Police? What do you want with me?” His voice was dry. He was trying to sound calm.

“Chen Mo, we have a search warrant and a summons. You need to come to the municipal bureau for questioning. We’ll also be searching your workshop.” Lu Zheng stepped forward and showed his identification, his eyes fixed on the man.
Chen Mo went pale. His lips trembled, and his gaze darted toward the back wall as he calculated a way out. But officers were already visible at both ends. The escape route was closed.
“I… I haven’t broken the law.” His throat tightened. His grip on the knife grew firmer.
“Put the tool down.” Jiang Chi moved half a step closer. “No sudden movements.”

Chen Mo’s nerves broke. He spun, trying to rush into the building. Jiang Chi stepped in at once, caught his arm, and drove him down against the workbench. The knife struck the concrete with a sharp clatter.
“Don’t move!”
Cold handcuffs clicked around Chen Mo’s wrists.
He struggled hard a few times, then quickly spent his strength. His shoulders heaved as he gasped for breath. Head lowered, he stopped resisting. Only the trembling continued.
“Take him out,” Lu Zheng said.
Two officers escorted Chen Mo to the car and seated him in the back.
Meanwhile, Su Wan and the scene-examination officers entered the workshop and began a thorough search.

The room was small. Metal stock and grinding equipment occupied half of it. Consumables lined the shelves in orderly rows, including the precision synthetic grease and a stack of microfiber barrier cloth matching the fibers recovered at the scene.
Faint brown, dried traces remained in the seams of the workbench. Su Wan carefully sampled them with a swab and sealed it.
“Team Leader Lu. Possible blood residue here. And matching consumables.”

Xu Yan entered and looked around. In a corner stood a simple storage cabinet. Inside, he found a notebook. The first part recorded equipment-calibration settings. Farther back were scattered written instructions, apparently steps in a procedure.
“Looks like notes copied from a set process.” He turned a couple of pages, frowning slightly. “The wording is stiff. Doesn’t read like something he worked out himself. More like a transcription.”
Lu Zheng came over and examined the notebook, his fingertip passing across the paper.
“Bag all of it. Bring it back as evidence.”

Only then did Shen Yu’an enter the workshop. His gaze moved slowly over the bench and the floor before settling briefly on the notebook. He said nothing about it. Bending to look at the traces Su Wan had sampled, he spoke softly. “We should compare the DNA from the workbench residue as soon as possible. Confirm whether it belongs to the victim.”
“Understood.” Su Wan nodded.
The search lasted an hour and a half. Every suspicious item was sealed, packed, and logged.
The sun edged westward, and the heat eased a little. The cars headed back to the municipal bureau with the suspect and a full container of evidence.
Chen Mo sat rigidly in the car, his head down. He said nothing.
Beside him, Jiang Chi occasionally turned to study his face. Chen Mo spoke only when questioned and avoided the important points. He looked like a frightened, cornered animal.
At the bureau, he was taken straight to an interrogation room.
Lu Zheng and Jiang Chi prepared to question him. Xu Yan waited in the observation room to assess changes in his state of mind. Su Wan rushed the newly collected samples to the lab for comparison.
Lu Zheng lifted his radio. “Begin the interrogation.”
Cold white light fell directly on Chen Mo’s face. The walls absorbed sound, and the enclosed room felt stifling.
He was secured in a metal interrogation chair, his handcuffs fastened at the edge of the table. His head hung low, hair falling over his eyes. His shoulders trembled faintly without stopping.

Jiang Chi sat opposite him with an interview notebook open and the recorder running. Lu Zheng sat beside Jiang Chi. He did not speak immediately. He simply watched Chen Mo, letting the silence bear down.

Behind the one-way glass, Xu Yan held a tablet and recorded the suspect’s fleeting expressions. Shen Yu’an stood beside him, his hands resting loosely in front of him. His calm gaze remained on the man beyond the glass. He looked like no more than an observer. Nothing in his manner was unusual.
“Chen Mo. I’ll ask again. The dismembered man at the unfinished Jin Xiu Lan Ting development. Did you do it?” Jiang Chi spoke first, level and unemotional.
Chen Mo lowered his head farther. His answer was muffled. “It wasn’t me. I told you. I was working in the studio that night.”

“We found matching grease and cloth in your workshop, and suspected blood residue in the workbench seams.” Jiang Chi pushed the evidence photographs into the middle of the table. “Highway footage shows your vehicle coming from the direction of the site in the early hours. Explain that.”

Chen Mo jerked. His lips worked, but he clung to his denial. “You can buy those things all over the place! Hundreds of cars use that highway. What makes you say I went to the site? Those traces you keep talking about are rust from metalwork, not human blood!”
His answers came quickly. Each defense sounded as though he had rehearsed it countless times.
Lu Zheng leaned forward slightly and held his gaze. “The notebook in your cabinet. The dismemberment instructions copied into it. Explain those.”
Chen Mo’s shoulders locked. His eyes flicked away in panic.
“That… that was just something I found online. I was curious. I never used it to hurt anyone.”
“Which website? Where’s the link? Who wrote it?” Lu Zheng followed immediately.
Chen Mo faltered. He stammered for a while without an answer. “I… I can’t remember. It was ages ago. I can’t find it now.”
In the observation room, Xu Yan spoke quietly to Shen Yu’an. “His defenses are starting to give. He avoids all the core details. Nothing in his invented account can be independently checked.”

Inside, Jiang Chi continued. “We took samples from the seams in your workbench. Su Wan is having them tested urgently. We’ll have the results soon. If they match the victim’s DNA, none of these denials will help.”
Chen Mo’s breathing grew faster. His chest rose and fell sharply. His fingertips dug into his palms, the nails almost breaking the skin.

A few minutes later, the observation room’s communications unit sounded. Su Wan’s voice came through. “Team Leader Lu. The DNA comparison is complete. The residue on the workbench is confirmed as blood tissue from our victim.”
The evidence was conclusive.
Lu Zheng picked up the radio. “Tell him.”
Jiang Chi laid a copy of the report on the table and slid it toward Chen Mo. “The DNA matches. The blood on your workbench belongs to the victim. Are you still going to deny it?”
Chen Mo stared at the words. His eyes widened, and he seemed to collapse in on himself. The front he had fought to maintain broke apart.
He buried his face in his arms. His shoulders shook violently, and a strangled sob forced its way out of his throat.
“It… it was me.”
The words were faint, hoarse, broken.
“I killed him.”
Jiang Chi picked up his pen. “Who was he? What was your relationship?”

“Zhao Qiang. We worked on a project together. He owed me a lot of money and kept putting off paying it back.” Chen Mo’s voice shook. “I went to him again and again. He strung me along every time. He even threatened to smash up my workshop.”
“That night I asked him to come over so we could discuss repayment. We argued. I lost control and picked up a cutting tool. I stabbed him in the chest.”
He paused, his eyes unfocused, then continued.

“After he died, I panicked. I didn’t know what to do with the body. I remembered those instructions I’d seen. I followed them, cut up the body, then drove it out to the unfinished site during the night and dumped it.”
“Why that site?” Lu Zheng asked.
“It’s out of the way. Hardly anyone goes there. Rain would wash the traces off. I thought once everything had soaked, there wouldn’t be much left to find.”
Chen Mo described the killing, dismemberment, and disposal in detail. The motive, sequence of events, and route to the site all fitted.

Asked where the notebook’s contents had come from, he said he had stumbled across a post on a niche forum and copied it down. The poster used an anonymous account. He had no idea who they were. He had only copied it because the description seemed so detailed.
“Have you ever met that person offline?” Lu Zheng seized on the point.

“No. Never.” Chen Mo shook his head. “We exchanged a few messages online. They didn’t say much. Just left those instructions. I was only browsing at the time. Then, when it happened, I remembered them and followed them.”
In the observation room, Xu Yan summarized the statement. “Debt dispute. A killing in the heat of the moment, then disposal based on online instructions. One perpetrator. All the leads tie up.”

Shen Yu’an listened in silence before speaking. “The statement is broadly consistent with the physical evidence and the scene. We can verify the victim’s identity next, and confirm that the debt dispute was real.”
Lu Zheng told Jiang Chi to continue questioning Chen Mo, check the details of his statement, and verify the timeline.

Xu Yan immediately began searching Zhao Qiang’s identity records and the financial dealings between the two men. Su Wan continued completing the physical evidence chain and filing the laboratory reports.
The interrogation ended toward evening. Chen Mo was taken back to a holding room.
The team returned to the conference room to review the statements and evidence.

“The victim’s identity is confirmed: Zhao Qiang. There was a payment dispute with Chen Mo over a project. We’ve found the written acknowledgment of debt and the transfer records.” Xu Yan projected the documents. “They argued on several occasions. The neighbors’ statements corroborate that.”
Jiang Chi rubbed his aching shoulders. “His account matches the scene, the autopsy, and the physical evidence. No contradictions in the disposal time or the vehicle route.”
Lu Zheng looked around the table. “The basic facts are clear. The evidence chain is complete. Once the paperwork is in order, we can prepare to close the investigation.”

Shen Yu’an leafed through the statement. His fingertip passed lightly over the passage describing the anonymous instructions online. “You do see morbid posts like that sometimes. I just never thought someone would actually follow one to commit a crime.”
His tone was casual, as though he were merely reflecting on the uglier corners of the internet.
Outside, darkness settled over the city and the lights came on.
The brutal dismemberment case was entering its final stage. Everyone believed it was almost over.

zh: 晚上十点整，市公安局刑侦支队主楼依旧通体透亮。整栋大楼没有深夜该有的沉寂，楼道间偶尔传来脚步声、对讲机滋滋的电流声、会议室收尾复盘的低声讨论。
市局不同于辖区派出所，这里囤积的永远是全市最棘手、最血腥、最颠覆常规的恶性案件。灯火通明，是刑侦支队一年四季不变的常态。
锦绣澜庭城郊碎尸案，从雨夜突发报案、现场勘查、物证筛查、轨迹锁定、外勤抓捕、连夜审讯，整整耗时七十二小时。
到此刻，所有侦办步骤全部走完。
顶层局长办公室的灯光亮着。
市局一把手周振海坐在办公桌后，手里翻阅着刚刚汇总上交的全套案卷，厚厚的一叠卷宗压在桌面，边角规整，封条严密。
年过五十的周振海，眉眼沉稳锐利，鬓角带着浅浅霜白，常年坐镇刑侦一线，见过无数极端凶案，心性早已沉淀得古井无波。但此刻逐字看着尸检报告与审讯笔录，指尖依旧轻轻点着桌面，神色审慎。
办公室沙发上，坐着刚结束全部收尾工作的陆峥。
两人之间沉默数秒，只有中央空调出风口均匀的送风声响。
“单人激情犯罪，债务纠纷诱发杀人，事后模仿网络猎奇教程分尸抛尸？”
周振海抬眼，目光落在陆峥身上，语气沉稳。
“是。”陆峥坐姿端正，汇报条理清晰，“全部证据闭环，无同伙、无教唆、无团伙特征。嫌疑人陈默口供稳定，全程无翻供，作案动机、行凶时间、抛尸路线、事后心理，全部经得起交叉核验。”
周振海翻开案卷中段，看着那页境外匿名论坛的溯源报告，微微蹙眉：
“技术科真的一点源头都扒不出来？”
“是。”陆峥如实回答，“多层虚拟IP跳转，境外隐蔽服务器，无账号实名、无发帖记录留存。技术支队那边加班溯源六个小时，最终判定无法追踪发布者身份。只能定性为境外私人猎奇非法内容站点。”
周振海轻轻叹气，合上卷宗：
“近些年网络乱象太严重，大量极端、变态、反人类的内容隐蔽流通，很多心智不稳、身处绝境的普通人，很容易被这些歪门邪道的东西诱导，走上绝路。”
“陈默本来是有手艺、能安稳过日子的匠人，就是被债务逼到心态失衡，又接触到这种黑色教程，一念之差，彻底毁了自己。”
他抬手揉了揉眉心，抬眼叮嘱：
“案子办得很漂亮，干净、利落、证据扎实。这几天你们整组连轴转，辛苦你们了。案卷立刻规整归档，走司法移送流程，尽快移交检察院。”
“明白。”陆峥颔首。
“不过。”周振海话锋微转，神色严肃几分，“你心里也要有数。南城今年下半年的恶性案发率，比往年高出太多了。普通民事纠纷、仇杀、财杀激增，极端个案层出不穷。”
“你带的重案一组是全市尖刀队伍，后续一定要绷紧弦，不能因为刚结大案就松懈。”
“我清楚。”陆峥应声。
简单的谈话，敲定了这桩案子的最终收尾。
办公室门外，刑侦办公区依旧一片忙碌。
重案组五人之外，整个楼层数十名警员各司其职，没人敢松懈。
档案室两名文职女警正在扫描案卷、录入系统、归档封存，指尖在键盘上飞快跳跃，屏幕蓝光映着认真的眉眼。技术支队三名技术员坐在专属工位，整理着这起案子剩余的影像素材、监控修复文件、物证备份资料。
隔壁经侦组的队员刚刚结束外勤回队，满身风尘，低声交接着手头的金融诈骗案件，和重案组的血腥凶案形成鲜明对比。
办公区中央。
许砚正坐在工位前，二次复核所有口供漏洞。
哪怕案子已经结案移交，他依旧习惯性把所有时间线、人物关系、证词细节再复盘一遍。这是他多年养成的职业习惯，绝不放过任何一丝微小破绽。
平板屏幕上，密密麻麻铺满时间节点：
赵强欠款上门寻衅记录、陈默工作室夜间异常开工记录、国道卡口行车轨迹、案发时间段天气水文记录、鄰居证词时间线。
线条严丝合缝，没有半点偏差。
“完美闭环。”
许砚低声自语，指尖轻轻划过屏幕，彻底放下心来。
不远处，江驰靠在办公桌旁，和两名年轻外勤警员低声交代后续流程。
“留置室笔录再核对一遍，嫌疑人签字手印全部确认，瑕疵笔录立刻补正。司法流程不能出一点纰漏，一旦案卷有瑕疵，后续庭审会出问题。”
两名年轻警员立刻应声：“收到驰哥，我们现在就核对。”
江驰性子直率，带新人极其严格，外勤、抓捕、文书流程，手把手教，组里大半年轻队员都是他带出来的。
苏晚坐在化验对接工位上，和技术科的专职化验员对接最终数据存档。
“所有微量物证、DNA比对报告、油脂纤维溯源报告，全部上传市局物证云库，加密留存。纸质报告一式三份，刑侦、法制、档案室各存一份。”
“没问题，苏姐，马上归档完毕。”技术科警员认真应答。
整个办公区忙而不乱、井然有序。
沈予安站在最角落的法医专属工位前，安静整理着最后一套法医归档材料。
他脱下沾满消毒水味道的外勤防护服，叠放整齐，放进专用消毒收纳柜。换上干净的浅色衬衫，袖口平整利落，身姿清挺温和。
桌上摊开的，是最终定稿的尸检总结、伤情图谱、残留物分析报告。
严谨、客观，没有主观偏差。
作为市局唯一一名全职在编主检法医，他经手了南城近三年百分之八十的重大命案尸检工作，零差错、零争议、零瑕疵。
队里所有人、领导、新人警员，提起沈予安，永远是同一个评价——温柔、耐心、专业、靠谱，是整个重案组最让人安心的存在。
整理材料的间隙，旁边档案室的文职小姑娘捧着一杯热温水走过来，轻声笑道：
“沈法医，又通宵收尾呀？每次大案结束，就你收尾最久。快喝点水歇歇，你都连着熬三天了。”
沈予安抬眼，眉眼柔和，浅浅点头：“谢谢。尸体是不会说谎的，每一份报告，都要对得起逝者。多核对一遍，心里踏实。”
他说话永远温和有礼，对待新人、文职、后勤，从来没有半点架子。
小姑娘忍不住感慨：“还好有你在，每次这么惨烈的案子，都是你一点点还原真相，看着都吓人，你居然一点都不怕。”
“习惯了。”沈予安淡淡笑了笑，“我们多细致一分，真相就清楚一分。也對得起那些死去的人”
两句对话，温柔坦荡，光明磊落。
那份让所有人奉为铁证、完美闭环的尸检报告里，有一处微乎其微、完全不影响案件定性的细节，被他不动声色地微调过参数误差范围。
正当所有人陆续收尾、准备结束连日苦战、短暂休整的时候。
办公区入口，一名穿着制式警服的通信警员快步走进来，手里拿着一份红色加急电传，神色凝重。
“陆队！紧急协查通报！”
声音落下，原本稍稍松弛的办公区，瞬间安静一瞬。
陆峥刚从局长办公室走出来，闻声脚步一顿：“什么情况？”
“邻市安安市发来的跨市紧急协查！”通信警员语速极快，将电报送至陆峥手中，“安安市城西老城区，今晚八点发现居民楼异常腐臭，破门之后，发现室内存在极端惨烈命案，疑似涉及人体组织异常留存，作案手法猎奇、极端变态，当地支队初步判断单人心理扭曲作案，请求南城市局协助支援！”
这句话一出，许砚、江驰、苏晚几人同时抬头，神色瞬间凝重。
南城大案刚结，邻市大案突发。
“安··安市？”江驰皱眉，“那边治安一直比我们稳，很少出这种极端的命案啊。”
许砚立刻上前，接过协查通报快速浏览。
通报内容不长，字字惊心。
【安安市西城区老旧居民小区，住户失联多日，邻居投诉屋内恶臭。辖区民警联合消防破门排查，屋内发现大量疑似人体残骸，现场环境诡异，存在明显人为留存、刻意囤积、变态处理痕迹，初步排除普通仇杀、财杀，疑似极端心理变态独立作案，手法罕见，无团伙痕迹，请求南城重案组支援侧写与物证技术协助。】
陆峥看完通报，神色沉冷，立刻进入工作状态：
“所有人立刻停手头收尾工作。”
“江驰，立刻整理外勤装备、抓捕器械、勘查全套设备。”
“苏晚，对接安安市物证科，建立临时物证互通通道，准备随时接收微量样本数据。”
“许砚，即刻调取安安市近三年变态犯罪、独居人员极端犯罪卷宗，提前做预案侧写。”
“沈予安，准备法医跨市支援器材，随时准备奔赴现场。”
“收到！”
五人齐声应下，动作干脆利落。
旁边几名年轻警员、文职人员也立刻主动帮忙整理装备、复印通报、对接通讯频道，整个刑侦区瞬间重新运转起来。
陆峥抬手看了一眼时间，沉声开口：
“十分钟后，全队整装出发，跨市支援安安市！”
刚刚落下帷幕的血腥尘埃尚未彻底冷却。
新一轮更加扭曲、更加恐怖、更加颠覆认知的猎奇罪恶，已然在邻市的黑暗角落里，悄然发酵成熟。
暗流无声，纯白依旧。
en: At ten that night, the main building of the municipal public security bureau’s Criminal Investigation Detachment was still ablaze with light. It had none of the stillness of a late hour. Footsteps sounded in the corridors, radios crackled, and low voices drifted from conference rooms where final case reviews were under way.

The municipal bureau was not a neighborhood police station. The city’s most difficult, bloodiest, most disturbing cases ended up here. For the Criminal Investigation Detachment, lights burning through the night were a year-round routine.

Seventy-two hours had passed since the call about the dismembered body at Jin Xiu Lan Ting: the rain-soaked scene, the examination of physical evidence, the tracing of movements, the arrest, and the overnight questioning.
Now every stage of the investigation was complete.
On the top floor, the bureau director’s office was lit.

Zhou Zhenhai, head of the municipal bureau, sat behind his desk, reading the complete case file that had just been submitted. The thick stack lay squarely on the desktop, its edges aligned and its seals secure.

Over fifty, Zhou Zhenhai had steady, penetrating eyes and a dusting of gray at his temples. Years at the forefront of criminal investigation had exposed him to countless brutal killings. Little could disturb him now. Yet as he read the autopsy report and interview transcripts word by word, his fingertips tapped lightly on the desk. His expression remained watchful.
Lu Zheng sat on the office sofa. He had just finished the last of the closing work.
For a few seconds neither spoke. Only the even rush of air from the central air-conditioning vent filled the room.
“A lone offender. A killing in the heat of the moment over a debt, followed by dismemberment and disposal copied from morbid instructions online?”
Zhou Zhenhai looked up at Lu Zheng, his voice measured.

“Yes.” Lu Zheng sat upright and delivered his report clearly. “The evidence chain is complete. No accomplice, no evidence of instigation, no indication of organized involvement. Chen Mo’s statement has remained consistent. He hasn’t recanted at any point. Motive, time of the killing, disposal route, and his state of mind afterward—all stand up to cross-checking.”
Zhou Zhenhai opened the middle of the file and frowned slightly at the report on the anonymous overseas forum.
“The technical section really couldn’t trace the source?”

“No,” Lu Zheng answered. “Multiple layers of virtual IP redirection. Concealed servers overseas. No verified account identity and no retained posting history. The technical detachment spent six hours tracing it and concluded they couldn’t identify the poster. All we can establish is that it’s a privately run overseas site carrying illegal, morbid content.”
Zhou Zhenhai sighed softly and closed the file.

“The internet has become a serious problem these past few years. Extreme, depraved, inhuman material circulates out of sight. Ordinary people who are unstable or desperate can be drawn in so easily. It leads them down a road they can’t come back from.”
“Chen Mo had a skill. He could have made an honest living. The debt pushed him off balance, then he encountered those instructions. One disastrous decision, and he destroyed himself.”
He rubbed the space between his brows, then looked up.

“You handled the case well. Clean work, efficient, solid evidence. Your whole team has been going nonstop. You’ve all worked hard. Put the files in order and archive them. Begin the judicial transfer process. Get the case to the procuratorate as soon as possible.”
“Understood.” Lu Zheng nodded.

“But.” Zhou Zhenhai’s expression sharpened. “Keep this in mind. The rate of serious violent crime in Nancheng this second half of the year is far higher than in previous years. Cases arising from ordinary civil disputes, revenge killings, killings for money—they’re all up. Extreme cases keep appearing.”
“Your Major Crime Team One is the city’s spearhead. Stay alert. Finishing a major case is no reason to let your guard down.”
“I understand,” Lu Zheng said.
That brief conversation settled the final handling of the case.
Outside the office, the criminal investigation floor was still busy.
Beyond the five members of the major crime team, dozens of officers worked at their own tasks. No one could afford to ease off.

In the records room, two female administrative officers scanned files, entered them into the system, and sealed them for storage. Their fingers moved quickly over the keyboards, blue screen light falling across intent faces. Three technicians at the technical detachment’s workstations organized the remaining footage, enhanced surveillance files, and copies of the physical evidence records.

Officers from the neighboring economic crime team had just returned from fieldwork, tired and dusty. They quietly handed over details of a financial fraud case—a sharp contrast to the bloody work of the major crime team.
In the middle of the office floor,
Xu Yan sat at his desk, checking the statements once more for gaps.

Even after an investigation was closed and handed over, he habitually reviewed every timeline, relationship, and detail of testimony. It was a discipline built over years. No discrepancy was too small to examine.
His tablet was crowded with entries on the timeline:

Records of Zhao Qiang’s visits and confrontations over the debt. Chen Mo’s unusual nighttime work. Vehicle movements at the highway checkpoint. Weather and water conditions during the relevant period. The timing of the neighbors’ observations.
Every line fitted. Nothing was out of place.
“A perfect chain.”
Xu Yan murmured it to himself, passing a fingertip over the screen. At last, he let his concern go.
A short distance away, Jiang Chi leaned against a desk and briefed two young field officers on the remaining procedures.

“Check the holding-room records again. Confirm every signature and fingerprint. Correct any deficiencies in the statements immediately. There can’t be a single procedural slip. If the file is flawed, we’ll have problems when it reaches trial.”
“Understood, Jiang Chi. We’ll check now,” the two officers answered at once.
Jiang Chi was direct and exacting with new officers. Fieldwork, arrests, paperwork—he taught every step himself. He had trained more than half the team’s younger members.
At the laboratory liaison desk, Su Wan worked with a dedicated analyst from the technical section to archive the final data.

“Upload all trace evidence records, DNA comparison reports, and grease and fiber source reports to the bureau’s cloud evidence repository. Keep the records encrypted. Three copies of each paper report: one for criminal investigation, one for legal affairs, and one for the records room.”
“No problem, Su Wan. We’ll finish the filing right away,” the technical officer answered earnestly.
The floor was busy but orderly.
In the farthest corner, Shen Yu’an stood at the forensic medicine workstation, quietly arranging the final set of documents for the archive.

He removed the field protective clothing that smelled of disinfectant, folded it neatly, and placed it in the designated disinfection cabinet. In a clean, pale shirt with crisp cuffs, he looked composed and gentle.
Spread across his desk were the final autopsy summary, injury diagrams, and residue analysis reports.
Rigorous. Objective. Free of personal bias.

As the municipal bureau’s only full-time staff forensic physician serving as lead examiner, he had conducted eighty percent of Nancheng’s major homicide autopsies over the past three years. No errors. No disputes. No flaws.
His colleagues, his superiors, the new officers—everyone described Shen Yu’an in the same way. Gentle, patient, professional, dependable. No one in the major crime team inspired greater confidence.
As he organized the papers, a young administrative officer from the records room came over with a cup of warm water. She smiled softly.
“Dr. Shen, another night finishing up? You’re always the last one still at it after a major case. Have some water and take a break. You’ve been going for three days.”
Shen Yu’an looked up with a mild expression and a small nod. “Thank you. The dead don’t lie. Every report has to do right by them. One more check gives me peace of mind.”
He was always courteous and soft-spoken. With new officers, administrative staff, or support workers, he never put on airs.
“It’s a good thing you’re here,” she said. “Every time we get a case this awful, you piece the truth together. Just looking at it is frightening. And you’re never scared at all.”
“I’m used to it.” Shen Yu’an smiled faintly. “The more careful we are, the clearer the truth becomes. We owe that to those who’ve died.”
A brief exchange. Gentle, open, entirely aboveboard.

Yet in that autopsy report—the one everyone regarded as incontrovertible evidence, the final link in a perfect chain—there was one minute detail. It had no bearing on the classification of the case. Without drawing attention to it, he had made a slight adjustment to a parameter’s margin of error.
Just as the others were finishing up, ready to put days of relentless work behind them and rest for a little while,
a communications officer in uniform hurried through the entrance. He carried an urgent red-marked dispatch. His expression was grave.
“Team Leader Lu! Urgent request for assistance!”
The floor, which had begun to relax, fell suddenly quiet.
Lu Zheng had just left the director’s office. He stopped. “What is it?”

“An urgent cross-city request from neighboring An’an.” The officer spoke quickly as he handed over the dispatch. “At eight tonight, an unusual smell of decomposition was reported in a residential building in the old western district. Officers forced entry and found an exceptionally brutal homicide scene. Possible abnormal retention of human tissue. The method is bizarre and severely disturbing. Their detachment’s preliminary assessment is a lone offender with serious psychological disturbance. They’re requesting assistance from the Nancheng municipal bureau.”
Xu Yan, Jiang Chi, and Su Wan looked up together, their faces tightening.
One major case closed in Nancheng. Another erupting next door.
“An… An’an?” Jiang Chi frowned. “Public order there has always been steadier than here. They hardly ever get a killing this extreme.”
Xu Yan stepped forward at once and took the notice to read it.
It was brief. Every line was unsettling.

[An’an, western district, older residential compound. Resident out of contact for several days. Neighbors reported a foul smell from the apartment. Local police and fire personnel forced entry and discovered a large quantity of suspected human remains. Unusual scene conditions, with clear indications of deliberate retention, accumulation, and abnormal treatment. An ordinary revenge or financially motivated killing has provisionally been ruled out. Suspected lone offender with severe psychological disturbance. Uncommon method; no indication of organized involvement. Assistance requested from Nancheng’s major crime team for profiling and technical examination of physical evidence.]
Lu Zheng finished reading. His expression turned cold and focused. He was already back at work.
“Everyone, stop the closing work.”
“Jiang Chi, get the field gear, arrest equipment, and full scene-examination kit ready.”
“Su Wan, contact An’an’s evidence section. Set up a temporary channel for sharing evidence data. Be ready to receive trace sample results at any time.”
“Xu Yan, pull An’an’s files from the past three years on psychologically abnormal offenses and extreme crimes committed by people living alone. Prepare a preliminary profile.”
“Shen Yu’an, ready the forensic equipment for cross-city support. Be prepared to leave for the scene.”
“Understood!”
The five responded together and moved without hesitation.

Nearby, younger officers and administrative staff immediately began helping with equipment, copying the notice, and coordinating communications channels. The entire criminal investigation floor sprang back into motion.
Lu Zheng glanced at the time.
“Ten minutes. The whole team leaves fully equipped. We’re going to An’an.”
The bloody dust of the case they had just closed had barely settled.
In a dark corner of the neighboring city, something more twisted, more horrifying, more difficult to comprehend had already ripened unseen.
The undercurrent made no sound. The white remained unstained.

zh: 夜里十点二十分。
南城刑侦支队三辆制式警车鸣着低调警笛，驶出市局大院，直奔高速入口。
深秋的夜风砸在车窗上，带着刺骨的凉。城市霓虹飞速向后倒退，刚刚平息下来的血腥卷宗、结案余温，彻底被新一轮紧绷的氛围取代。
按照两市公安联防机制，邻市重大猎奇命案、变态心理犯罪，南城重案一组作为片区标杆尖刀队，必须第一时间跨市支援。
安安市距离南城车程四十分钟，不算远，但两市辖区治安风格、案发特点、刑侦节奏截然不同。
南城多市井纠纷、债务仇杀、暴力分尸；安安市老旧城区密集、流动人口杂、独居人群多，极少出现极端食人式变态凶案。
队内车厢气氛压抑到极致。
前车驾驶位，陆峥全程沉默开车，神色冷峻。跨市协查命案不同于本地办案，流程更繁琐、对接更复杂，且对方初步通报“现场极度诡异、存在人体组织留存囤积”，光是文字描述，就足以预判现场冲击力远超普通碎尸案。
副驾，许砚摊开安安市传来的全部前置资料，指尖快速滑动屏幕，低声梳理信息。
“案发地：安安市西城区，建安老小区。建成二十年以上，无物业精细化管理，楼道监控大半损坏，租户居多，邻里互不熟悉。”
“报警起因：三楼住户连续一周在家中传出浓烈腐臭，邻居起初以为是死老鼠、垃圾腐败，多次敲门无人应答，今晚臭味扩散整层楼道，居民恐慌报警。”
“辖区消防破门后，当场确认屋内为人尸腐臭味，立刻封锁现场，上报市局，启动跨市协查。”
后排，江驰靠在窗边，眉头紧锁，指尖无意识摩挲着手腕。
他跑过无数血腥现场、碎尸现场、抛尸荒山野岭的腐败尸体现场，但“刻意囤积人体组织、疑似食人猎奇”的案子，依旧是所有刑侦人员最抵触、最生理性不适的一类。
“食人向变态案，是所有凶案里心理摧残最狠的。”江驰低声开口，“普通凶手求财求仇，有迹可循、有动机可抓。这类变态，犯罪只为满足病态欲望，毫无逻辑，毫无底线。”
苏晚坐在一旁，提前打开随身物证系统，调试便携显微设备、微量物证采集仪。她神色紧绷，指尖微微发僵。
她常年泡在化验室，见惯了血迹、残肢、腐烂样本，但实验室是隔离处理、可控环境。
密闭活人居住空间、长期囤积人体组织、居家式变态留存，完全是两个维度的恐怖。
最后一排，沈予安坐姿端正松弛。
他随身法医工具箱放置在脚边，提前分类摆好解剖器械、取样试管、防腐试剂、痕迹固定棉片。动作细致平稳，呼吸均匀，脸上没有半点即将面对极致猎奇凶案的紧绷感。
他听见几人的对话，只是轻声补了一句，语气客观温和：
“这类心理畸变案件，凶手会把案发现场改造成自己的‘安全区’。现场痕迹密集、私人执念极强，反而更容易留下个人特征。”
警车一路疾驰，高速畅通，四十分钟后，准时驶入安安市西城区。
夜里十一点零三分。
建安老小区外围，早已被当地辖区民警拉起双层警戒线。
整条老旧街道清空围观群众，路口停靠消防车辆、辖区警车、安安市市局刑侦车，红蓝爆闪交织，把灰暗老旧的居民楼照得忽明忽暗，氛围感阴森压抑。
不同于南城工地露天抛尸的开阔荒凉，这里是居民区密闭室内凶宅。
活人居住、日夜作息、做饭起居的屋子，沦为猎奇犯罪、囤积腐尸的人间炼狱。
光是站在街口，就能闻到一缕缕顺着晚风飘出的、粘稠、浑浊、让人胃里翻涌的腐腥气。
那种味道不同于普通尸臭。
普通尸臭是衰败、腐败、死寂。
这里的味道，混杂着油脂酸败、肉质发酵、密闭空间闷捂、人居烟火残留的诡异混合气息，黏在鼻腔、糊在喉咙，生理性恶心极强。
陆峥带队下车。
安安市刑侦支队副支队长李建军立刻上前对接，满脸疲惫与凝重，眼底带着明显的反胃残留。
“陆队，辛苦你们连夜赶过来。”李建军声音沙哑，“说实话，干刑侦二十多年，我第一次碰见这么邪门的现场。我们队里四个年轻队员，破门进去第一眼，直接蹲在楼道吐了。”
他侧身让路，语气沉重：“你们要有心理准备，现场冲击力，远超你们想象。”
陆峥点头握手：“情况简单同步。”
“住户身份确认了吗？”
“确认了。”李建军沉声回道，“户主，林深，男，二十九岁，无固定职业，长期独居，社交透明，邻里无人熟悉。三个月前租住在此，深居简出，极少出门。”
“屋内目前发现大量碎片化软组织、人工切割留存的人体残骸、疑似烹煮残留痕迹。”
一句话落下，身后苏晚呼吸瞬间一滞。
江驰脸色微微发白，喉结狠狠滚动了一下。
烹煮留存。
这四个字，直接把案件定性钉死在极端食人变态犯罪上。
许砚笔尖一顿，眼神彻底沉下去。
旁边两名跟着对接的安安市年轻警员，光是复述案情，脸色都一阵青一阵白，明显还没从现场阴影里缓过来。
整个人群里，唯独沈予安神色如初。
他轻轻戴好一次性医用口罩、双层防护手套，扣紧防护服领口，轻声提醒身旁一名脸色发白的安市见习警员：“屏住呼吸，不要大口吸气，气味直冲胃管会更难受。实在撑不住就退到警戒线外。”
语气温柔，体贴入微。
那名小警员抬头，看着这位全网闻名、口碑极好的南城法医，勉强点头：“谢谢沈法医……我、我第一次见这种现场，有点顶不住。”
“正常。”沈予安淡淡安抚，“任何人第一次接触这类畸变现场，都会生理性不适，不用勉强自己。”
对接完毕，两队人马协同进场。
楼道老旧狭窄，墙皮斑驳脱落，白炽灯接触不良，滋滋电流杂响，光线忽闪忽灭。
越靠近三楼，空气里的腐腥黏腻感越重，压得人胸闷窒息。
走到二楼半楼梯转角，最先扛不住的是苏晚。
她常年在无菌化验室工作，鼻腔对异常气味极度敏感，浓烈的发酵腐腥钻进呼吸道，瞬间刺激得她胃里剧烈翻涌。
她停下脚步，弯腰、双手撑膝，死死憋着喉咙口的恶心，脸色从白皙变得泛青。
“没事吧？”江驰立刻侧身扶住她胳膊，自己也眉头紧蹙，强忍反胃，“撑不住先下楼。”
“不用。”苏晚咬牙摇头，深呼吸压下干呕感，声音发颤，“我能坚持，物证必须第一时间固定。”
许砚走到三楼平台时，太阳穴突突直跳。
他擅长心理侧写、接触过无数变态卷宗，但真实居家食人囤积现场，和纸面文字完全是两个概念。头皮一阵阵发麻，喉咙干涩发苦，生理性的心悸、反胃层层叠叠往上冒。
陆峥站在最前，肩背绷得笔直。
他心理素质全队最强，依旧能稳稳压制生理不适，但眼底凝重、眉心死死皱起，胸腔压抑发闷。
整条楼道，除了沈予安，全员都在硬扛恶心、反胃、心悸、头皮发麻的真实刑侦反应。
没有人能在这种人间恶景里坦然如常。
除了他。
三楼302室，房门完全敞开。
屋内漆黑一片，只有刑侦临时架设的冷光源探照灯打入室内，照亮了这片彻底颠覆人认知的凶宅。
普通居民小户型，客厅、卧室、厨房、阳台格局规整，本该是干净朴素的独居小屋。
此刻，满屋狼藉，血腥腐臭扑面而来，浓烈得让人瞬间窒息。
地面被反复清洗过，却洗不掉渗入地板缝隙、墙根死角的暗红污渍。
客厅茶几、置物架上，整齐摆放着大量经过精细切割、脱水、防腐处理的人体软组织残块。
不是慌乱抛置粗暴的分尸。
屋裡的肉塊规整摆放收纳、长期留存。
部分残骸表面，带着明显高温炙烤、水煮烹煮后的收缩硬化痕迹。
厨房灶台、料理台、洗菜池，残留大片反复清洗却无法彻底去除的血垢与油脂残留。
最让人脊背发凉的是——
整个屋子干净得诡异。
除了刻意留存的残骸，没有多余血迹、凌乱打斗、没有散落杂物。
凶手极其冷静、极其细致、极其耐心，把犯罪现场整理得井井有条，只留下自己想要珍藏的“藏品”。
身后一名安市年轻警员再也扛不住，转身冲到楼道窗口，弯腰剧烈干呕，吐得浑身发抖。
另一名老警员脸色惨白，死死咬着牙关，视线不敢往屋内多看一秒。
江驰站在门口，视线扫过屋内规整摆放的残块，胃部狠狠抽搐，喉咙一阵翻涌，他立刻移开视线，强迫自己冷静，指尖却控制不住微微收紧。
“典型的恋物型食人犯罪。”
许砚压下心底的寒意与生理性不适，声音微微发哑，开始临场初步侧写。
“凶手极度自律、洁癖、偏执、控制欲极端。作案不为财、不为仇、不为冲动泄愤，只为满足长期畸变的心理欲望。”
“留存、处理、规整摆放，是他的仪式感。”
陆峥抬手稳住心神，沉声下令：
“全员穿戴全套防护，分区域勘查。”
“江驰，带队封锁楼道、排查整栋楼出入轨迹、筛查住户作息。”
“许砚，现场行为痕迹侧写，记录凶手所有偏执习惯。”
“苏晚，优先采集灶台油脂、残骸表层附着物、地板缝隙血垢，重点筛查烹煮残留成分。”
所有人应声，强压生理不适，踏入屋内开展工作。
唯独沈予安，缓步走入核心现场。
他穿行在满屋腐腥、诡异藏品、死寂血腥之间，步伐平稳、呼吸均匀、眼神沉静。
冷白灯光落在他干净的防护服上，落在他温顺柔和的眉眼间。
他蹲下身，近距离观察每一块被精细切割、脱水、处理的人体组织，指尖悬空比对切割角度、肌理断面、脱水程度。
眼神专业、审慎、平静。
没有一丝恶心、没有一丝抗拒、没有一丝生理波动。
仿佛眼前不是人间至恶的食人凶宅，不是让人全员干呕崩溃的猎奇现场。
只是一场普通、寻常、毫无波澜的常规尸检勘查。
他轻声开口，声音平稳清亮，穿透屋内压抑死寂：
“切割手法精细，刀口统一，肌理剥离极度干净。凶手熟悉人体软组织结构，耐心极强，具备长期精细操作的习惯。”
“脱水、风干、防腐处理手法成熟，不是第一次做。”
“这不是初犯激情作案，是长期隐秘、循序渐进、多次实施同类犯罪的惯犯。”
一句话，让在场所有人心里彻底一沉。
不是个案。
是连环隐案。
陆峥心头猛地一紧：“排查安安市近三年失踪人口，重点排查独居青年、短期租住、社交透明人群！”
“立刻联动南城、周边两市，筛查同类隐秘失踪案！”
屋内众人瞬间提速，压抑的反胃、恐惧，被更沉重的警情压迫下去。
en: Three marked vehicles from Nancheng’s Criminal Investigation Detachment left the municipal bureau compound, their sirens restrained, and headed straight for the expressway.
Late-autumn wind struck the windows, bitterly cold. Neon lights streamed past. The grim files they had just put away, the brief warmth of a case completed—all of it gave way to a fresh tension.

Under the two cities’ joint policing arrangements, Nancheng’s Major Crime Team One, the region’s specialist response team, was required to provide immediate cross-city assistance in major homicides involving unusual methods or severe psychological disturbance.
An’an was a forty-minute drive from Nancheng. Not far, yet the two jurisdictions differed sharply in their public-order problems, patterns of crime, and pace of investigation.

Nancheng had its neighborhood disputes, debt-related revenge killings, and violent dismemberments. An’an had densely packed older districts, a varied transient population, and many people living alone. Extreme killings involving suspected cannibalism were rare.
Inside the team’s vehicle, the atmosphere was oppressive.

Lu Zheng drove the lead car in silence, his expression grim. A homicide assistance request across city boundaries meant more procedure and more complicated coordination than a local investigation. And the preliminary notice—“highly unusual scene; retention and accumulation of human tissue”—already suggested something far more disturbing than an ordinary dismemberment case.
In the passenger seat, Xu Yan reviewed all the preliminary material An’an had sent. His fingers moved quickly over the screen as he summarized it in a low voice.

“Location: the old Jian’an residential compound in An’an’s western district. Built more than twenty years ago. Limited property management. Most corridor cameras are broken. Mainly tenants; neighbors don’t know one another well.”

“Reason for the call: a strong smell of decomposition from a third-floor apartment for the past week. Neighbors initially assumed a dead rat or rotting rubbish. They knocked several times and got no answer. Tonight the smell spread through the entire corridor. Residents panicked and called police.”
“Fire personnel forced entry. They immediately identified the smell as human decomposition, sealed the scene, and reported to the municipal bureau. The cross-city assistance request followed.”
In the back, Jiang Chi sat by the window, frowning. His fingers moved absently over his wrist.

He had worked countless bloody scenes: dismemberments, decomposed bodies dumped in remote hills. But deliberate accumulation of human tissue and suspected cannibalism remained among the cases every investigator found hardest to stomach.

“Cannibalism cases do the worst damage to your head,” he said quietly. “An ordinary killer wants money or revenge. There’s a trail, a motive you can get hold of. Someone like this kills to satisfy a twisted appetite. No logic. No limits.”
Beside him, Su Wan opened her portable evidence system and checked the microscope and trace-collection equipment. Her face was tense. Her fingers had grown slightly stiff.
Years in the laboratory had accustomed her to blood, severed remains, and decomposing samples. But a lab meant isolated material in a controlled environment.
An enclosed living space, human tissue stored over time, someone keeping remains as part of domestic life—that was an entirely different kind of horror.
In the last row, Shen Yu’an sat upright and at ease.

His forensic case rested at his feet. He had already sorted the dissection instruments, sample tubes, preservation reagents, and evidence swabs. His movements were precise and steady, his breathing even. Nothing in his face suggested the scene they were approaching troubled him.
Listening to the others, he added only a quiet observation, objective and gentle.

“In cases involving this kind of psychological distortion, the offender turns the scene into a ‘safe space.’ There tend to be many traces and very strong personal fixations. That can make individual characteristics easier to identify.”
The police vehicles sped along the clear expressway. Forty minutes later, they entered An’an’s western district.
Local officers had already set up a double cordon around the old Jian’an compound.

Bystanders had been cleared from the entire street. Fire engines, local patrol cars, and An’an municipal criminal investigation vehicles stood at the intersection. Their red and blue lights crossed and flashed over the drab residential buildings, leaving them alternately bright and dark. The street felt ominous and airless.
This was nothing like the open desolation of the body dump at Nancheng’s construction site. Here, the scene was inside an apartment in a residential neighborhood.
A home where someone lived, slept, cooked, and went about daily life had become a place for grotesque crime and the storage of decaying human remains.
Even at the street entrance, the night wind carried a thick, foul smell that turned the stomach.
It was different from ordinary decomposition.
Ordinary decomposition smelled of decay and death.
This mingled rancid fat, fermenting flesh, the stale heat of a sealed room, and traces of everyday cooking. It clung to the nose and coated the throat, provoking an immediate wave of nausea.
Lu Zheng led the team out of the car.
Li Jianjun, deputy head of An’an’s Criminal Investigation Detachment, came forward at once. His face was tired and grave. He still looked faintly sick.

“Team Leader Lu. Thank you for coming out tonight.” His voice was rough. “I’ve worked criminal investigation for over twenty years, and I’ve never seen a scene like this. Four of our younger officers took one look after the door came down and ended up vomiting in the corridor.”
