He stepped aside. “Prepare yourselves. It’s worse than you’re imagining.”
Lu Zheng shook his hand and nodded. “Give us the essentials.”
“Have you identified the occupant?”

“Yes,” Li Jianjun said. “Lin Shen. Male, twenty-nine. No regular occupation. Has lived alone for a long time. Few apparent social ties; none of the neighbors knows him. He rented the place three months ago. Keeps to himself, hardly goes out.”
“We’ve found large quantities of fragmented soft tissue, human remains deliberately cut and retained, and what appear to be traces of cooking.”
Behind Lu Zheng, Su Wan’s breath caught.
Jiang Chi went a little pale and swallowed hard.
Cooked. Kept.
Those words placed the case squarely in the territory of extreme cannibalistic crime.
Xu Yan’s pen stopped. His eyes darkened.
The two young An’an officers helping with the briefing looked ill simply hearing the details repeated. Neither had recovered from what they had seen.
Only Shen Yu’an’s expression remained unchanged.

He put on a disposable medical mask and two pairs of protective gloves, then fastened his collar. Beside him, a pale An’an probationary officer stood rigidly. Shen Yu’an spoke softly. “Hold your breath for a moment. Don’t take great gulps of air. Drawing in too much of the smell will make your stomach worse. If you can’t manage, step outside the cordon.”
His voice was gentle, his concern attentive.

The young officer looked up at the Nancheng forensic physician whose reputation was so widely known online, and managed a nod. “Thank you, Dr. Shen… I’ve never seen anything like this. I’m finding it hard.”
“That’s normal,” Shen Yu’an reassured him. “Anyone would feel physically ill the first time they encountered a scene like this. Don’t force yourself.”
With the briefing complete, the two teams entered together.
The stairwell was old and narrow, its plaster peeling. A faulty incandescent bulb buzzed and flickered overhead.
The closer they came to the third floor, the heavier the smell grew. It pressed against the chest, thick and suffocating.
At the turn between the second and third floors, Su Wan was the first to falter.
Years in a sterile laboratory had left her acutely sensitive to unusual odors. The fermented stench filled her airways, and her stomach lurched.
She stopped, bent over with both hands on her knees, and fought the nausea rising in her throat. Her pale face took on a sickly tinge.
“All right?” Jiang Chi caught her arm. He was frowning too, struggling with his own nausea. “Go downstairs if you need to.”
“No.” Su Wan shook her head through clenched teeth. She drew a breath to suppress the retching. Her voice trembled. “I can manage. We need to secure the evidence immediately.”
By the time Xu Yan reached the third-floor landing, his temples were pounding.

He specialized in profiling and had read countless files on disturbed offenders. But reading about a home used to store human remains for cannibalism was nothing like standing in one. His scalp prickled, his mouth was dry and bitter, and waves of nausea and palpitations rose through him.
At the front, Lu Zheng stood with his back and shoulders rigid.
He had the strongest nerves on the team and could still control his physical reaction. But his eyes were grave, his brow tightly drawn. His chest felt constricted.
All along the corridor, everyone except Shen Yu’an was fighting the body's response to the scene: nausea, retching, a racing heart, skin crawling.
No one could face this and remain entirely at ease.
Except him.
The door to Apartment 302 stood wide open.
Inside was darkness, pierced only by the portable examination lights set up by the investigators. Their cold beams revealed a home that defied comprehension.
It was an ordinary small apartment: living room, bedroom, kitchen, balcony. A simple, orderly layout that should have made a modest home for one person.
Now the place was a scene of ruin. The smell of blood and decomposition struck them with suffocating force.
The floor had been washed repeatedly, but dark red stains remained in the seams and the corners along the walls.
On the living-room coffee table and shelving stood neatly arranged pieces of human soft tissue, carefully cut, dehydrated, and preserved.
This was not a body hacked apart and discarded in panic.
The pieces had been sorted, stored, and kept.
Some showed clear shrinkage and hardening from roasting or boiling.
On the stove, worktop, and sink remained broad traces of blood and grease that repeated washing had failed to remove.
What chilled them most was this:
The apartment was unnaturally clean.
Apart from the deliberately retained remains, there was no excess blood, no disorder from a struggle, no scattered belongings.
The offender had been calm, meticulous, patient. The crime scene had been put in order, leaving only the “collection” he wished to treasure.
A gagging sound broke the silence.
Behind them, a young An’an officer could bear no more. He rushed to the corridor window and doubled over, retching so violently that his whole body shook.
An older officer stood deathly pale, his jaw clenched, unable to keep looking into the room.
At the doorway, Jiang Chi glanced across the neatly arranged pieces. His stomach cramped. He turned away at once and forced himself to stay calm, but his fingers tightened involuntarily.
“A classic fetish-driven cannibalistic offense.”
Xu Yan suppressed the cold dread and physical sickness. His voice was slightly hoarse as he began a preliminary profile.

“The offender is extremely disciplined, obsessively clean, fixated, and controlling. This isn’t about money, revenge, or an impulsive release of anger. It serves a longstanding, distorted psychological desire.”
“Keeping, processing, arranging. That’s his ritual.”
Lu Zheng raised a hand, steadied himself, and gave the orders.
“Full protective equipment. Divide the scene into sections.”
“Jiang Chi, take a team. Secure the stairwell. Check movements in and out of the building and establish the residents’ routines.”
“Xu Yan, build a profile from the behavioral traces. Record every sign of the offender’s fixations.”
“Su Wan, start with grease from the stove, deposits on the remains, and blood residue in the floor seams. Focus on identifying cooking residues.”
They answered and went inside, forcing down their nausea to begin work.
Shen Yu’an alone walked slowly into the center of the scene.
Through the stench, the grotesque collection, the stillness and blood, his steps remained even. His breathing was steady. His eyes were calm.
Cold white light fell across his clean protective suit and his mild, gentle face.
He crouched to examine each carefully cut, dehydrated, treated piece of human tissue. His fingers hovered as he compared cutting angles, tissue surfaces, and the degree of dehydration.
His gaze was professional, cautious, composed.
Not a trace of nausea. Not a moment’s resistance. No physical disturbance at all.
As though this were not a home of cannibalistic horror, a scene that drove everyone else to retching and near collapse.
Only an ordinary, uneventful forensic examination.
He spoke softly, his clear, steady voice carrying through the oppressive silence.

“The cuts are precise and consistent. The tissue has been separated very cleanly. The offender knows the structure of human soft tissue, has considerable patience, and is accustomed to sustained, delicate work.”
“The dehydration, air-drying, and preservation methods are practiced. This isn’t the first time.”

“This is no first offense committed in the heat of the moment. We’re dealing with a repeat offender who has been working in secret, developing the method over time and committing similar crimes again and again.”
The words sank heavily into everyone in the room.
Not an isolated case.
A hidden series.

Lu Zheng felt a sharp tightening in his chest. “Check An’an’s missing-person reports for the past three years. Prioritize young people living alone, short-term tenants, and those with few social ties.”
“Coordinate with Nancheng and the two surrounding cities immediately. Look for similar disappearances that have gone unnoticed.”
Work inside the apartment accelerated. The nausea and fear were pushed down beneath the weight of something more urgent.

alt.en: Investigators and a forensic physician approach a cordoned-off apartment building in Jian’an at night.
alt.zh: 夜晚，刑侦队员与法医走向建安小区拉起警戒线的老旧居民楼。

zh: 密闭的三十平米小户型，空气像是凝固了一般。
腐腥混杂着肉质发酵、油烟残留、长期密闭霉气的味道层层堆叠，死死裹在每一个角落。临时架设的冷光源探照灯光束笔直落下，将屋内所有细节照得纤毫毕现，也将这片人间炼狱的诡异与扭曲，毫无保留地暴露在所有人眼前。
楼道口，两名安市市局的年轻辅警扶着墙，还在压抑地干呕。
他们入警时间短，平时处理的大多是纠纷、盗窃、普通治安警情，从未直面过这种带有极端私人仪式感的变态凶案。胸腔翻涌的恶心感压不住，脸色惨白如纸，连指尖都在微微发颤。
支队副队长李建军守在楼道中段，眉头死死拧着，眼底布满血丝。他抬手按住耳麦，低声和指挥中心同步现场初步情况，嗓音带着压抑的沙哑。
“对，初步判定非普通凶杀。现场存在大量人工精细处理的人体组织留存，疑似长期、多次、隐秘作案。请求失踪人口档案加急调档，重点筛查近一年安安市无迹可寻的独居失联人员。”
挂断通讯，他转头看向屋内正在勘查的南城重案组，心底满是佩服。
同样面对这场极致冲击的现场，他手下大半队员已经彻底心态崩盘，唯独这支跨市支援的队伍，即便人人面露不适，依旧稳稳守住各自岗位，没有一人擅自懈怠、退缩。
屋内勘查工作，正式分区铺开。
陆峥踩着无菌鞋套，站在客厅中央位置，目光缓缓扫过全屋，将整体布局、物品摆放、痕迹分布尽收眼底。
常年侦办重案的直觉，让他心底的沉重不断叠加。
普通凶手作案后，第一反应是慌乱、掩盖、逃离，现场大多凌乱、仓促、漏洞百出。
但这套房子，干净得太过反常。
地面瓷砖缝隙被反复刷洗过，水渍干涸的纹路规整划一，墙角、踢脚线、家具底部，没有散落的血迹碎渣，没有搏斗拖拽的凌乱痕迹。所有不该留存的痕迹，被彻底清理干净。
唯独凶手刻意珍藏、留存、加工过的人体组织，被分门别类，整齐摆放在透明保鲜盒、陶瓷浅盘、干燥托盘之中。
分门别类，条理清晰。
苏晚带着随身化验设备，蹲在厨房料理台前，强压着喉咙口不断翻涌的恶心，专注采集样本。
她戴着双层防护口罩与防毒过滤棉，依旧挡不住那股黏腻入骨的腐腥。鼻尖、喉咙始终萦绕着发酵肉质的怪异气味，脑袋一阵阵发沉，胃里反反复复痉挛抽搐。
她抬手稳住微微发颤的手腕，用无菌棉签仔细刮取料理台缝隙的残留油脂，装入采样管，低声报出数据：
“灶台台面残留多层油脂叠加痕迹，新旧覆盖。表层是普通家用食用油残留，底层固化油脂，含有人体皮下脂肪高温熬制后的特异性成分，成分占比高度吻合。”
“洗菜池下水口滤网残留微量骨粉碎屑、肌肉纤维残渣，确认为人骨及人体软组织残留。”
身旁跟着协助采样的安市化验科技术员，听完汇报后，喉结狠狠滚动了两下，下意识别开视线，不敢再看操作台一眼，低声感慨：
“太冷静了……这人做完这些事，居然还能认认真真擦洗灶台，规整物品，完全像是在处理日常食材。”
这句话，让在场所有人心底发凉。
這種惡像是一個人的常态、习慣。
江驰带着两名外勤警员，对全屋门窗、锁具、阳台防护、楼道出入口痕迹进行全面排查。
他逐一检查窗户锁扣、防盗网焊点、门锁锁芯磨损痕迹，指尖抚过冰冷的金属，神色愈发凝重。
“门窗完好，锁具无撬动、无技术开锁痕迹。”
“阳台防盗网没有攀爬摩擦痕，楼道监控长期损坏，无外来人员闯入记录。”
他站直身体，转头向陆峥汇报：“大概率是熟人、或者是受害者自愿入户。凶手无暴力闯入行为，作案全程隐秘、平和，毫无外力冲突痕迹。”
两名年轻外勤警员站在身后，视线扫过置物架上整齐摆放的残块，头皮一阵发麻，其中一人忍不住低声发问：“驰哥，这人……到底杀了多少人？”
江驰沉默两秒，没有回答。
这个问题，没人敢轻易定论。
许砚坐在客厅边缘的折叠勘查凳上，平板屏幕亮得刺眼，上面密密麻麻记录着凶手的全部行为特征。他强压着生理性的心悸与反胃，指尖飞速滑动，完善初步心理侧写。
空气里持续不散的腐腥，让他太阳穴突突直跳，大脑始终处于一种紧绷的眩晕感中，但思维依旧保持极致缜密。
“凶手，男性，年龄二十五至三十五岁。”
“独居，长期独处，社交完全封闭，无亲友往来，无社会羁绊，在所有人眼中是‘透明人’。”
“极度洁癖，强迫症严重，控制欲极端，做事条理极强，具备精细手工、耐心处理、长期独处操作的生活习惯。”
“心理彻底畸变，漠视人命，将猎杀、处理、留存人体组织当成私人仪式、精神寄托，无负罪感，无恐惧心理。”
“作案极度隐秘，擅长隐藏自身，日常外表普通、温和、无害，完全不会引起周遭任何人警惕。”
写到最后，许砚笔尖微微一顿。
这类凶手，是所有连环凶手里最难抓的一类。
他们不张扬、不泄愤、不挑衅警方，安静地藏在市井烟火里，日复一日，完成自己扭曲的私人癖好。
与此同时，房间最内侧的卧室，沈予安正在做核心痕迹与组织断面的最终核验。
卧室比客厅更加干净。
一张单人床，被褥叠得整整齐齐，床单平整无褶皱，床头柜摆放着简单的水杯、书籍、香薰摆件，完全是普通独居青年的干净卧室。
唯独床头柜的封闭式收纳盒内，分层摆放着数块脱水风干后的人体软骨组织，断面平整，剥离得极度干净。
沈予安半蹲在收纳盒前，手持便携式放大窥镜，逐一观察每一处切割纹理、剥离角度、脱水痕迹。
他动作轻柔、规整、不急不缓，每一次观察、每一次比对、每一次记录，都精准到位。
屋内其余人时不时需要停顿、深呼吸、转移视线来缓解生理不适，唯独他始终状态平稳，节奏稳定，没有丝毫被周遭血腥诡异的环境干扰。
他低头记录数据，声音清亮平稳，供所有人听清：
“所有软组织切割角度统一，刀口深度、间距误差极小，工具单一，为固定精细窄刃刀具。”
“软组织剥离极度干净，无多余筋膜残留，凶手对人体肌肉、脂肪、软骨结构认知清晰，远超普通常识层面。”
“脱水、风干、低温留存手法成熟，循序渐进，每一块留存组织的处理工序完全一致，标准化程度极高，不像临时摸索、首次作案。”
他抬手，轻轻触碰收纳盒边缘的细微磨损痕迹：
“收纳盒长期高频使用，分层摆放、分类留存，具备长期收藏、定期整理的习惯。结合厨房多层叠加的熬制残留，可以确定，至少三至五名受害者，在此屋内遇害、被处理留存。”
三至五人。
这个数字落下的瞬间，楼道内外一片死寂。
原本只是一桩猎奇命案，此刻彻底升级为跨时长、隐案多、极具迷惑性的连环变态杀人案。
陆峥立刻抬手对讲机下令：“立刻联动安安市局指挥中心！彻查近二十四个月，全市所有失联、失踪、主动销户、长期杳无音信的独居人口！重点排查租房青年、自由职业、无社交人群！”
“通知户籍科、社区网格中心、街道办，全员联动摸排！”
指令层层下达，屋外警笛、对讲电流、紧急通话声瞬间交织在一起，原本压抑的深夜，彻底进入全城紧急侦办状态。
李建军快步走入屋内，脸色凝重至极：“陆队，我们刚刚翻查档案，发现一个致命疑点。”
“近一年，安安市西城区、老城区，一共七名独居年轻人失联。全部无打斗报案、无绑架勒索、无纠纷前科，失踪得干干净净，被系统归类为自愿离开、外出务工、失联待定，全部没有立案侦查。”
七人。
所有人心脏重重一沉。
七起被忽略的隐秘失踪，对应屋内至少三至五名受害者的痕迹。
足以印证，凶手在这片老城区，已经悄无声息地猎杀了整整一年以上。
“受害者身份完全无法对应。”许砚抬起头，语气凝重，“尸体主体、头颅、躯干全部被彻底处理、销毁、转移，只留下这些无特征、无DNA快速匹配的细碎组织。凶手刻意抹去了所有受害者的身份信息。”
苏晚刚好完成第一轮全面采样，起身摘掉半湿的口罩，脸色依旧泛白，声音带着一丝疲惫的沙哑：
“我这边确认，现场没有任何受害者私人物品。衣物、手机、证件、饰品，全部被彻底清空，屋内除了户主林深的生活用品，没有第二个人的物件留存。”
江驰沉声接话：“楼道、垃圾桶、小区绿化带、垃圾中转站，我已经安排队员全面排查，暂时没有发现丢弃的衣物、遗体残骸。凶手处理痕迹的完整度，远超普通刑侦认知。”
多条线索汇总，案件的诡异程度持续升级。
户主林深是凶手還是受害者的一員？
深夜十一点五十分。
安安市局技术科、网安科、户籍科的增援人员全部抵达现场，大批量卷宗、失踪人口名单、社区网格记录被临时搬运到楼道平台，十几名警员就地铺开，分组筛查、比对、统计。
整个楼道灯火通明，数十名警务人员分工协作，有人筛查档案、有人统计数据、有人复盘轨迹、有人持续勘查现场。
年轻警员的压抑干呕渐渐平息，取而代之的是满场紧绷、严肃、高速运转的办案氛围。
许砚带着两名文职警员，逐行比对七名失联人员的年龄、身高、职业、居住习惯、社交轨迹，试图从海量琐碎信息里找出与林深、与这间凶宅契合的关联点。
“七人，年龄区间二十二至三十岁。”
“全部独居、全部无固定工作、全部社交极简、全部很少与邻里往来。”
“其中四人，曾在失联前三个月内，有同城租房置换、短期租住、临时搬家记录。”
线索渐渐收拢，指向一个清晰的猎杀模式。
凶手针对性极强，专门挑选独居、无牵挂、无人惦记、消失了也不会有人追问的年轻人下手。
这类人群失踪，自带“自愿离开”的完美伪装，是最完美的猎杀目标。
陆峥听完汇总，眼神彻底冷沉：“锁定凶手作案模式。看看是不是利用同城租房、邻里互动、同城社交的普通身份接近受害者，以合租、转租、借用物品、邻里帮忙为借口，诱骗入户，隐秘作案。”
案情推演至此，所有人终于明白，为什么这起连环凶案，能隐藏整整一年不为人知。
与此同时，卧室之内。
沈予安完成全部组织痕迹初勘，整理好手中的记录平板，起身走出卧室。
他穿过依旧弥漫腐腥的客厅，走到陆峥身侧，轻声汇报完整法医初勘结论：
“现场留存的所有人体组织，最少来自三名不同个体，骨质密度、软组织肌理、脂肪层厚度存在明显个体差异。”
“所有被害者，死亡时间跨度极大，最早可追溯至十四个月前，最近一起死亡时间，不超过二十天。”
“凶手长期保留、定期整理、持续新增留存组织，作案频率稳定，心态始终平稳，无情绪波动式作案特征。”
他的汇报客观、冷静、精准，没有多余情绪，只有纯粹的专业结论。
陆峥点头：“辛苦你了，沈法医。后续尸体溯源、身份比对，还要靠你这边重点支撑。”
“应该的。”沈予安微微颔首。
楼道夜风从敞开的窗户灌入，稍稍冲淡了屋内黏腻的腐腥。
屋外城市深夜依旧灯火零星，老旧小区住户早已沉睡。
抓捕、溯源、匹配受害者、串联隐案，成为眼下唯一的重中之重。
没人松懈，没人喘息，全员沉浸在紧张的破案节奏里。
新一轮的追捕，正式全面铺开。
en: The air in the sealed thirty-square-meter apartment seemed to have congealed.

Decomposition, fermenting flesh, cooking grease, and the moldy closeness of a room shut for too long lay in suffocating layers in every corner. Portable examination lamps cast hard, cold beams through the space, exposing every detail—and every distortion of this private hell.
At the entrance to the corridor, two young auxiliary officers from An’an’s municipal bureau leaned against the wall, still trying to suppress their retching.

They had not been in the service long. Most of their work had involved disputes, theft, and ordinary public-order incidents. They had never confronted a killing marked by such extreme personal ritual. Nausea surged through their chests. Their faces were paper-white, even their fingertips trembling.

Deputy Detachment Head Li Jianjun stood midway along the corridor, his brow knotted and his eyes bloodshot. Pressing a hand to his earpiece, he quietly relayed the initial findings to the command center. His voice was strained and rough.

“Yes. Preliminary assessment: not an ordinary homicide. Large quantities of human tissue have been carefully processed and retained. We suspect repeated offenses over an extended period, committed in secret. Expedite the missing-person files. Prioritize people living alone who disappeared without a trace in An’an over the past year.”
He ended the call and looked toward the Nancheng team at work inside, filled with respect.

More than half his own officers had been overwhelmed by the scene. Yet this team, brought in from another city, held their positions. Their discomfort was obvious, but not one had neglected a task or backed away.
Inside, the examination was now proceeding section by section.

Wearing sterile shoe covers, Lu Zheng stood in the middle of the living room. His gaze moved slowly around the apartment, taking in its layout, the arrangement of objects, and the distribution of traces.
Instinct honed over years of major investigations deepened his unease.
After killing, an ordinary offender’s first responses were panic, concealment, flight. The scene was usually disordered, hurried, full of mistakes.
This apartment was far too clean.

The grout between the floor tiles had been scrubbed repeatedly. Dried water marks followed orderly, uniform patterns. In the corners, along the skirting, and beneath the furniture, there were no scattered blood traces or fragments, no disarray from struggling or dragging. Every trace the offender did not want had been removed.
Only the human tissue he had deliberately processed and kept remained, sorted into clear food-storage boxes, shallow ceramic dishes, and drying trays.
Categorized. Methodical.
With her portable testing equipment beside her, Su Wan crouched at the kitchen worktop, concentrating on sample collection while fighting the nausea rising in her throat.

Even two protective masks and filtering material could not keep out the clinging stench. The strange smell of fermenting flesh lingered in her nose and throat. Her head felt heavy; her stomach cramped again and again.
She steadied her trembling wrist and carefully scraped residual grease from a seam with a sterile swab. Placing it in a sample tube, she reported quietly.

“Several overlapping layers of grease on the stovetop, newer deposits over older ones. Ordinary cooking oil on the surface. The hardened lower layer contains components characteristic of human subcutaneous fat subjected to high heat. The proportions are a close match.”
“The sink strainer contains traces of bone powder and muscle fibers. Confirmed human bone and soft tissue.”
The An’an laboratory technician helping her swallowed twice. He looked away, unable to face the worktop again, and spoke under his breath.
“So calm… After doing all this, he still scrubbed the stove and put everything away. As though he were handling ordinary ingredients.”
The remark chilled everyone who heard it.
This evil seemed to be someone’s normality. A habit.
Jiang Chi and two field officers inspected the doors, windows, locks, balcony security fittings, and traces around the corridor entrances.
He checked the window catches, welds in the security bars, and wear inside the door lock one by one. His fingertips passed over cold metal, his expression growing graver.
“Doors and windows intact. No prying or signs of lock picking.”
“No climbing scuffs on the balcony bars. The corridor cameras have been broken for a long time. No recorded intrusion by an outsider.”

He straightened and turned to Lu Zheng. “Most likely someone known to the victims, or the victims entered voluntarily. No forced entry by the offender. Everything was concealed and quiet. No evidence of a violent confrontation.”
Behind him, the two younger officers glanced at the pieces arranged on the shelves. One could not suppress a quiet question. “Jiang Chi… how many people has he killed?”
Jiang Chi was silent for two seconds. He gave no answer.
No one could venture an easy conclusion.

Xu Yan sat on a folding examination stool at the edge of the living room. His tablet shone harshly, crowded with notes on the offender’s behavior. Suppressing his racing heart and nausea, he worked quickly to refine the preliminary profile.
The persistent stench made his temples throb. A tense dizziness pressed on him, but his thinking remained exact.
“Male. Between twenty-five and thirty-five.”
“Lives alone. Spends long periods in isolation. Entirely closed off socially. No visits from family or friends, no social ties. To everyone around him, he is invisible.”

“Extreme concern with cleanliness. Severe compulsive behavior. An intense need for control. Highly methodical, accustomed to delicate manual work, patient processing, and working alone for long periods.”
“Profoundly distorted psychologically. Indifferent to human life. Hunting, processing, and keeping human tissue serve as a private ritual, a source of emotional attachment. No guilt. No fear.”
“Extremely secretive. Skilled at concealment. In daily life, ordinary, mild, harmless-looking. Nothing to put the people around him on their guard.”
At the last point, Xu Yan’s stylus paused.
Among serial offenders, this kind was one of the hardest to catch.
They did not advertise themselves, vent their rage, or taunt the police. They hid quietly in the routines of ordinary life, satisfying their private obsessions day after day.
Meanwhile, in the bedroom at the back of the apartment, Shen Yu’an was completing his examination of the key traces and cut tissue surfaces.
The bedroom was cleaner still.

A single bed, its bedding neatly folded and its sheet without a crease. A plain drinking cup, books, and an aroma ornament on the bedside table. It could have been the tidy room of any young person living alone.
Except for the closed storage box on the bedside table. Inside, layers of dehydrated, air-dried human cartilage lay stacked, the cut surfaces smooth, the tissue stripped clean.
Shen Yu’an crouched in front of it with a portable magnifying viewer, examining each cutting mark, separation angle, and trace of dehydration.
His movements were gentle, orderly, unhurried. Every observation, comparison, and note was precise.
The others periodically had to stop, breathe, or look away to manage their physical distress. He alone maintained the same steady pace, entirely undisturbed by the blood and strangeness around him.
He lowered his head to record the data, speaking clearly enough for everyone to hear.
“The cutting angles are consistent across the soft tissue. Very little variation in depth or spacing. A single type of tool: a fine, narrow blade.”
“The tissue has been separated very cleanly, without excess fascia remaining. The offender’s understanding of muscle, fat, and cartilage is well beyond ordinary knowledge.”

“The dehydration, air-drying, and low-temperature storage are practiced and systematic. Each piece has undergone the same sequence of treatment. Highly standardized. This does not look like someone improvising or offending for the first time.”
He raised a hand and lightly touched the minute wear marks along the edge of the box.

“The container has seen frequent use over a long period. Layered storage, separate categories. A habit of collecting and regular sorting. Combined with the overlapping cooking residues in the kitchen, we can establish that at least three to five victims were killed here, processed, and retained.”
Three to five people.
Silence fell inside the apartment and along the corridor.
What had begun as a bizarre homicide had become a deeply concealed serial murder investigation, extending over time and across multiple hidden cases.

Lu Zheng lifted his radio immediately. “Coordinate with An’an’s command center. Check every person living alone who has been out of contact, reported missing, voluntarily deregistered, or unheard from for a prolonged period over the past twenty-four months. Prioritize young tenants, freelance workers, and people with few social connections.”
“Bring in household registration, the community grid centers, and the subdistrict offices. A coordinated canvass by all of them.”
The orders traveled outward. Sirens, radio static, and urgent calls overlapped beyond the apartment. The oppressive night became a citywide emergency investigation.
Li Jianjun hurried inside, his face grave. “Team Leader Lu. We’ve just reviewed the files. There’s a critical point.”

“In the past year, seven young people living alone have disappeared in An’an’s western and old-city districts. No reported fights, no abduction demands, no recorded disputes. They vanished cleanly. The system classified them as having left voluntarily, gone away for work, or lost contact under undetermined circumstances. None was opened as a criminal investigation.”
Seven.
The number landed heavily.
Seven overlooked disappearances. Traces of at least three to five victims in the apartment.
Enough to indicate that the offender had been hunting unnoticed in this old district for more than a year.

“We can’t match the victims’ identities at all,” Xu Yan said, looking up. “The main remains, heads, and torsos have been processed, destroyed, or moved. All that’s left is fragmented tissue without identifying features or an immediate DNA match. The offender has deliberately erased their identities.”
Su Wan had just completed the first full round of sampling. She stood and removed her damp mask. Her face was still pale; fatigue roughened her voice.

“I can confirm there are no victims’ belongings here. Clothes, phones, identification, jewelry—all cleared out. Apart from Lin Shen’s everyday possessions, there’s nothing belonging to a second person.”

Jiang Chi spoke in a low voice. “I’ve assigned officers to check the corridors, bins, planted areas, and waste-transfer station. So far, no discarded clothing or remains. The completeness of the cleanup goes far beyond what we normally encounter.”
As the findings came together, the case grew stranger.
Was Lin Shen, the occupant, the killer—or one of the victims?

Reinforcements from An’an’s technical section, cyber police section, and household registration section had all arrived. Stacks of case files, missing-person lists, and community grid records were brought to the landing. More than a dozen officers spread out in groups to screen, compare, and collate them.
The entire stairwell was brightly lit. Dozens of police personnel worked together: checking records, compiling data, reconstructing movements, continuing the scene examination.
The younger officers’ suppressed retching gradually subsided. In its place came a tense, serious rhythm of concentrated work.

With two administrative officers, Xu Yan compared the seven missing people’s ages, heights, occupations, living habits, and social movements line by line. Somewhere in the mass of minor details, they needed a connection to Lin Shen and this apartment.
“Seven people. Ages twenty-two to thirty.”
“All lived alone. None had regular employment. All had minimal social contact and little interaction with neighbors.”
“Four had records of changing rentals within the city, short-term accommodation, or temporary moves during the three months before they disappeared.”
The findings began to converge on a clear pattern.
The offender chose his targets carefully: young people living alone, with few attachments, no one waiting for them, no one likely to ask questions if they vanished.
Their circumstances supplied a ready explanation for disappearance: they had chosen to leave. It made them ideal targets.

Lu Zheng’s eyes hardened as he listened. “Establish the approach. Check whether he used an ordinary identity through local rental listings, neighborhood contact, or local social networks. Shared accommodation, subletting, borrowing something, helping a neighbor—any pretext to draw them inside and act unseen.”
At last, the team understood how a series of killings could remain hidden for an entire year.
Meanwhile, in the bedroom,
Shen Yu’an finished the preliminary examination of the tissue traces, organized his notes on the tablet, and stood.
He crossed the living room, still thick with the smell of decay, and came to Lu Zheng’s side to give the full preliminary forensic findings.
“The retained human tissue comes from at least three different individuals. There are clear differences in bone density, soft-tissue structure, and the thickness of fat layers.”
“The times of death span a considerable period. The earliest dates back fourteen months. The most recent is no more than twenty days ago.”

“The offender keeps the tissue over time, sorts it regularly, and continues adding to it. The frequency is steady. His state of mind appears consistently stable, without signs of offending driven by emotional fluctuations.”
His report was objective, calm, exact. No excess emotion. Only professional conclusions.
Lu Zheng nodded. “Thank you, Dr. Shen. We’ll be relying heavily on you to trace the remains and establish identities.”
“Of course.” Shen Yu’an inclined his head.
Night air entered through the open corridor windows, thinning the apartment’s clinging stench a little.
Outside, scattered lights still burned across the city. The residents of the old compound had long since gone to sleep.
Finding the offender, tracing the remains, identifying the victims, and connecting the hidden cases were now the sole priorities.
No one relaxed. No one paused for breath. Everyone was absorbed in the urgent pace of the investigation.
The next phase of the hunt had begun in full.

alt.en: Investigators compare missing-person files at a temporary station in the apartment stairwell.
alt.zh: 刑侦队员在居民楼楼道的临时办案点核对失踪人口档案。

zh: 安安市公安局指挥中心大楼灯火通明，整栋指挥枢纽进入一级紧急侦办状态。
不同于深夜零星的治安调度，今晚整层大厅坐满了值班警员、情报研判员、网安技术人员、户籍筛查专员。数十台电脑屏幕同时亮起，数据流、人口档案、轨迹监控、社区台账密密麻麻铺满墙面巨屏。
建安小区食人连环案的定性升级通知，正式下发所有联动单位。
非单一命案、非临时激情犯罪。
确诊长期隐秘连环杀人、涉嫌十余起人口失踪、恶性猎奇变态作案。
市局一把手亲自督办，分管刑侦副局长坐镇指挥中心，跨区调度、全城布控、人口溯源、轨迹抓捕四组同时启动。
南城重案组全员留守案发现场，配合安市本地警力，双线同步推进。
三楼302凶宅的封锁范围再次扩大，从原本的单户房门封锁，延伸至整层楼道、整栋单元楼出入口。辖区消防、刑事技术二次勘查组、痕迹复勘人员分批进场，进行第二轮、第三轮精细化搜证。
越是深挖，现场透出的寒意越是刺骨。
第一轮勘查只是肉眼可见的诡异与血腥。
第二轮精细化物证筛查，开始挖出凶手藏在细节里的、长达一年多的连环罪证。
苏晚带着两队技术人员，对全屋进行毫米级痕迹复勘。
经过整整两个小时的适应，鼻腔喉咙的生理性反胃依旧存在，却已经能被职业素养强行压制。她戴着全新的防毒级防护面罩，手持高倍冷光勘查灯，一寸寸扫过墙面、吊顶缝隙、地板拼接纹路、家具死角。
“吊顶夹缝发现密封式黑色收纳袋。”
苏晚的声音透过对讲机平稳传出，带着长期专注的沉静。
“内含多层塑封包裹的人体牙齿、指骨碎节、指甲角质留存，独立分装，按大小排序摆放。”
旁边协助勘查的安市技术科老技术员，闻言指尖微微一顿，沉沉吐出一口气：“收藏癖，极致的仪式感留存。这类连环变态，每一名受害者都会留下专属‘纪念品’。”
拆开逐层塑封，里面的细小人体部件干净得吓人。
没有腐臭、没有血污，经过彻底脱脂、风干、防腐、密封处理，保存得完好无损。每一袋部件规格统一、摆放整齐，甚至在外层塑封上，用极细的黑色水笔，标注着肉眼几乎难以分辨的日期编号。
不是胡乱收藏。
是按猎杀顺序、作案时间，逐一归档。
沈予安蹲在吊顶下方，手持放大镜逐一对部件骨质、齿体发育程度做区分核验。
屋内依旧压抑阴森，其余警员哪怕已经适应现场，动作依旧谨慎紧绷，下意识避开那些细碎可怖的藏品。只有他姿态松弛平稳，视线专注落在物证之上，逐一分类记录。
“目前初步区分，这批留存部件，至少对应十一名不同个体。”
一句话落地，整个楼道瞬间陷入死寂。
十一人。
之前预判的三到五人，被直接翻倍突破。
整整十一条人命，悄无声息葬送在这间不足三十平米的小屋里，被凶手以最扭曲、最隐秘的方式，珍藏、归档、留存。无数个日夜，楼下居民正常起居、楼上邻里正常作息、整栋楼烟火如常。
无人知晓，头顶方寸之地，藏着堆积累累的白骨冤魂。
陆峥站在客厅中央，听完数据汇报，眼底彻底覆上一层寒霜。
从业十几年，他经手的重案、连环案、碎尸案不计其数，但如此隐秘、如此漫长、如此大批量、且完全脱离社会视线的连环猎杀，极其罕见。
“立刻更新案情定性。”陆峥对着对讲机沉声下令，“受害者数量修正为十人以上，正式挂牌特级督办连环变态杀人案。”
“所有警力，全员提速！”
楼下，江驰早已带队铺开全域排查网。
他带着南城外勤队员、安市特警机动组、辖区网格员，分成十二支小队，以建安小区为中心，向外辐射三公里全域摸排。
老旧小区巷道错综复杂、私房连片、小巷四通八达，极易逃窜、极易藏匿。
江驰手持手电筒，沿着漆黑巷道快步推进，同时给小队分配任务：
“一组排查小区全部地下室、楼顶夹层、废弃储物间！”
“二组排查周边废弃老房、拆迁滞留空地、无人居住危房！”
“三组卡点所有出城小路、省道辅路、城乡结合部卡口！”
“四组联动交通局，筛查近七日所有出城私家车、网约车、短途客运轨迹！”
指令层层落地，数百警力瞬间铺满整片老城区。
夜色之下，无数手电光束划破黑暗，密集织就成一张抓捕大网，死死罩住整片城区。
与此同时，指挥中心的人口溯源筛查，传来大批量数据反馈。
许砚坐在临时研判席位，面前铺满厚厚的纸质档案与电子台账，数十名文职警员围着他同步整理数据。
之前筛查出的七名失联人员名单，已经全部完成基础信息建档。而随着凶手十一名受害者物证的出现，指挥中心再次扩大筛查年限，将排查范围拉升至二十八个月。
海量失踪、失联、销户、离市名单被批量调出。
“陆队！新增筛查结果！”
一名网安警员快速汇总数据，高声汇报：“二十八个月内，安安市西老城区、城郊结合部，共计十四名适龄独居青年无因失联！全部无纠纷、无报警、无亲友报案、被系统默认自愿迁出！”
十四人。
和法医物证核验的十一名个体高度吻合，剩余三人大概率是早期作案、残骸彻底销毁、无任何留存痕迹。
许砚指尖飞快敲打键盘，将十四人信息逐一建档归类，眼底寒意越来越重。
“凶手的猎杀周期，从两年前就已经开始。”
他快速梳理出完整的凶手作案成长轨迹，对着赶来的陆峥快速汇报：
“早期作案极度谨慎，不留任何藏品、不留任何痕迹，彻底销毁遗体，所以早期几起案件完全隐形。”
“后期心态逐步膨胀、自信爆棚，开始留存纪念品、建立私人归档体系，仪式感越来越重，胆子越来越大，蛰伏周期越来越短。”
“整整两年，十四名年轻人，人间蒸发，无人问津。”
许砚侧头看向窗外漆黑的夜空，语气沉得发冷：“最可怕的是，这些受害者，全部是社会最透明、最无牵挂的群体。”
“孤儿、独居租客、异地务工、无亲无故自由职业、和原生家庭断联的年轻人。”
“他们消失之后，没有家人追问、没有朋友报警、没有邻里留意，天生就是完美的猎杀对象。”
这也是这桩惊天连环大案，能沉默两年不发一案、不破一功的根本原因。
凶手从来不是随机杀人。
他是精准筛选、精准挑选、精准猎杀。
专门挑“消失了也没人在乎”的人下手。
陆峥听完汇报，沉默良久，低声开口：
“查受害者的全部生平。从小到大、求学、务工、社交、病史、前科、租房记录，全部扒干净。我要知道，这个人的深渊，到底是从什么时候开始的。”
“收到！”
户籍科、情报组立刻全速溯源。
凌晨一点，完整人生履历，被层层剥开，赤裸裸铺在众人眼前。
最有可能的人
林深，二十九岁，安安市本地人。
幼年父母离异，双方再婚，彻底弃养，自幼在亲戚家辗转寄居，无固定居所、无亲情羁绊、无任何人真正关照。
少年时期辍学流浪，无学籍、无社交、无同学往来。
成年后打零工、短工、零散务工，频繁换城市、换住所、换行业，征信干净、无违法前科、无打架斗殴、无盗窃诈骗记录。
在所有公开档案里，他是一个干净、透明、毫无存在感的普通人。
可在隐藏的生活轨迹里，他独居、自闭、彻底隔绝社会，不交友、不恋爱、不社交、不参与任何社群活动。
网安队员调出他仅有的网络账号，空白一片，无动态、无关注、无互动，两年内零发言、零浏览痕迹，彻底与世隔绝。
“心理彻底社会化死亡。”许砚看着屏幕资料，精准定论，“他早就不属于社会体系了，他只是披着普通人皮囊，活在人群里的异类。”
资料一页页往下翻，一条不起眼的租房轨迹，突然让所有人眼神一凝。
“发现关键轨迹！”
警员高声汇报：“林深两年前，曾在多个城市短期租住，频繁更换独居出租屋！最早的疑似作案落脚点，在邻市县区！和我们筛查出的第一批早期失联人员时间、地点完全重合！”
跨市、跨区域、流动式猎杀。
案情再次升级。
不止安安市。
跨市连环作案！
两年时间，数市流转，择人而噬，悄无声息收割十几条人命。
屋外，天色依旧沉黑，距离天亮还有四个小时。
全城布控依旧高压运转，所有出城路口、小巷、废弃建筑、无人角落，全部被死死封锁。
可最诡异的一点，始终压在所有人心头。
全城地毯式排查至今，没有林深任何踪迹。
他没有出城记录、没有乘车记录、没有住宿记录、没有消费记录、没有监控抓拍。
仿佛作案曝光之后，整个人凭空蒸发。
江驰从外勤现场赶回楼道，满头薄汗，呼吸微促，脸色凝重：“所有卡点零收获，全域摸排零目击，周边监控全部断层。”
“他太懂监控死角、太懂巡查规律、太懂城市盲区。”
陆峥眼神锐利，快速判断：“他没有逃远。”
“长期独居、长期隐秘作案的人，心态极度保守，不会贸然远距离逃窜。他一定还在老城区范围内，藏在所有人想不到的、绝对安全的盲区里。”
就在所有人全力追踪凶手踪迹、梳理海量受害者信息、承受着十几条人命带来的极致压抑与心理冲击时。
沈予安已经完成了全屋所有人体藏品的初步个体区分、死亡周期排序、作案手法归类。
他将十四名疑似受害者、十一名物证匹配个体，按时间线梳理出完整的猎杀链条，整理成一份条理清晰、逻辑严密、零漏洞的法医技术报告。
身边来回奔走的警员人人神色紧绷、身心压抑、被这场人间炼狱折磨得心神不宁，反复出现胸闷、恶心、失眠前兆的刑侦应激反应。
他收起记录平板，抬头看向满目漆黑的窗外，轻声向陆峥汇报：
“所有物证梳理完毕。”
“凶手手法逐年精进，早期销毁彻底，后期留存成瘾。作案逻辑清晰、心态极度稳定，反侦察能力远超普通变态罪犯。”
“他对这片老城区地形、监控、警力布控规律，了如指掌。”
话音落下，指挥中心巨屏上，最新一条研判数据弹出。
红色加粗字体，刺目惊心。
【研判结论：嫌疑人具备极强蛰伏能力，大概率长期藏匿于无监控、无人流、废弃封闭空间，继续就地藏匿观望，等待警方排查松动、伺机二次逃窜。】
深渊现世。
恶魔，依旧藏在夜色里。
整座城市的抓捕大网，还在持续收紧。
十四桩尘封两年的冤魂，终于迎来被看见、被昭雪的机会。
而这场横跨两年、累及十数条人命的连环食人炼狱，真正的攻坚，才刚刚走到中段。
凌晨一点四十分，安安市老城区彻底沉入深秋最浓重的黑暗里。

连片老旧居民楼遮挡了城市主干道的零星灯火，错综复杂的巷道割裂了规整的城市格局，十年搁置的拆迁废墟盘踞在城区西侧，成为整片繁华都市边缘被彻底遗忘的灰色地带。湿冷的夜风穿透坍塌的墙体缝隙，卷动废墟里干枯的杂草与腐烂碎屑，带着泥土深埋经年的阴冷气息，在空旷无人的片区里来回穿梭。夜色之下，整片废弃拆迁区死寂无声，没有行人过往，没有车辆途经，就连夜间巡防的路灯也尽数损毁熄灭，目之所及尽是幽深厚重的阴影，每一处角落都藏着不为人知的隐秘与晦暗。

建安小区32号302室曝出的连环食人凶案，已经牵动全城警力运转近两个小时。从最初单一室内猎奇命案的定性，到后续物证堆叠爆出十余起隐案，再到法医初步核验锁定多名未知受害者，案情的恶劣程度始终在不断突破所有人的心理底线。市公安局一把手亲自坐镇指挥中心，省厅同步启动重大恶性案件应急预案，跨区域联防机制全面激活，数百名警务人员、特警队员、社区网格员、消防搜救人员、技术勘查人员全员在岗，以案发小区为核心，向外层层辐射铺开地毯式排查，封堵所有出城通路，严控全部城乡盲区，誓要将藏匿在城市阴影中的凶手死死困死在这片老城区之内。
可高强度的全域排查持续至今，嫌疑人林深的踪迹依旧是一片空白。
全城所有监控卡口、道路轨迹、出行记录、消费流水、实名登记信息全部完成多层回溯筛查，无论是二十四小时实时轨迹，还是七日历史数据倒查，亦或是跨月流动人口比对，都没有捕捉到半分凶手逃窜的痕迹。这个人仿佛在案发现场暴露的瞬间，就彻底剥离了自己所有的社会轨迹，凭空消失在密集布控的城区之中，彻底隐匿于层层黑暗之内，不留给警方任何可供追踪的线索。

临时研判中心内，紧张高压的氛围几乎让人窒息。数十台电脑屏幕不间断跳动着海量数据，密密麻麻的人口档案、失踪台账、社区登记信息、区域轨迹图层铺满整面高清巨屏，数十名研判警员、网安技术员、户籍筛查员埋头高速作业，指尖敲击键盘的声响连绵不绝，在寂静的深夜里交织成急促压抑的韵律。所有人双目布满红血丝，身心被持续的高压工作层层透支，却没有一人敢有半分松懈，每一条数据的疏漏，都可能让一桩沉冤彻底石沉大海，让穷凶极恶的凶手再次蛰伏逃窜。

许砚坐在研判区最核心的位置，作为全队唯一的心理侧写与轨迹研判核心早已身心俱疲。连续数个小时不眠不休的高强度分析，让他太阳穴持续胀痛，大脑始终处于紧绷眩晕的状态，鼻腔里依旧残留着凶宅室内挥之不去的腐腥异味，生理性的疲惫与心理层面的压抑双重叠加，不断侵蚀着他的状态。但他依旧死死撑着最后一丝清醒，逐字逐句核对每一名失联人员的档案资料，将二十八个月内老城区所有无因失踪、被动销户、长期失联的人群信息逐一归类建档，不放过任何一处细微的疑点。

经过多轮细化筛查与交叉比对，十四名高度疑似受害者的完整信息，彻底梳理完毕。这些散落市井角落的年轻人，有着高度重合的人生轨迹与生存状态，他们大多出身破碎家庭，自幼缺乏亲友管束与牵挂，成年后独自奔赴异乡谋生，常年独居出租屋，社交圈极度贫瘠，没有稳定的工作与固定的生活圈子，极少与人深交，日常行踪无人关注，生死安危无人挂念。正是这种彻底透明、毫无羁绊的生存状态，让他们成为了凶手精准锁定的猎杀目标，悄无声息消失在人间之后，没有家人报案追问，没有朋友寻人打探，没有邻里察觉异常，最终被社会体系默认自愿离市，沦为无人知晓的亡魂。

长期深耕刑侦心理侧写的许砚，从未感受过如此刺骨的寒意。过往经手的所有连环案件，凶手大多拥有明确的作案动机，或是仇怨纠葛，或是利益纷争，或是情绪宣泄，哪怕是心理畸变的变态凶手，也会存在心态波动、作案破绽与行为漏洞。可林深截然不同，他的罪恶没有情绪、没有冲动、没有宣泄，只有极致的冷静、缜密与规划，他如同蛰伏在市井缝隙中的冷血猎手，精准筛选社会最边缘、最无声的弱势群体，将杀戮与藏匿打磨成日复一日的常态，整整两年时间，安稳藏匿于烟火人间，收割数十条鲜活人命，却从未暴露过半分踪迹。

安安市刑侦副支队长李建军站在研判台旁，看着屏幕上一排排冰冷的失联名单，脸色铁青沉重。从警二十余年，他亲历过无数血腥暴力的恶性案件，见过人性最极致的贪婪、愤怒与恶毒，却从未遇见这般泯灭人性、心思缜密、蛰伏能力恐怖至极的罪犯。寻常凶手作案之后必然慌乱逃窜、漏洞百出，而林深在两年数十次杀戮之中，不断打磨自己的作案手法与反侦察能力，心态愈发平稳冷静，行事愈发隐秘偏执，将罪恶完美掩藏在市井烟火之下，骗过了社区排查、户籍登记、警力巡查的所有体系，造就了这场横跨两年、无人知晓的连环炼狱。

陆峥始终保持着绝对的冷静沉稳，作为南城重案组组长，经手重案无数的他，早已练就泰山崩于前而色不变的心理素质。但此刻看着层层堆叠的罪证档案、密密麻麻的失联名单，眼底依旧覆上了一层厚重的寒霜。他清晰地意识到，这起案件的恐怖之处，从来不在于单一的血腥猎奇，而在于凶手极致的社会化隐身与精准的人性拿捏。凶手深谙社会体系的漏洞，知晓无人牵挂之人的消亡不会引发任何波澜，利用人性的冷漠与社会的盲区，肆无忌惮地持续作恶，将杀戮变成了无人察觉的日常。
他沉声下达指令，要求所有筛查人员彻底打破常规排查范围，不再局限于传统的失踪销户记录，全面筛查近三年老城区内所有注销手机号、清空社交账号、切断所有消费出行轨迹、彻底脱离社会活动的人群，最大限度挖掘所有被彻底抹去的人生痕迹，绝不放过任何一名潜在的受害者，绝不遗漏任何一条潜藏的线索。
指令层层落地，网安科全员再度提速，海量数据疯狂刷新流转，全城数据筛查力度再度升级，多部门联动的筛查网络愈发严密，全方位挖掘所有被隐藏、被忽略、被抹去的人生轨迹，誓要将凶手掩藏两年的所有罪恶，彻底暴晒于阳光之下。

与此同时，室外外勤排查工作依旧在夜色中艰难推进。江驰带队的十二支外勤小队，早已将整片老城区主次干道、小区楼栋、街巷死角、废弃空地全部排查完毕。深夜湿冷的雾气打湿了众人的作训服，浑身浸透寒意，持续数个小时的高强度徒步摸排，让所有人双腿酸胀、身心疲惫。更难熬的是心理与生理的双重折磨，凶宅室内那股黏腻入骨、挥之不散的腐腥气息，始终萦绕在众人鼻腔咽喉，反复诱发反胃干呕的生理不适，不少年轻队员脸色持续泛白，呼吸紊乱，却依旧咬牙坚守在排查一线，不敢有半分懈怠。

长期扎根外勤抓捕一线的江驰，心理素质远超普通队员，可此刻心底依旧压着沉甸甸的压抑。他太清楚这片老城区的地形特点，十年搁置的拆迁工程留下了无数废弃楼栋、封堵巷道、地下管道、人防暗渠，错综复杂的地下与地面盲区，数不胜数。凶手在此蛰伏两年，对整片区域的地形布局、监控死角、警力巡查规律、街巷通行盲区的了解程度，远超任何一名外来排查警力，他可以轻易找到最隐蔽的角落藏匿身形，避开所有排查视线与封堵卡点，在密布全城的抓捕大网之下，依旧保有喘息与观望的空间。
就在全域排查陷入僵局、凶手踪迹彻底断层的关键时刻，外勤二组的紧急汇报从对讲机内骤然响起，打破了深夜的沉寂。队员在建安小区西侧废弃拆迁片区最深处，发现了一处被人工精心伪装封堵的老旧排污暗渠入口，整片入口被建筑垃圾、生锈铁皮、废旧木板层层堆叠遮挡，表层杂草枯枝自然覆盖，从外观上看，与常年废弃的自然废墟别无二致，极具迷惑性。若非队员细致摸排、逐层核查，根本无法发现这处暗藏玄机的隐秘入口。
这条消息瞬间牵动了所有人的神经，陆峥当即下令全员原地警戒，禁止任何人擅自触碰封堵设施、擅自深入探查，同时带领沈予安、苏晚、许砚以及技术勘查、消防搜救全员力量，火速奔赴现场，开展深度勘查。
短短数分钟，核心办案力量全员集结到位。
深夜废墟深处的环境愈发阴冷幽暗，连片烂尾楼栋遮挡了所有光源，整片区域笼罩在浓稠的黑暗之中，只有队员手持的强光手电划破夜色，照亮眼前层层堆叠的封堵废墟。凑近细致观察便能清晰分辨，表层看似杂乱的建筑垃圾，实则堆叠规整、受力均匀、封堵严密，每一处遮挡物的摆放角度、覆盖位置，都经过精心设计，完美契合废墟自然废弃的状态，彻底规避人为痕迹。
封堵墙体侧面，杂草被长期踩踏碾压，形成一条极窄、隐蔽性极强的单人通行小路，小路完全避开周边所有残存监控的拍摄角度，隐匿在楼栋夹缝与杂草深处，若非近距离细致观察，根本无法察觉。常年稳定的踩踏痕迹足以证明，这条隐秘通路，早已被人长期、反复、规律地使用，是凶手专属的隐秘通行通道。
夜风裹挟着地底深处溢出的阴冷气息扑面而来，一丝极淡、幽深、区别于普通腐烂草木的人体朽味，顺着晚风缓缓飘散。这股气味稀薄隐晦，混杂在泥土腥气与草木腐味之中，普通人根本无法分辨，但对于常年接触各类命案现场、嗅觉极度敏锐的刑侦技术人员而言，一眼便能确定，这是长期土埋深埋、缓慢腐败的人体残骸特有的气息。
苏晚第一时间蹲身开展土质采样核查，佩戴无菌防护手套的指尖轻轻抚过表层泥土肌理，细致触摸土质湿度、硬化程度与微生物发酵痕迹。经过精准比对分析，她迅速确认这片区域的土质存在明显的人工干预痕迹，深层土壤有机物堆积异常，菌群结构与普通自然土层差异极大，地底深处必然埋藏着大量长期腐败的人体有机质残骸，是一处典型的人工隐秘埋尸点。
后续抵达的安市本地老刑警、基层网格员看着眼前隐蔽诡异的场景，皆是心底发凉，面色凝重。深耕本地警务工作多年，他们自认为熟悉辖区内每一处风险隐患，却从未知晓，这片看似荒芜废弃的拆迁废墟之下，竟然潜藏着如此骇人听闻的罪恶，整整两年时间，凶手利用这片无人问津的黑暗角落，藏匿罪证、掩埋尸骨，在所有人的眼皮底下，持续作恶、持续藏罪，无人知晓。
消防搜救队员穿戴好全套防护装备、气体监测设备与照明设备，按照规范流程，小心翼翼逐层剥离封堵在外的建筑垃圾与铁皮木板。随着封堵层被一点点拆除，漆黑幽深的暗渠洞口彻底暴露在众人眼前，一股混杂着潮湿霉气、朽骨寒意、地底浊气的阴风扑面而来，阴冷刺骨，让人浑身发麻。
老式排污暗渠建成年限久远，整体纵深极长，内部巷道四通八达、分支纵横交错，如同巨大的地下迷宫，贯穿整片老城区地底。渠壁常年被污水浸润，布满湿滑青苔与经年污垢，地面淤积厚厚的黑色淤泥，积水遍布坑洼，环境阴暗潮湿、密闭压抑，是绝佳的隐秘藏罪与藏匿窝点。
全员做好安全防护与通讯保障之后，勘查小队两两编组，手持照明设备、痕检仪器，缓步递进深入暗渠内部。深入不足十米，干燥渠壁的高台处，一排排整齐摆放的黑色密封收纳箱、加厚防水布袋、塑封储物袋，赫然出现在众人视线之中。
规整划一的摆放方式、分类清晰的收纳习惯、极致偏执的仪式感，与三零二室凶宅屋内的藏品摆放风格完全一致，高度重合的行为特征，彻底坐实这里就是凶手的第二藏罪据点，是他专门用来批量存放残骸、掩埋尸骨的隐秘地下仓库。
技术组立刻就地搭建临时勘查平台，逐层逐件拆封收纳物证，全程录像留痕、全程无菌操作、全程细致记录，确保每一处物证、每一丝痕迹，都能完整固定、精准留存。
第一批收纳箱开启的瞬间，在场所有人的心脏骤然下沉。箱内整齐码放着大量经过精细脱脂、风干、打磨、固化处理的人体肢骨碎段、指骨节、软骨残片，所有残骸全部剔除筋膜、洗净血污、干燥封存，处理工艺精细规整，如同经过专业加工的标本，完全看不出血腥罪恶的痕迹。
每一个独立收纳袋的外侧，都用极细的黑色签字笔标注着精准的年月编号，字迹工整、排列有序、顺延递进，形成一套完整规范的私人归档体系。勘查人员逐一对编号进行登记梳理，从最早的初始编号，顺延至最新的四十八号，整整四十八组独立编号，清晰罗列在众人眼前。
冰冷的数字，彻底击碎了此前十余起案件的初步预估。短短两年七百多个日夜，凶手以精准、冷静、偏执的姿态，完成了至少四十八次独立猎杀，四十八条鲜活的人命，被他悄无声息收割、归档、藏匿，沦为自己黑暗癖好的私人藏品，掩埋在城市地底的黑暗之中。
接连开启的收纳箱不断爆出更骇人的罪证，不同体型、不同年龄段、不同人体部位的残骸被分门别类存放，新旧痕迹层层叠加，处理工艺从早期粗糙简陋，逐步过渡到后期精细完美，清晰勾勒出凶手两年间的罪恶蜕变轨迹。从最初试探性猎杀、慌乱销毁痕迹，到熟练作案、选择性留存标本，再到心态彻底膨胀、建立完整归档体系、常态化杀戮藏罪，凶手在无尽的黑暗与罪恶之中，一步步完成了自我驯化，将屠戮同类变成了日复一日的寻常作息。
现场多名年轻警员、见习辅警早已撑不住极致的心理冲击，有人浑身僵硬、指尖发抖，有人胸闷窒息、头皮发麻，有人忍不住退至洞口外侧，弯腰剧烈干呕，胃酸翻涌不止。常年面对治安纠纷、普通案件的他们，从未见过如此扭曲病态、丧心病狂的罪恶，密密麻麻的人体标本、规整冰冷的尸骨归档，彻底突破了常人的认知底线与心理承受极限。
即便是从业多年的老刑警，此刻也面色发白、呼吸沉重，心底被极致的寒意与压抑填满。他们见过碎尸、见过埋尸、见过连环命案，却从未见过凶手能将杀戮变得如此冷静、规整、日常，没有丝毫情绪波动，没有丝毫愧疚恐惧，以极致的偏执与理性，系统性地收割生命、藏匿罪恶、归档尸骨。
沈予安深入暗渠核心勘查，穿梭在层层骸骨与罪证之间，逐一对每一组残骸的断面肌理、打磨痕迹、脱水程度、腐化周期进行细致核验、分类区分、时间定位。周遭所有人都被密闭阴暗的环境、层层堆叠的尸骨、极致扭曲的罪恶冲击得身心紧绷、生理不适，唯独他状态平稳、神色淡然，动作不急不缓、精准规整，始终保持着极致的专业与冷静。
他精准梳理出凶手四个清晰的作案阶段，从早期试探猎杀的粗糙处理，到中期手法成熟的选择性留存，再到后期仪式成瘾的规整归档，直至近期完美标准化的罪恶操作，每一个阶段的作案特征、心态变化、处理工艺，都被他精准拆解、完整复盘。同时精准判定，暗渠深处的淤泥回填层存在大面积人工改造痕迹，分层压实的土层结构之下，埋藏着大批量完整的人体遗骸，是凶手长期集中掩埋主体尸骨的核心区域。
陆峥当即下令启动精细土方开挖作业，消防队员与技术人员使用轻型工具逐层剥离土层，分层取样、逐层筛查，严格遵循痕检规范，杜绝任何痕迹破坏与物证遗漏。
随着淤泥层被缓缓剥开，一具具规整摆放、层层叠压的完整人体遗骸，陆续从深埋地底的黑暗中现世。所有遗骸都经过人为规整折叠、统一朝向摆放、严密包裹封存，掩埋方式极具仪式感，没有丝毫随意丢弃的凌乱，每一处细节都彰显着凶手极致的偏执与控制欲。
一具、两具、三具……连续出土的完整遗骸，让现场压抑的氛围彻底抵达顶点。苏晚持续高强度开展物证筛查、成分检测、痕迹比对，长时间面对海量人体残骸与腐质土层，让她脸色惨白如纸，呼吸急促紊乱，喉咙的恶心感反复翻涌，只能靠着极强的职业素养强行支撑，不间断输出精准的化验结论。
通过土层检测、腐化程度比对、痕迹叠加分析，现场彻底确认，这片埋尸点的时间跨度长达二十四个月，完美覆盖凶手两年的作案周期，最早一批遗骸深埋时长超过两年，最新一批遗骸埋藏时间仅有十余天，凶手直至案发前夕，依旧在持续作案、持续埋尸，从未终止过自己的罪恶。

许砚结合现场出土罪证、编号体系、埋尸周期、作案手法，快速完善终极心理侧写。他清晰判定，林深从始至终都不是突发畸变的变态罪犯，而是在长期的孤独、隔绝、社会化死亡的状态之中，一步步自我驯化罪恶，将杀戮、分尸、藏骨、归档，塑造成了唯一的精神寄托与日常作息。他彻底剥离了人性的共情、愧疚与恐惧，活在自己黑暗偏执的世界里，以猎杀同类为乐趣，以归档尸骨为成就，以藏匿罪恶为常态，完美隐身于市井人间，持续制造无尽的悲剧。
沈予安最终完成全部残骸的个体区分与统计核验，精准锁定独立受害者个体总数在四十二至四十八人之间。两年光阴，近五十条人命，无声消逝在这座平和的城市之中，无人知晓、无人悼念、无人探寻，最终只剩地底累累白骨，静静诉说着两年的黑暗炼狱。
就在所有人沉浸在无尽的沉重与震怒之中，全力梳理罪证、复盘案情、追查踪迹之时，许砚看着最新的埋尸时间、编号顺序与作案周期，骤然捕捉到一处致命的漏洞。
凶手最新的埋尸记录停留在十五天前，按照他后期稳定的作案频率，每十余天就会完成一次猎杀与归档，周期规律、从未中断。如今距离上一次作案周期早已逾期，却没有新增埋尸痕迹与归档编号，唯一的可能性就是，凶手在案发前夕，刚刚完成新一轮猎杀，受害者尸骨尚未掩埋归档，大概率依旧被凶手藏匿掌控，生死未卜。
这条全新的研判结论，让现场所有人的心神瞬间紧绷到极致。
全城布控、全域追查、深挖罪证、复盘旧案，所有人都以为这场持续两年的连环罪恶，只剩下抓捕凶手、结案昭雪最后一步。却无人想到，恶魔依旧在逃，且极有可能依旧掌控着鲜活的人质，一条全新的人命，依旧悬于生死一线之间。
夜色依旧浓稠，全城抓捕大网持续收紧。
地底白骨累累，旧冤未雪。
活人危机迫在眉睫，新险暗藏。
真正的攻坚追凶可能才刚刚进入最凶险的阶段。
en: The command center of the An’an Municipal Public Security Bureau blazed with light. The entire building had entered its highest level of emergency investigative response.

This was no ordinary night of scattered public-order calls. Duty officers, intelligence analysts, cybercrime technicians and household-registration specialists filled the hall. Dozens of computer screens glowed at once, while data streams, personal records, surveillance tracks and community registers crowded the huge wall displays.
An official notice upgrading the Jian’an serial cannibalism case had gone out to every cooperating unit.
This was not an isolated homicide. It was not a spontaneous crime of passion.
The findings established a long-concealed series of murders, suspected links to more than a dozen disappearances, and acts of extreme, grotesque violence.

The bureau chief personally supervised the investigation. The deputy chief responsible for criminal investigation took command at the center. Four operations began simultaneously: coordination across districts, citywide containment, the tracing of missing persons and the pursuit of the suspect.
Every member of the Nancheng Major Crime Team remained at the scene, working with local An’an officers as both lines of investigation advanced together.

The cordon around Apartment 302 on the third floor expanded again. What had begun at a single front door now covered the entire corridor and every entrance to the building. Local fire personnel, a second criminalistics team and trace-evidence examiners entered in batches, carrying out second and third rounds of painstaking searches.
The deeper they dug, the more bitterly the scene chilled them.
The first search had exposed the horror and bloodshed visible to the naked eye.
The second, more exacting examination began uncovering the evidence of over a year of serial murder that the killer had hidden in the details.
Su Wan led two technical teams through a fresh examination of every millimeter of the apartment.

Even after two full hours, the nausea in her nose and throat remained. Professional discipline merely allowed her to force it down. Wearing a fresh protective respirator, she passed a powerful cool-light examination lamp over the walls, the gaps in the suspended ceiling, the seams between floorboards and the hidden corners behind furniture, inch by inch.
“We’ve found sealed black storage bags in a gap above the ceiling.”
Her voice came steadily over the radio, quiet with prolonged concentration.
“Human teeth, sections of finger bones and preserved nail material, wrapped in multiple layers of sealed plastic. Separately packaged and arranged by size.”

An experienced technician from the An’an technical section, assisting beside her, paused. He let out a heavy breath. “Compulsive collecting. Preservation as ritual. Serial offenders like this keep a personal ‘souvenir’ from each victim.”
Beneath the successive layers of plastic, the small human fragments were disturbingly clean.

There was no stench, no blood. They had been thoroughly degreased, air-dried, treated against decay and sealed, leaving them perfectly preserved. The contents of each bag were uniform and neatly arranged. On the outer plastic, an extremely fine black pen had marked dates and numbers so tiny they were barely visible.
This was no haphazard collection.
Each item had been filed according to the order of the killings and the time of the crime.
Crouching below the ceiling, Shen Yu’an used a magnifying glass to examine the bone structure and dental development of each fragment, distinguishing and checking them one by one.

The apartment remained oppressive and sinister. Even the officers who had grown accustomed to it moved with tense caution, instinctively avoiding the terrible little trophies. Only Shen Yu’an remained composed, his attention fixed on the evidence as he classified and recorded it.
“On preliminary examination, these preserved fragments represent at least eleven different individuals.”
The corridor fell utterly silent.
Eleven people.
The earlier estimate of three to five had more than doubled.

Eleven lives had quietly ended in this room of less than thirty square meters, preserved, cataloged and treasured by the killer in the most twisted secrecy. For countless days and nights, the residents downstairs had gone about their lives, the neighbors above had kept their usual hours, and the whole building had carried on as normal.
No one had known how many murdered people lay concealed in that narrow space above their heads.
Standing in the middle of the living room, Lu Zheng listened to the figures. His gaze turned icy.

In more than a decade on the job, he had handled countless major crimes, serial murders and dismemberment cases. But a prolonged series of killings on this scale, so well concealed and so completely invisible to society, was extraordinarily rare.

“Update the case classification immediately,” he ordered into his radio. “Revise the victim count to more than ten. Formally designate this a serial murder case involving a deviant offender, under the highest level of special supervision.”
“Every unit—step up the pace!”
Downstairs, Jiang Chi had already spread his teams across the search area.
With Nancheng field officers, An’an tactical police mobile units and community grid workers, he had formed twelve squads to conduct a comprehensive search within three kilometers of Jian’an.
The old neighborhood was a maze of alleys and adjoining private houses, with narrow lanes running in every direction. It offered countless routes of escape and places to hide.
Flashlight in hand, Jiang Chi advanced rapidly through the dark alleys, assigning tasks as he went.
“Team One, every basement, rooftop cavity and abandoned storage room in the compound!”
“Team Two, the abandoned houses nearby, stalled demolition sites and unoccupied unsafe buildings!”
“Team Three, block every minor road out of the city, every service road beside the provincial highways and every checkpoint on the urban fringe!”
“Team Four, coordinate with the transport bureau. Check the past seven days of outbound private cars, ride-hailing vehicles and short-distance passenger services!”
The orders passed down through the teams. Within moments, hundreds of officers were deployed across the old quarter.
Countless flashlight beams cut through the night, weaving a dense net around the district.
Meanwhile, the command center’s efforts to trace the missing began producing a flood of results.
Xu Yan sat at a temporary analysis station surrounded by thick paper files and electronic registers. Dozens of civilian-duty police personnel worked alongside him, organizing the data.
Basic files had been completed for the seven people identified earlier. Now that the physical evidence pointed to eleven victims, the command center expanded the search period to twenty-eight months.
Vast lists of missing people, lost contacts, canceled household registrations and recorded departures were retrieved in batches.
“Team Leader Lu! New results!”

A cybercrime officer rapidly compiled the findings and called out, “Over twenty-eight months, fourteen young adults in the relevant age range, all living alone in An’an’s western old quarter or on the urban fringe, lost contact without explanation! No disputes, no emergency calls, no missing-person reports from relatives or friends. The system treated all of them as having moved away voluntarily!”
Fourteen people.

The findings aligned closely with the eleven individuals identified from the forensic evidence. The remaining three were most likely early victims whose remains had been completely destroyed, leaving nothing preserved.
Xu Yan’s fingers flew over the keyboard as he created and classified their files. His expression grew colder with each one.
“The killer’s hunting cycle began two years ago.”
He quickly mapped the development of the crimes and reported to Lu Zheng as the team leader arrived.
“He was extremely cautious at first. No trophies, no traces. He destroyed the bodies completely. That’s why the earliest cases were effectively invisible.”

“Later, his confidence grew until it became arrogance. He began keeping souvenirs and building a private catalog. The rituals grew more elaborate, he became bolder, and the intervals between killings shortened.”
“Two full years. Fourteen young people vanished, and no one asked.”
Xu Yan turned toward the black sky beyond the window. His voice was heavy and cold. “The worst part is that every victim belonged to the most invisible, least connected part of society.”
“Orphans. Tenants living alone. Migrant workers. Freelancers with no relatives or close ties. Young people cut off from their families.”
“After they disappeared, no family asked questions, no friend called the police, no neighbor noticed. They were ideal targets.”
That was the fundamental reason this appalling series of crimes had remained silent for two years, without a single case coming to light or being solved.
The killer had never chosen at random.
He screened with precision, selected with precision, killed with precision.
He specifically chose people whose disappearance would matter to no one.
Lu Zheng listened in silence for a long time before speaking quietly.
“Go through the victims’ entire lives. Childhood, education, jobs, social contacts, medical history, criminal records, rental histories—everything. I want to know when this man’s descent began.”
“Understood!”
The household-registration section and intelligence team immediately intensified their work.
By one in the morning, a complete life history had been stripped bare, layer by layer, and laid before them.
The most likely man.
Lin Shen. Twenty-nine. An An’an native.

His parents had divorced when he was small. Both remarried and abandoned him. He had moved between relatives’ homes throughout childhood, with no fixed place to live, no family bond and no one who truly looked after him.
As a teenager, he left school and drifted. No continuing school record, no social circle, no contact with former classmates.
In adulthood, he took odd jobs and short-term work, frequently changing cities, homes and trades. His credit record was clean. He had no criminal history, no record of fighting, theft or fraud.
In every public file, he was an ordinary man: clean, transparent, barely present.

But the less visible pattern of his life showed complete isolation. He lived alone, withdrew into himself and cut himself off from society. No friends, no relationships, no social contact, no involvement in any group.

Cybercrime officers retrieved his only online accounts. They were blank: no posts, no follows, no interactions. In two years there had been no comments and no browsing traces. He had severed every connection.

“Complete social death at the psychological level,” Xu Yan concluded, studying the screen. “He ceased to belong to society long ago. He lives among other people wearing the appearance of an ordinary man, but he’s outside it.”
As they turned through the records, an inconspicuous trail of rentals suddenly caught every eye.
“We have a key movement pattern!”

An officer raised his voice. “Two years ago, Lin Shen rented short-term accommodation in several cities, repeatedly moving between places where he lived alone! His earliest suspected base was in a county-level district of a neighboring city. The dates and locations match the first group of early disappearances exactly!”
Mobile predation, across cities and administrative boundaries.
The case escalated again.
Not just An’an.
Serial crimes across multiple cities.
For two years, he had moved from city to city, choosing victims and consuming them, quietly taking more than a dozen lives.
Outside, the sky was still black. Dawn remained four hours away.
The citywide containment operation continued at full pressure. Roads out, alleys, abandoned buildings and deserted corners were all tightly sealed.
Yet one inexplicable fact weighed on everyone.
Despite the exhaustive citywide search, there was still no trace of Lin Shen.
No recorded departure, no journey, no hotel registration, no purchase, no surveillance image.
It was as though he had vanished the moment his crimes were exposed.

Jiang Chi returned to the corridor from the field, a sheen of sweat on his forehead, his breathing slightly quickened and his face grave. “Nothing at any checkpoint. No sightings anywhere in the search area. The surrounding surveillance trail breaks off completely.”
“He knows the blind spots too well. The patrol schedules. Every gap in the city.”
Lu Zheng made his judgment at once, his gaze sharp. “He hasn’t gone far.”

“Someone who lives alone and commits crimes in secret for years is deeply cautious. He won’t risk a long-distance escape without preparation. He must still be in the old quarter, somewhere he considers completely safe—a blind spot none of us has thought of.”
While everyone devoted themselves to finding him and working through the mass of victim information, struggling under the crushing weight of so many lost lives,
Shen Yu’an completed his preliminary separation of the human trophies into individuals, arranged estimated times of death and classified the methods used.

He placed the fourteen suspected victims and eleven individuals identified from physical evidence on a single timeline, reconstructing the chain of killings in a forensic report that was clear, rigorous and free of gaps.

The officers hurrying around him were all strained and oppressed. The scene tormented them. Again and again came the stress responses of investigative work: tightness in the chest, nausea, the first signs of sleeplessness.
He put away his recording tablet, looked toward the darkness beyond the window and reported softly to Lu Zheng.
“All the physical evidence has been organized.”

“The killer’s methods improved over time. Early on, he destroyed everything. Later, preserving things became an addiction. His crimes follow a clear logic, his emotional state is exceptionally stable, and his ability to evade investigation far exceeds that of the average deviant offender.”
“He knows the terrain, the surveillance coverage and the pattern of police deployment in this old quarter inside out.”
As he finished, the command center’s giant screen displayed the latest assessment.
Bold red lettering struck the eye.

[ASSESSMENT: The suspect is exceptionally capable of lying low. He is highly likely to have used abandoned enclosed spaces with no surveillance or foot traffic over a prolonged period. He may remain concealed locally, watching and waiting for the police search to ease before attempting a further escape.]
The abyss had been exposed.
The monster was still hidden in the night.
The net around the city continued to tighten.
Fourteen victims, buried in silence for two years, finally had a chance to be seen and to receive justice.
But the hardest work in this two-year ordeal of serial killing and cannibalism had only reached its midpoint.
At 1:40 a.m., An’an’s old quarter sank into the deepest darkness of late autumn.

Rows of aging residential buildings blocked the sparse lights along the main roads. Tangled alleys broke up the city’s orderly grid. To the west, demolition ruins abandoned for a decade sprawled across a forgotten gray zone at the edge of the thriving city. The damp, cold wind passed through gaps in fallen walls, stirring dry weeds and rotting debris. It carried the deep chill of earth long undisturbed, wandering through the empty district. Under the night sky, the entire abandoned demolition area lay silent. No pedestrians, no passing cars. Even the streetlights used by night patrols had all been damaged and gone dark. Everywhere they looked was dense shadow, every corner holding its own unknown secrets.

The serial cannibalism case discovered in Apartment 302, Building 32, Jian’an, had kept the city’s police force mobilized for almost two hours. What was first classified as a single grotesque indoor homicide had grown, through accumulating evidence, into more than a dozen hidden cases. Preliminary forensic examination then established multiple unidentified victims. Each development pushed the horror beyond another boundary of what the investigators could bear. The municipal bureau chief personally directed operations at the command center, while the provincial public security department activated its emergency plan for major violent crimes. Cross-regional coordination was fully engaged. Hundreds of police officers, tactical officers, community grid workers, fire and rescue personnel and forensic technicians were on duty. From the compound, exhaustive searches spread outward, sealing every route from the city and controlling the blind spots between urban and rural areas. They were determined to trap the killer in the old quarter.
Yet after all that intense searching, the trail of the suspect, Lin Shen, remained blank.

Surveillance checkpoints, road movements, travel histories, transaction records and real-name registrations had all undergone repeated retrospective checks. Neither the previous twenty-four hours, nor seven days of historical data, nor comparisons of migrant-population records across several months revealed the slightest sign of his flight. It was as though, the instant the scene was discovered, he had stripped away every trace of his social existence. He had vanished inside a district dense with police, retreating into darkness without leaving anything they could follow.

Inside the temporary analysis center, the pressure was almost suffocating. Dozens of screens flickered continuously with enormous volumes of data. Personal files, missing-person registers, community records and maps of regional movements covered the huge high-definition display. Analysts, cybercrime technicians and household-registration specialists worked heads down, their constant typing weaving an urgent, oppressive rhythm through the still night. Their eyes were bloodshot. The sustained pressure was exhausting mind and body alike, but no one dared relax. A single overlooked entry might bury a victim’s case forever and allow a vicious killer to hide or escape again.

Xu Yan sat at the heart of the analysis area. As the team’s sole specialist in psychological profiling and movement analysis, he was already exhausted. Hours of uninterrupted, intense concentration had left his temples throbbing and his mind taut and dizzy. The stench from the apartment still seemed lodged in his nose. Physical fatigue and psychological oppression wore away at him together. Still, he clung to the last of his clarity, checking every missing person’s file word by word. He classified and recorded all unexplained disappearances, administratively canceled household registrations and prolonged losses of contact in the old quarter over twenty-eight months, refusing to miss even the smallest doubt.

After repeated rounds of detailed screening and cross-checking, complete records for fourteen highly probable victims were assembled. These young people, scattered through the unnoticed corners of the city, had strikingly similar lives. Most came from broken families, with little care or concern from relatives or friends as they grew up. As adults, they had traveled alone to unfamiliar places to earn a living. They spent years in rented rooms, with meager social circles, no stable work or settled community, and few close relationships. No one watched their movements; no one worried whether they were safe. That invisible, unattached existence had made them the killer’s chosen targets. Once they quietly vanished, no family reported them missing, no friend searched, no neighbor noticed anything wrong. The system ultimately assumed they had left voluntarily. They became the dead whom no one knew to mourn.

For all his years studying criminal psychology, Xu Yan had never felt such a penetrating chill. In previous serial cases, most killers had an identifiable motive: a grudge, a dispute over money or advantage, an outlet for emotion. Even severely disturbed offenders showed fluctuations, mistakes and gaps in their behavior. Lin Shen was different. There was no emotion, impulse or release in his crimes—only extraordinary calm, precision and planning. Like a cold-blooded hunter concealed in the cracks of ordinary life, he selected the most marginal and voiceless people, making killing and concealment a daily routine. For two full years, he had lived safely among everyone else, taking dozens of lives without revealing himself.

Li Jianjun, deputy head of An’an’s Criminal Investigation Detachment, stood beside the analysis desk. He stared at the rows of names on the screen, his face grim. In more than twenty years as a police officer, he had witnessed countless brutal crimes and the extremes of human greed, rage and malice. Never had he encountered someone so devoid of humanity, so meticulous, so terrifyingly adept at concealment. Ordinary killers panicked and fled after a crime, leaving mistakes everywhere. Across two years and dozens of killings, Lin Shen had instead refined both his methods and his ability to evade detection. He grew calmer, more secretive and more obsessive. He concealed his crimes beneath everyday life, slipping through community checks, household registration and police patrols to create a two-year ordeal no one knew existed.

Lu Zheng remained outwardly composed. Countless major cases had taught the leader of Nancheng’s Major Crime Team to remain steady in a crisis. Yet even his eyes grew cold as he looked at the mounting files and crowded lists of missing people. He understood clearly that the true horror of this case was not merely its bloodshed or grotesqueness. It was the killer’s ability to become socially invisible, and his precise understanding of human behavior. He understood the gaps in society. He knew the disappearance of someone with no one to care would make no ripple. Exploiting indifference and institutional blind spots, he had continued unchecked, turning murder into an unnoticed routine.

Lu Zheng issued a low, firm order. Everyone screening the records was to break out of the conventional search categories. They were no longer to confine themselves to missing-person entries or canceled household registrations. They would examine everyone in the old quarter who, within the past three years, had canceled a phone number, emptied social media accounts, ceased all recorded spending and travel, and withdrawn completely from social activity. They were to recover as many erased life histories as possible, missing no potential victim and no concealed lead.

The orders spread. The cybercrime section accelerated again. Vast quantities of data refreshed and circulated at frantic speed. The citywide checks intensified, and the multi-agency network tightened further, searching every hidden, overlooked or erased trace of a life. All the crimes the killer had concealed for two years would be brought into the light.

Outside, the field searches continued with difficulty through the night. Jiang Chi’s twelve squads had already covered the main and side streets, residential buildings, alley corners and abandoned plots throughout the old quarter. The cold, damp mist soaked their training uniforms, chilling them through. Hours of strenuous searching on foot had left their legs aching and their bodies exhausted. Harder still was the combined physical and psychological strain. The apartment’s clinging stench seemed to remain in their noses and throats, repeatedly provoking nausea and dry heaving. Many of the younger officers stayed pale and breathed unevenly, but they gritted their teeth and remained on the search line, unwilling to slacken even for a moment.

Years of field operations and arrests had given Jiang Chi greater resilience than most, yet a heavy oppression still weighed on him. He knew the nature of the old quarter too well. A demolition project stalled for ten years had left abandoned buildings, blocked lanes, underground pipes and civil-defense culverts everywhere. The complex blind spots above and below ground were innumerable. Having hidden here for two years, the killer knew the layout, surveillance gaps, patrol schedules and unseen passages far better than any visiting search officer. He could find the most obscure hiding place, avoid search lines and checkpoints, and still have room to breathe and watch beneath the net spread across the city.

Just as the search stalled and the suspect’s trail appeared completely lost, an urgent report from Field Team Two broke over the radio. Deep in the abandoned demolition area west of Jian’an, officers had found the entrance to an old drainage culvert, deliberately blocked and carefully camouflaged. Construction waste, rusty sheet metal and discarded boards were piled over it in layers, covered by weeds and dead branches. From outside, it looked exactly like the surrounding long-abandoned ruins. Without a meticulous, layer-by-layer search, the hidden entrance would never have been found.

The report brought everyone instantly to attention. Lu Zheng ordered the officers to hold position and secure the area. No one was to touch the covering or enter on their own. He took Shen Yu’an, Su Wan and Xu Yan, together with the forensic and fire-rescue teams, straight to the site for a thorough examination.
Within minutes, the core investigative team had assembled.

Deep in the ruins, the air was colder and the darkness thicker. Unfinished buildings blocked every outside light. Only the officers’ powerful flashlights illuminated the layers of debris before them. Close inspection revealed that the apparently random construction waste was actually stacked evenly and securely, sealing the entrance. Every angle and position had been chosen to fit the appearance of natural abandonment, concealing all signs of deliberate arrangement.

Beside the barrier, repeated trampling had flattened the weeds into an extremely narrow, well-hidden path just wide enough for one person. It avoided the view of every surviving camera nearby, winding through gaps between buildings and dense weeds. Only close examination revealed it. The established pattern of wear showed that someone had used this concealed route repeatedly and regularly over a long period. It was the killer’s private passage.

The night wind brought a subterranean chill. On it drifted a faint, deep odor of human decay, distinct from ordinary rotting vegetation. It was almost lost among the smells of damp earth and decomposing plants, impossible for an untrained person to distinguish. But the forensic technicians, accustomed to homicide scenes and acutely sensitive to such traces, recognized it immediately: the particular odor of human remains decomposing slowly after prolonged burial.

Su Wan crouched at once to take soil samples. Through sterile gloves, her fingertips lightly examined the surface, checking moisture, hardening and signs of microbial activity. Detailed comparisons quickly confirmed clear human disturbance. Organic material had accumulated abnormally below the surface, and the microbial composition differed greatly from ordinary soil. A substantial quantity of long-decomposing human organic remains must lie beneath it. This was characteristic of a concealed burial site.

The experienced local detectives and community grid workers who arrived afterward stared at the strange, hidden scene with grave faces and a deep chill. After years working in the neighborhood, they had believed they knew every potential risk. They had never imagined such appalling crimes lay beneath these apparently barren demolition ruins. For two years, the killer had used this neglected darkness to conceal evidence and bury remains. Under everyone’s eyes, he had continued committing crimes and hiding them, unknown.

Fire-rescue personnel put on full protective equipment, gas monitors and lighting gear. Following procedure, they carefully removed the construction waste, sheet metal and boards layer by layer. As the covering came away, the black mouth of the culvert emerged. A cold draft carrying damp mold, the chill of decayed remains and foul underground air struck them, penetrating to the bone.

The old drainage system had been built long ago. It extended deep beneath the district, its branching passages forming an underground maze across the entire old quarter. Years of wastewater had left the walls slick with moss and accumulated grime. Thick black sludge covered the floor, and stagnant water filled every hollow. Dark, wet, enclosed and oppressive, it offered an ideal hiding place for both the crimes and their perpetrator.

Once protective measures and communications were secured, the search party divided into pairs. With lights and trace-examination equipment, they advanced slowly inside. Less than ten meters in, rows of sealed black storage boxes, heavy waterproof sacks and sealed plastic bags appeared on raised ledges beside a dry section of wall.

The uniform arrangement, clear sorting system and obsessive ritual matched the trophies in Apartment 302 exactly. The behavioral similarities confirmed that this was the killer’s second evidence cache: a hidden underground storeroom used to keep large quantities of remains and bury bodies.

The technical team immediately set up a temporary examination station and began opening and collecting the evidence item by item. Everything was filmed, handled under sterile conditions and recorded in detail, so that every trace could be documented and preserved intact.

When the first boxes opened, everyone’s heart sank. Inside lay neatly stacked fragments of human limb bones, finger bones and cartilage, carefully degreased, dried, smoothed and stabilized. Connective tissue had been removed, blood washed away and the remains dried and sealed. The meticulous preparation made them resemble professionally processed specimens, disguising the violence from which they came.

On every separate bag, an extremely fine black pen had marked a precise year-and-month code. The writing was neat, ordered and sequential, forming a complete private filing system. Examiners logged the numbers one by one. From the earliest entry to the latest, number forty-eight, forty-eight separate numbered sets lay before them.

Those cold figures shattered the earlier estimate of a little over a dozen crimes. In just two years—more than seven hundred days and nights—the killer had carried out at least forty-eight separate hunts with precision, calm and obsession. Forty-eight living people had been quietly taken, cataloged and hidden, turned into private trophies of his dark compulsion and buried beneath the city.

Each newly opened box revealed more terrible evidence. Remains from different body sizes, age groups and anatomical regions had been stored by category. Older and newer traces overlapped. The preparation progressed from crude early attempts to later, meticulous work, tracing the killer’s transformation over two years. Tentative killings and panicked destruction of evidence had given way to practiced crimes and selective preservation. Then came total arrogance, a complete archive and routine killing and concealment. In darkness, he had conditioned himself step by step until slaughtering other people became part of his ordinary daily life.

Several young officers and trainee auxiliary police could no longer withstand the shock. Some froze, fingers shaking. Some felt their chests constrict and their scalps prickle. Others retreated to the entrance and bent over, retching violently as acid rose in their throats. Accustomed to public-order disputes and ordinary cases, they had never encountered such twisted, deranged evil. The mass of human specimens and the cold, orderly catalog of remains exceeded everything they understood and everything they could bear.

Even detectives with many years of experience were pale and breathing heavily, filled with cold and oppression. They had seen dismemberment, hidden burials and serial murder. Never had they seen killing rendered so calm, orderly and routine. With no visible emotion, guilt or fear, the killer had systematically taken lives, concealed crimes and cataloged bones through an appalling combination of obsession and reason.

Shen Yu’an moved deeper into the culvert, working among the accumulated remains and evidence. He examined the cut surfaces, smoothing marks, dehydration and stages of decay of each set, distinguishing individuals and assigning dates. Everyone around him was tense and physically distressed by the dark enclosure, the layers of bones and the enormity of the crimes. He alone remained steady and composed. His movements were unhurried, precise and orderly, his professionalism and calm unbroken.

He identified four distinct stages in the killer’s development: rough treatment during the earliest tentative murders; selective preservation as his methods matured; orderly filing as ritual became addiction; and, finally, the recent standardization of every operation. For each stage, Shen Yu’an reconstructed the crime patterns, psychological changes and treatment methods. He also determined that the backfilled sludge deeper in the culvert had been extensively disturbed. Beneath compacted layers of soil lay a large quantity of complete human remains. This was the central burial area where the killer had repeatedly disposed of bodies.

Lu Zheng immediately ordered careful excavation. Fire personnel and technicians used light tools to remove the earth layer by layer, sampling and screening at each stage. They followed trace-evidence procedures strictly, ensuring nothing was damaged or overlooked.

As the sludge was gradually removed, complete human remains emerged from the buried darkness, laid out in order and stacked in layers. Each had been deliberately folded, positioned in the same direction and tightly wrapped. The burials were intensely ritualistic. Nothing showed the disorder of careless disposal; every detail expressed the killer’s obsession and need for control.

One, two, three... As more complete remains were uncovered, the oppressive atmosphere became almost unbearable. Su Wan continued the demanding work of evidence screening, material analysis and trace comparison. Prolonged exposure to so many remains and layers of decayed organic soil left her white as paper, breathing quickly and unevenly, nausea rising again and again in her throat. Only formidable professional discipline kept her working, producing precise findings without a break.

Soil testing, comparisons of decomposition and analysis of overlapping traces confirmed that the burial site spanned twenty-four months, covering the killer’s full two-year period of offending. The earliest remains had been underground for more than two years; the newest had been buried only a little over ten days. Right up to the discovery of the case, the killer had continued to murder and bury his victims. He had never stopped.

Combining the evidence, numbering system, burial intervals and methods, Xu Yan rapidly completed his final psychological profile. His assessment was clear: Lin Shen was not an offender who had undergone a sudden pathological change. Through prolonged loneliness, isolation and social death, he had gradually conditioned himself to evil. Killing, dismemberment, storing bones and keeping records had become his only psychological anchor and daily routine. He had stripped away empathy, guilt and fear, living inside his own dark, obsessive world. He took pleasure in hunting other people, pride in cataloging their remains and accepted concealment as normal. Invisible among ordinary citizens, he had continued creating tragedy without end.

Shen Yu’an finally completed the separation and verification of all the remains, placing the number of individual victims between forty-two and forty-eight. In two years, almost fifty lives had silently disappeared from this peaceful city. No one had known, mourned or searched. Only the bones beneath the ground remained to bear witness to that long ordeal.

While everyone struggled with grief and anger, organizing evidence, reconstructing the crimes and searching for a trail, Xu Yan studied the most recent burial dates, the numbered sequence and the pattern of offending. Suddenly, he spotted a deadly discrepancy.

The latest burial dated to fifteen days earlier. In the killer’s later, settled pattern, he completed a killing and added it to his archive roughly every ten days or so, regularly and without interruption. The next cycle was already overdue, yet there was no fresh burial or new catalog number. The only possible explanation was that, just before the case came to light, he had begun another hunt. The victim’s remains had not yet been buried or filed. The victim was likely still hidden under his control, their fate unknown.
The new assessment brought every person at the scene to an immediate, unbearable tension.

Through the citywide cordons, searches, excavations and reconstruction of old cases, they had all believed this two-year series of crimes needed only one final step: catch the killer and bring justice to the dead. No one had considered that the monster was still at large and might still be holding a living hostage. Another life could be hanging in the balance.
The night remained dense. The city’s net continued to tighten.
Beneath the ground lay the dead, their wrongs still unanswered.
Above it, a living person might be in immediate danger.
The hunt might only now be entering its most perilous stage.

alt.en: Investigators and fire-rescue personnel examine a concealed drainage culvert in the old quarter at night.
alt.zh: 刑侦人员与消防救援队员深夜勘查老城区废墟中的隐蔽暗渠入口。

zh: 暗渠地底的残骸清理工作仍在无声继续推进，潮湿的泥土被一点点刷开经年积压的厚重淤泥，每剥离一层土层就会露出一截惨白枯朽的骨面，那些被深埋在城市地底整整两年的躯体层层叠压整齐排布，全部按照统一朝向规整放置，没有一具尸骨是随意丢弃凌乱堆砌的。持续不断出土的遗骸彻底压垮了现场大半年轻警员的心理防线，从入夜接到协查奔赴安市到此刻深夜深耕取证，所有人连续数个小时浸泡在极致阴暗扭曲的罪恶氛围中，感官被无尽的腐朽阴冷填满，生理层面的恶心反胃心理层面的压抑恐惧双重叠加不断侵蚀着每个人的耐受底线。不少队员只能反复退到废墟风口大口呼吸冷风试图压下喉咙翻涌的酸涩，眼底的红血丝层层蔓延，浑身肌肉因为长期紧绷僵硬酸胀，却没有一个人敢真正停下手中的工作放过任何一处物证痕迹。

技术组的取证流程严谨细碎从未中断，苏晚带领两支交叉采样小队分区作业将暗渠划分为十二个独立区块逐寸筛查，土层样本骨质残留纤维附着物油脂渗透物全部分区编号独立封存确保后续化验能够精准对应每一处埋藏位置每一个作案阶段。她长时间弯腰蹲伏在湿冷地面腰背早已僵直发麻指尖因为反复捏取取样工具微微泛白发凉鼻腔里牢牢黏着朽骨与湿土混合的厚重异味无论怎么换气都无法彻底冲淡。她比任何人都清楚这些细微残留物证的重要性凶手两年数十次作案全部依靠极致的清理手段抹去显性痕迹所有定罪突破口全部寄托在这些普通人无法察觉的微量渗透残留之上任何一丝疏漏都可能导致一条沉冤无法昭雪一桩罪证无法钉死。

浅层浮土之下检测出的新鲜人体蛋白残留是整晚所有线索中最锋利最致命的突破口，残留物氧化程度极低水分含量充足皮脂结构完整完全可以锁定十五天之内的新鲜遗留痕迹和深层所有钙化陈旧的遗骸残留形成了极其清晰的时间断层。这意味着凶手在最近一次作案之后彻底打破了自己坚持两年的固化仪式流程他不再掩埋尸体不再归档编号不再整理藏品不再完成整套闭环式罪恶工序。对于一个偏执型人格深入骨髓依靠刻板秩序维系自身病态心理的连环凶手而言打破规律绝非偶然只会是突发的外力干扰或是刻意的主观留存。案发突然暴露全城警力瞬间封控打乱了他的作案节奏让他来不及完成收尾工序或是他从一开始就刻意保留了活体目标将最新的猎物留在身边作为自己绝境蛰伏的底牌。
两种可能性无论哪一种最终落点都指向唯一的真相当下极有可能仍有一名受害者存活被凶手隐秘藏匿在整片老城区的核心盲区之中随时面临死亡威胁留给警方救援的时间已经所剩无几。

许砚站在夜风最盛的位置强迫自己抛开整夜累积的疲惫眩晕全身心投入凶手行为逻辑的深度复盘。他翻阅着平板内同步更新的所有侧写档案将两年间每一次作案升级每一次手法变化每一次心态转折逐条拆解对比。林深的畸变从来不是突发的精神崩溃而是长达数年的自我驯化自我封闭自我异化幼年被家庭抛弃青年被社会隔绝长期无社交无牵挂无归属的生存状态让他彻底剥离了普通人的共情体系道德体系恐惧体系。他没有朋友没有亲人没有羁绊没有软肋世界里只有自己单一的生存轨迹单一的黑暗执念别人活着依靠烟火温情支撑他活着依靠隐秘杀戮病态收藏偏执秩序支撑。

这类罪犯的领地意识极端强悍终生固守自己熟悉的方寸空间极度排斥陌生环境高压未知地带。常规逃窜罪犯案发第一时间会逃离案发地越远越安全但林深这类长期蛰伏型变态凶手的避险逻辑完全相反外界封控越严密排查越凶狠局势越绝望他越不敢踏出自己熟悉的领地半步陌生的街道陌生的人流陌生的管控区域对他而言都是致命风险。整整两年他日夜游荡在建安小区周边的废墟巷道楼栋死角每一处隐蔽通道每一处夹层暗格每一处监控盲区每一处空置空间都被他反复摸索熟记于心这里是他唯一的安全区唯一的掌控域唯一能够隐匿身形对抗全城警力围剿的避风港。
此前三公里全域地毯式排查从逻辑上看似无懈可击覆盖了所有外围巷道废墟空地城乡结合部盲点却陷入了最致命的刑侦惯性误区所有人都默认凶手案发后必然外逃必然远离作案楼栋必然规避曝光核心却偏偏忽略了最基础最反常规也最真实的罪犯心理绝境之中最危险的核心即是最安全的盲区。
凶手从未离开建安小区甚至从未离开案发三单元楼栋他只是藏在了所有人习惯性忽略建筑死角里借着居民楼整夜的烟火遮蔽人声掩护结构遮挡安静蛰伏冷眼旁观整晚睡遍数百警力封城搜巷挖骨查踪看着自己掩藏两年的罪恶一点点被掀开看着自己精心构建的黑暗秩序一点点被攻破始终隐忍不动不逃不躁静待警方排查消耗静待局势松动伺机而动。
思路彻底打通的瞬间许砚不再迟疑攥紧平板快步穿过层层警戒人员抵达临时指挥核心区将全新的研判逻辑完整上报推翻此前所有外围侦查方向。他条理清晰逐层拆解凶手人格特质领地习性蛰伏规律作案断层心理变化将所有细节串联成完整证据链精准锁定凶手藏匿核心区域就在案发楼栋内部并未远遁同时明确提出现存人质就近藏匿风险给出立刻收缩警力放弃外围撒网全员回撤原点毫米级深耕清查的最终侦查方案。
陆峥听完汇报瞬间敲定作战指令没有丝毫迟疑拖沓整夜大范围分散警力导致排查面广漏洞多效率低此刻必须彻底收拢拳头集中所有精锐力量攻坚唯一核心盲区。对讲机瞬间传出密集指令所有外围卡点仅保留基础值守剩余全部外勤小队特警机动组网格排查队技术备用力量即刻全员回撤建安小区重新部署清查任务重新划定作战区域重新锁定攻坚重点。
散落在老城区各个街巷废墟的外勤队员收到回撤指令后立刻调转方向全速奔赴小区核心点位整夜徒步摸排的高强度奔波让所有人双腿酸胀脚底发麻衣衫被夜风露水浸透冰凉贴身持续数小时的心理压迫让不少年轻队员情绪濒临疲惫临界点可一想到仍有无辜人质身处恶魔掌控生死未卜所有人瞬间压下所有疲惫不适感迅速集结列队整装待命。
江驰带队归队之后立刻配合市局领导重新划分清查区块以案发三单元为中心点向内收缩向外辐射覆盖整栋楼栋相邻单元楼顶地下室所有空置建筑区域实行分层分户逐角逐缝清零模式清查标准再度升级突破常规警务排查限度不止基础入户核查不止可见空间巡查所有建筑夹层管道竖井吊顶暗格墙体缝隙隔热层空腔废弃烟道弱电井全部纳入必查清单任何狭小隐蔽常人忽略的死角绝不放过真正做到楼不漏层层不漏户户不漏角。
新一轮清查工作正式启动整栋居民楼从一楼开始逐层向上清零基层住户大多熟睡被敲门声惊醒后纷纷配合开门核查每户居家环境都充满寻常烟火气息陈设温馨作息安稳邻里和睦平淡日常与三零二室地底暗渠的炼狱罪恶仅一墙相隔极致的反差让逐户排查的警员心底寒意层层叠加谁都无法想象朝夕相处的普通楼栋里藏着横跨两年累积近五十条人命的黑暗罪恶谁都无法感知日常路过的楼道夹层里蛰伏着冷血嗜杀毫无底线的变态恶魔。
逐层排查推进速度沉稳有序一二四层常规居住空间全部清查完毕住户身份信息居住轨迹作息状态全部核对无误无任何异常痕迹无任何陌生人员藏匿迹象楼道杂物堆消防柜夹层电表箱后侧全部清空排查没有发现凶手与人质踪迹所有常规可见空间全部彻底排除。
整栋楼栋能够藏匿身形的常规点位尽数清零最后仅剩楼顶天台隔热夹层这一处终极盲区也是整栋楼结构最隐蔽空间最狭窄遮挡最多排查难度最大最容易长期隐匿身形的死角位置。
两名身形灵巧的年轻队员轻步登顶抵达天台入口临近铁门时立刻放缓动作屏住呼吸全身心进入临战警戒状态厚重铁门表层布满常年锈蚀痕迹落灰厚重外观上呈现常年封闭无人触碰的废弃状态极具迷惑性常人第一眼只会默认此处长期闲置不可能藏人。
队员俯身贴近门框借助微光细致探查锁边缝隙积灰底层一处极浅极新鲜的侧向摩擦划痕清晰显露划痕规整单一没有杂乱痕迹是单人侧身挤入门缝反复推拉才能形成的专属痕迹灰尘覆盖度极低完全可以锁定二十四小时内新鲜人为动作痕迹。
细微破绽彻底坐实所有研判结果凶手确实蛰伏在楼顶夹层之内整夜未动全程隐匿在警力眼皮底下。
队员立刻抬手打出静默战术手势全员瞬间合围站位左右两侧封锁侧向退路后方队员压阵兜底枪口稳稳对准铁门方向形成无死角攻坚阵型杜绝一切突袭逃窜风险楼顶瞬间陷入极致压抑的寂静只剩众人紧绷的心跳声均匀起伏。
紧随登顶的江驰贴近铁门指尖轻触锈蚀锁扣能够清晰感知锁扣虚挂松动并未真正锁死凶手刻意制造铁门常年封闭废弃闲置的假象完美规避所有常规排查视线将绝境藏身术发挥到极致。
江驰深吸一口气抬手示意全员做好突进准备指尖轻发力缓慢推开铁门缝隙没有剧烈响动没有粗暴破拆最大程度避免刺激夹层深处蛰伏的凶手防止其应激伤人伤害人质性命。
门缝撑开的瞬间一股特殊混杂气味扑面而来没有室内腐腥的浓烈厚重没有地底朽骨的阴沉腐烂只有长期密闭空间积压的沉闷浊气裹挟着一丝极淡却锋利刺骨的新鲜血腥气息气味清淡却辨识度极强瞬间印证所有人的最坏猜想夹层之内凶手人质尽数在此。
强光手电光束精准穿透漆黑狭小的夹层空间扫过漫天浮动的灰尘照亮这片低矮逼仄的废弃区域老化脱落的隔热棉杂乱缠绕的电线管线经年堆积的尘土杂物交错堆叠形成无数错落阴影完美遮蔽视线构建出天然的隐秘蛰伏空间。
光束逐层扫过阴影死角最终稳稳定格在夹层最深处的幽暗角落一道瘦削佝偻的黑影静静蜷缩在墙角最内侧浑身彻底融入黑暗一动不动姿态沉静得诡异没有慌乱没有躁动没有抵抗没有逃窜哪怕此刻重兵合围绝境已成依旧保持着长期独居蛰伏的极致冷静心性远超所有常规罪犯的心理素质。
而在黑影身侧地面一道纤细柔弱的躯体无力瘫倒在地年轻女孩四肢被粗麻绳层层捆缚绳结死死勒入皮肉深处手腕脚踝布满密集淤青红肿勒痕皮肤表层遍布细碎擦伤干裂血点口鼻被厚实布条严密缠绕封堵彻底无法发出半点声响她发丝凌乱沾满尘土脸色惨白毫无血色双眼紧紧闭合单薄的身躯在冰冷地面上克制不住微微战栗微弱起伏的胸口是这片死寂绝境里唯一残存的生机。
所有人在看清画面的瞬间心脏骤然紧缩神经绷至极限整夜所有的焦灼压抑疲惫紧绷在这一刻尽数汇聚成极致的凝重对峙。
两年横跨两市的连环猎杀数十名无人牵挂的弱势群体悄无声息陨落无数被社会遗忘的沉冤深埋地底全城彻夜不休的封控排查全域深挖罪证复盘轨迹所有警力通宵达旦的付出所有技术人员细致入微的取证所有研判人员层层递进的推演最终全部收拢汇聚在这一方狭小幽暗的楼顶夹层之中。
恶魔蛰伏整夜未曾远离罪恶源头人质绝境残存命悬一线终极抓捕与绝境营救的最后对决已然无可避免。
