He started to rise, but a hand lightly caught his wrist.
Shen Yu’an’s grip was weak, gentle and restrained. He held on only slightly, an apology in his eyes.
“I’m sorry... I disrupted your operation.”
“I didn’t think... I just moved.”
“The trail’s broken... because of me.”
A perfect display of vulnerability.
Every action became an instinctive rescue, an unthinking response. Open, innocent, without a flaw.
Looking at that pale, guilty face, Lu Zheng felt his remaining anger dissolve. Only helpless concern remained.
He turned his hand and gently enclosed the cool fingers. His voice was low and hoarse. “It has nothing to do with you.”
“I was careless. I underestimated them.”
“You did nothing wrong.”
“Thank you, Yu’an.”
Thank you for saving my life.
Night deepened.
Tenderness pulled between them in the room, feelings moving beneath it.
At the bureau, the investigation was stalled on every front.
The decoy had taken poison, and the network had withdrawn cleanly.
Shen Yu’an’s hidden nature remained unseen, concealed beneath the light.

An’an’s burned-body and drug case was at a standstill. Yet far away in Nanshi, an unidentified body dumped by the river a month earlier was quietly finding its first hidden connection to that night’s dead end.
The room’s silence seemed soft. Only the regular beeping of the monitor marked the darkness.

Lu Zheng’s palm enclosed Shen Yu’an’s cool hand, his fingers resting lightly against its back. He dared not pull at the injured shoulder. Shen Yu’an curled his fingers slightly but did not withdraw. Long lashes cast faint shadows on his pale cheeks.
The dull ache continued to work into the bone. A small shift of his upper body sent tearing pain along his nerves. Still bloodless, he spoke slowly, his breath uncertain.
“Lin Hao... they couldn’t save him?” His voice retained the roughness of waking from anesthesia.
A shadow passed through Lu Zheng’s eyes. He nodded slowly and kept his voice low, unwilling to distress someone just out of surgery.
“No. He had poison concealed under his tongue. He waited after the arrest and released it once the questioning began. Emergency treatment couldn’t reach him in time.”
He swallowed, helpless anger in the movement.
“Every lead ran through him. With him dead, the gunman’s identity, the production site, the person directing them—it all stops. We’re left with fragments of evidence and no complete chain.”
Jiang Chi had just reported the aftermath by phone. The entire team was stuck at the bureau, staring at files. After a full day and night of work, this was the result. Morale had hit bottom.
Shen Yu’an listened quietly, eyes half-lowered, apparently full of regret.
“A discarded pawn... ready to die from the start.” He sighed softly. “We underestimated them. Their planning goes much deeper than we thought.”
It sounded like an investigator reflecting on an error. No one could see the momentary calm deep in his eyes: the indifference of a plan carried out exactly as expected.
Lu Zheng suppressed his frustration and softened his voice. “Stop thinking about the case. Your first job is to recover. We’ll handle the team’s work. You don’t need to worry.”
“But I can’t settle while it’s unresolved.” Shen Yu’an looked at him with a fragile persistence. “I performed the autopsy. I want to see the truth uncovered.”

“I know.” Lu Zheng’s thumb moved lightly over the back of his hand. “But your shoulder is badly hurt. The doctor says no large movements for at least a month, and no strain on the left arm. Let the other forensic physicians handle autopsies and scene work for now.”
Shen Yu’an did not argue. He murmured assent and rested against the pillow.
The monitor’s green light flickered across his face.
Soft footsteps approached. Jiang Chi entered carefully, carrying an insulated food container. He looked deeply tired, his eyes more bloodshot than the day before.

“Team Leader, I brought some plain congee. And the technical team has finished checking Lin Hao’s belongings. His phone was wiped in advance, the SIM damaged. No readable chats or call records. Nothing he carried points to anyone behind him.”

He put the container at the corner of the bedside cabinet and lowered his voice. “They left nothing. They never intended to leave a way back. Lin Hao was expendable from the start. Used, then destroyed.”
He turned to Shen Yu’an, guilt in his eyes. “Dr. Shen, I’m sorry. Such a serious failure on the operation, and you hurt so badly.”
“It wasn’t your fault. The trap was too well concealed,” Shen Yu’an said evenly. “No one could have foreseen the ambush.”
Jiang Chi gave a bitter smile. “We thought arresting him would open the case. Instead, they played us. Now we’re stuck, and the leadership has already called for progress. The pressure’s heavy.”
Lu Zheng released Shen Yu’an’s hand and stood. The criminal investigator’s steadiness returned.

“Pressure or not, we keep going. Don’t abandon the physical evidence. Trace the crystals, cord fibers and hard fragment further. Change direction. Stop centering everything on Lin Hao and follow the illicit circulation of the drug intermediate outward.”
“And keep comparing the footwear model. Expand the database search across cities. We may find a matching record.”

“Understood.” Jiang Chi paused, then added, “There’s something else. The provincial department sent a request for assistance. Nanshi had an unidentified body dumped by the river a month ago. Similar drug-production chemicals were found in the victim. The body had been handled to conceal evidence, and the case is still open. Their investigators suspect a group manufacturing and transporting drugs across regions. They sent the files for comparison.”
There it was.
Lu Zheng’s brows lifted slightly.
He had thought it a local An’an group. Now an older case in another city had entered the picture.
“Send the files to my phone. I’ll read them when I can.”
“I’ll forward them now.” Jiang Chi looked at Shen Yu’an again, urged him to rest, then left to supervise the continuing work.
The room grew quiet again.
Shen Yu’an lay still, apparently resting his eyes. In fact, he had heard every word.
The Nanshi case had finally emerged along the broken trail. The timing was exactly right. Neither early nor late.

Lu Zheng looked at the newly arrived file. A few indistinct scene photographs, brief autopsy notes—not much information. But the key chemical residues closely matched those found in the burned-body victim.
Two deaths, a month apart and in different cities, connected by the same illicit drug-production material.
He scrolled slowly, his expression grave.
“So it’s a network moving between cities, not a small local group,” he murmured.
Shen Yu’an opened his eyes. “Was the body in Nanshi deliberately treated to conceal identity too?”

“Yes. Dumped by the river. Water destroyed many of the surface traces.” Lu Zheng looked at him. “For now, it’s only a comparison request. We can’t say it’s the same group yet. Too little evidence. We’ll have to work through it.”
Shen Yu’an nodded, asked nothing further and closed his eyes.
Pain came in waves through his shoulder. His face paled slightly, but he made no sound.
Lu Zheng noticed his brow tighten and immediately pressed the call bell for a nurse to check the wound.

The nurse carefully lifted the outer dressing and examined the gauze for seepage. “It’s stable for now. But no large turns, and try not to get agitated. Pulling at the wound could make it bleed again.”
After she left, Lu Zheng drew a chair beside the bed and looked at the pale face.
Two thoughts tugged at him.
One was concern. Shen Yu’an had taken that shot for him and now lay quietly bearing the pain. The debt weighed heavily. The affection he had restrained was no longer easy to conceal.
The other was a small, persistent doubt.
At the yard, Shen Yu’an had moved too fast and too decisively. Almost as if he had anticipated the ambush, rather than reacted instinctively to sudden gunfire.
The thought flashed through him, and he quickly pushed it down.
It had been a life-or-death instant. Extreme tension could produce extraordinary reactions. He refused to think ill of someone who had risked his life to save him.

Feeling the prolonged gaze, Shen Yu’an opened his eyes and offered a faint, weak smile. “Team Leader Lu, you don’t have to stay here. There’s so much to do at the bureau. Go back. The nurses check regularly. I’ll be all right.”
Lu Zheng shook his head. “I’m staying tonight.”
“No buts.” His voice was gentle but firm. “You were hurt on my operation. I’m staying.”
Shen Yu’an watched him, a little warmth entering his eyes as though he were moved. He nodded and said no more.
Night deepened, and the city lights gradually thinned.
Lu Zheng leaned in the chair, checking the monitor now and then, sometimes looking at the quiet figure in bed. His phone rested nearby, the Nanshi files waiting for further comparison.
On the surface, An’an’s case was completely stalled: the decoy dead, the gunman escaped, the network hidden.
But the threads of two deaths had begun to intertwine.
The hidden arrangement continued. Eyes closed, breathing steady, Shen Yu’an looked weak and harmless. Inside, he was already calculating the next step.
Recovery would give him a legitimate reason to avoid all field arrests. Police attention would turn toward the older Nanshi case, giving the deeper network more time to withdraw and erase its traces.
After an uncertain interval, his quiet voice broke the silence.
“Team Leader Lu, when I’m better, shall we investigate this together?”
Lu Zheng looked up, his eyes soft. “Yes. When you recover, we’ll find every one of them together.”
Beyond the window, night lay deep. Lies and sincerity intertwined, and two murders remained inside the mist.
Three days passed.

Shen Yu’an’s condition did not worsen, but his shoulder healed slowly. The slightest lift of the arm sent tearing pain along the nerves. Thick gauze still wrapped it. Each dressing change, as fabric separated from healing tissue, brought a layer of cold sweat.

The room did not smell strongly of disinfectant. Lu Zheng had arranged a small bottle of a mild, plant-scented fragrance, barely noticeable. Jiang Chi and the other officers took turns visiting during the day, bringing updates. Most were bad.

Tracing the drug material had stalled at intermediaries. The illicit transactions peeled away into leads without names. Cross-city footwear comparisons had produced no matching prior offender. Every known contact of Lin Hao’s had either dealt with him briefly or disappeared long ago. None led directly to whoever was behind him.
The task force was stuck.

At two in the afternoon, sunlight slanted through the window onto the bedside cabinet. Lu Zheng sat beside the bed with a thick file from the bureau on his knees: the month-old riverside case from Nanshi.
While Shen Yu’an was awake, he read slowly through printed scene photographs, autopsy records and witness interviews.

Shen Yu’an rested against thick pillows. Unable to turn far, he angled his face slightly and let his gaze pass over the pages. He did not lean in or seem eager, merely glancing naturally. Yet every line quietly entered his eyes.

“The Nanshi victim was a woman, thirty-one. Her body was dumped on a downstream riverbank after nearly a week in the water. Many surface traces had washed away.” Lu Zheng spoke softly as he read, almost to himself, almost to Shen Yu’an. “The autopsy found a drug intermediate too. The same substance as in our burned-body victim.”
He placed a finger on one line of the report, frowning.

“Their police thought she belonged to a drug-production group and was killed in an internal dispute. But they couldn’t find the primary scene. No witnesses, no useful cameras, too many possible suspects. After a month, they had to set it aside as unresolved.”

Shen Yu’an listened with lowered lashes. His voice was level, weakened by injury. “Water carries away most evidence. That would be difficult. But the approach resembles our case: destroy identification and remove traces as completely as possible.”

“Exactly. That’s why the province asked us to compare.” Lu Zheng looked at him. “The method is very similar. Destroy the body, erase identity, use expendable people prepared to die rather than talk. The ruthlessness matches. It’s probably one group operating across cities.”

Shen Yu’an nodded and asked with the natural professionalism of a forensic discussion, “Do they still have the Nanshi victim’s bone sections? If so, we could compare injury patterns and see whether the same people were responsible.”
“They say the samples are properly preserved. We can apply to have them sent for comparison.” Lu Zheng turned the page. “But it’s a long journey and a complicated procedure. We need approval.”
Shen Yu’an murmured assent and looked slowly toward the window, apparently tired and letting his mind rest.
He was matching details in the file against information he already knew.

The cross-city drug group had deep, tangled roots and many expendable agents like Lin Hao. When they sensed danger, they sacrificed a pawn and cut off the threatened branch. The recycling-yard trap was only one of their defenses.
Lu Zheng kept reading the interviews, unaware of the subtle change beside him.
His phone vibrated. Jiang Chi. He answered quietly to avoid disturbing Shen Yu’an.
“Go ahead.”

“We kept tracing the material supply and found an intermediary known as Old Ghost. He moves between the two cities, handling chemical transfers. Someone saw him meet Lin Hao. But he’s extremely cautious: no settled address, constantly changing phones. Hard to locate.” Jiang Chi sounded exhausted. “We found that he’s been active near the Nanshi riverbank—the area of the dumped body.”
Lu Zheng’s gaze sharpened. “Can you locate him?”

“Not yet. He never uses one number for long. We have only broad areas, nothing precise enough for an arrest.” Jiang Chi paused. “And while checking footage, we found that a masked bodyguard often stays with him. Apparently very capable. Someone who saw him from a distance said his build resembled the gunman at the yard.”
Lu Zheng felt a jolt.
After all the circling, a fresh lead at last.
“Stay on it. Don’t alert them. Put plainclothes officers around the boundary between the cities. Report the instant you see movement.”
“Understood.”
He ended the call and turned to Shen Yu’an. “An intermediary called Old Ghost. Linked to both cases, and possibly accompanied by the gunman who ambushed us. But he’s too careful for us to pin down.”
Shen Yu’an turned slightly. Just the right degree of surprise entered his eyes, then faded. “Be careful. If he’s stayed hidden this long, he’ll have precautions. Don’t walk into another trap.”
The warning sounded entirely natural, a simple concern for field officers.

Looking at his pale face, Lu Zheng remembered the shot and felt his chest tighten again. “I’ll warn everyone. We won’t underestimate them. You concentrate on healing. No more dangerous fieldwork until you’re recovered.”
A soft smile touched Shen Yu’an’s lips. “All right. I’ll listen.”
Then a small surge of pain came from his left shoulder. He frowned instinctively and kept it absolutely still.
Lu Zheng set down the file and leaned forward. “The wound? Shall I call the nurse?”
“Only a little. I pulled it slightly.” Shen Yu’an shook his head and steadied his breathing. “No need. It’ll ease if I rest.”
The restraint left Lu Zheng aching and helpless. He was always like this, accustomed to enduring whatever hurt and rarely asking for relief.
He carefully drew the slipped blanket upward, avoiding the left shoulder. His fingertips brushed Shen Yu’an’s wrist in a brief touch of skin.
Shen Yu’an did not move away. He quietly let him continue.
Silence settled, with the monitor’s steady beeping moving through it.
Lu Zheng picked up the file but did not read. His eyes rested on Shen Yu’an’s profile, and the small doubt rose again.
At the yard, he had moved too quickly into the shot.
So quickly that he seemed to know it was coming.

Yet there was no reasonable evidence to support that thought. Shen Yu’an was a forensic physician. He had stayed with the team; they had uncovered every lead together. He had no motive to collude with criminals. And he had truly taken a bullet, suffered a serious injury and lay here in pain.
Lu Zheng shook the thought away.
One unusual movement could not justify doubting someone who had risked his life for him.
Still, the doubt remained like a grain of sand buried inside.
Shen Yu’an sensed the scrutiny but did not turn. He watched the view beyond the window, his eyes deeply still.
He knew Lu Zheng had begun to wonder. That was expected. A faint doubt was exactly enough: it would not erupt now, but could slowly take root through the investigation ahead.
“Team Leader Lu,” he said softly, “after I leave hospital, I’d like to see the section reports for the unidentified body in Nanshi.”
“When approval comes, I’ll bring them.”
“Mm.” Shen Yu’an closed his eyes. “I hope we catch Old Ghost this time, and uncover everyone behind him.”
The words sounded like a wish for truth. Inside, he was already prepared for what might change.
Sooner or later, the police would focus on Old Ghost. The people behind him had already prepared another move.
Outside the room, the task force spread its net along the boundary between the cities, waiting for Old Ghost to appear.

alt.en: Lu Zheng keeps watch beside Shen Yu’an in a quiet hospital room at night.
alt.zh: 陆峥夜间守在病床旁，陪伴受伤休养的沈予安。

zh: 凌晨五点半，天刚破一线青灰。

晨雾是凉软的，像浸了水的棉絮，压在两市交界的荒滩上。风刮过连片废弃铁皮棚，磨出细碎沙哑的嗡鸣，声响贴着地皮滚远，听得人耳膜发空。整片物流荒地区域死寂得吓人，早年这里是短途货运临时中转站，后来新区规划变更，商户陆续迁走，只留下大片被遗弃的建筑与场地。龟裂的土路纵横交错，路面嵌着干透发黑的泥块，荒草从裂缝里钻出来，细长的草叶托着饱满晨露，指尖轻轻一碰，露水便顺着草秆滚落，砸在泥土上悄无声息。报废货车歪歪斜斜泊在阴影里，锈蚀的铁皮表层剥落，红褐锈迹一层叠一层，被夜风啃得斑驳，和灰蒙蒙的天色融成一片模糊的剪影。
四组便衣全员蛰伏在暗处，分散在三处隐蔽点位。
没人说话，连呼吸都压得极浅。湿冷的空气钻透薄薄的作训服，顺着骨缝往里渗，凉意在四肢百骸慢慢沉淀，浸得人指尖发僵。江驰半蹲在卡车底盘后方，后背紧紧抵着冰冷的铁皮，金属外壳隔夜积攒的寒气源源不断渗进后背。下巴抵着膝盖，眼底红血丝密得吓人，整整七十二小时蹲守，昼夜连轴轮换，人的精气神早就熬得发虚。视野里除了浮动的白雾和摇曳荒草，再无半分活气。
耳麦里只有电流细碎的滋滋声，空落落的，衬得旷野更静。
“驰哥，还是没动静。”队员的声音压得极低，裹着藏不住的疲惫烦躁，声音隔着麦，带着一丝微弱的失真，“周边几条小路全部轮巡过，没有可疑车辆，也没有陌生行人。这片地方白天偶尔会有拾荒的老人，天没亮的时候，连野狗都很少过来。”
江驰闭了闭眼，睫毛上沾了一点薄薄的水汽，再睁开时，眼底只剩刑侦队员刻进骨子里的执拗。他抬手攥紧手里的对讲机，指节泛白。
“熬着。”他低声吐字，气息放得很轻，“这种靠黑链子吃饭的，越是沉，絕對在憋事。他不可能一辈子窩在裡面。老鬼要流转原料，要对下线，交易有周期，早晚要出来。”
一同蹲守的另一名队员侧过头，眉头紧锁，嘴唇抿成一条细线。他已经连续两晚没有合眼，眼下乌青厚重。“我们已经把所有进出这片荒地的主干道全部布控，监控调阅了半个月，只捕捉到几次模糊的背影，车牌全部是临时套牌，查下去全是报废车辆信息。”
“这是常态。”江驰微微转动脖颈，骨骼发出细微的咔咔轻响，“普通罪犯贪利、浮躁、耐不住寂寞，一旦嗅到一点风声就会慌乱逃窜。可代号老鬼的中间人不一样，像荒滩里蛰伏的蛇，阴、稳、狠，懂得藏息、懂得断尾，懂得把所有暴露的苗头掐死在萌芽里。”
三天蹲守，整片荒原干净得过分。
没有多余生活垃圾和临时搭建的简易棚屋，甚至连废弃车辆里，都被清理得干干净净，找不到任何遗留的包装、烟蒂、饮料瓶。对方做事细致到这种地步，每一处痕迹都会提前清扫。
天边的青灰色缓缓淡去，一点点透出浅白，雾没有散去，只是薄了少许，远处国道传来货车引擎低沉的轰鸣，隔着层层雾气，闷闷地飘过来。
队员轮流交替警戒，轮流小口啃着冷掉的压缩饼干，不敢生火，不敢开强光手电，所有动作都控制在最低限度。饼干干硬，吞咽的时候刮着喉咙，只能抿一点点矿泉水送下去。所有人心里都憋着一股劲，上次城郊抓捕遭遇伏击，队员遇险，线索因为林浩自尽彻底断裂，全队上下都憋着一口气，等着抓住这条唯一的突破口。
同一时间，市中心医院VIP病房。
室内恒温暖煦，窗帘是极浅的米白色，厚重的布艺面料滤掉了窗外灰蒙蒙的冷光，落得一室温软。床头柜上放着一小瓶香薰，淡淡的草木香漫在空气里，压过了刺骨的消毒水味，闻起来清浅安稳，像初春掠过湖面的风。房间空间宽敞，靠墙摆放着单人陪护沙发，墙角立着空气净化器，低低地嗡鸣，细微的声响融进房间的安静里。
沈予安半靠在床头，后背垫着两层蓬松的纯棉软枕，调整出一个不拉扯伤口的角度。左肩缠绕的白纱布，封得严实，从锁骨蔓延至肩峰，医用胶带固定住边缘，死死定住伤肢。昨夜护士来换药，纱布和新生的嫩肉粘连在一起，撕开的时候，细碎的痛感顺着神经蔓延开来，当时他没有发出一点声音，只是指尖攥紧了床单。残留的痛感不尖锐，却绵长磨人，像细小的针，一下下轻扎着骨缝。
他不敢大幅度动肩，连侧身的弧度都克制到极致。
他露在被外的右手手背上，冷白的皮肤透着薄淡的青血管，修长的指节微微虚拢，是常年握持解剖器械养出的细微惯性，安静又脆弱。他垂着眼，视线落在窗外出神，玻璃窗外是林立的城市楼宇，楼间距之间，能看见行道树的树冠，风一吹，树叶轻轻晃动。
侧脸线条清浅柔和，睫羽浓密，安静垂落，投下浅浅的阴影。脸色是大病初愈的瓷白，透着几分脆弱的苍白，唇色偏淡，整个人安静得像一個易碎的瓷娃娃。床头放着一杯温水，还有医生开的口服消炎药，药片整齐码放在白色药盒里。
房门被轻轻推开，门锁转动的声音很轻。
陆峥走了进来。
身上带着湿凉寒气，连日两头奔波，队里通宵复盘卷宗，眼底叠着厚重的疲惫，黑眼圈清晰可见，却丝毫不折他挺拔的气场。他放轻脚步走到床边，将温水和药片稳稳放在床头柜上。
“今早痛感有没有加重？”
陆峥的声音压得很柔，褪去了办案时的冷硬凌厉，尾音裹着细碎的暖意。目光精准落在那一圈白纱布上，细细扫过，检查纱布边缘有没有渗血、胶带有没有移位，确认伤口状态稳定，才稍稍松了口气。
沈予安侧过头，避开牵扯伤口。眼底盛着温软的光，眸光干净透亮，他轻轻摇了摇头，声线带着刚醒的微哑：“还好，就是還有點疼，能忍。夜里睡着的时候偶尔会疼醒，缓一会儿就能再次入睡。”
顿了顿，他看着陆峥眼底压不住的疲惫，唇角浅浅弯起一点弧度，语气温顺又体贴：“你别总这么来回跑，队里僵局难破，你已经够累了，不用天天盯着我。队里还有江驰他们，有情况护士会第一时间联系。”
陆峥拉过床边的椅子坐下，距离不远不近，分寸得当。指尖无意识摩挲着膝盖布料，是他思考案情时独有的小动作。
“案子有他们盯着。”他看着沈予安苍白的眉眼，语气沉缓，“你这边，我不放心。肩伤不是小事，伤到软组织，稍有不慎就会影响以后手臂活动。你是法医，解剖、现场勘验都离不开手臂。”
他简单两句，轻轻带过郊外蹲守的僵局，不愿让伤病在身的人跟着焦虑费心。
沈予安安静听着，睫羽轻轻颤动。眼底浮起一层恰到好处的惋惜与无奈，情绪淡得很，完全是旁观者替案情焦灼的模样。
“明明都摸到链条了，次次卡住。”他轻声轻叹，气息放得很轻，“对方藏得也太深了，布下的圈套一环套一环。上次抓捕，谁也没想到林浩会随身藏毒自尽，直接切断所有线索。”
陆峥看着他温顺安然的样子，心头积压多日的郁堵悄悄散了大半。这阵子全队所有人都被僵局磨得浮躁压抑，线索次次摸到、次次落空，每一次抓捕布局都像打在棉花上，有力无处使，憋气又窝火。队里办公室的灯光连续几天彻夜不灭，案卷铺满整张长桌，所有人反复复盘抓捕录像、尸检报告、走访笔录，一点点排查，却始终找不到突破口。唯独在这间安静的病房里，他能暂时卸下紧绷的压力，得片刻安稳。
“对方反侦察太强。”陆峥低声道，“上次伏击自尽断线索，这次直接全线蛰伏，摆明了跟我们耗时间。我们扩大了排查范围，跨市调取监控，走访黑市相关人员，收获寥寥。”
沈予安轻轻点头，不再多问，重新转头看向窗外。暖光落在他半边侧脸，柔和得近乎温柔。他安安静静靠着枕，呼吸平缓绵长，看上去全然沉浸在休养的静谧里，两人安静坐着，房间里只有空气净化器低低的嗡鸣。陆峥拿出手机，简单翻看江驰刚刚发来的蹲守简报，文字简短，依旧是无异常的汇报。他指尖在屏幕上缓慢滑动，眉头微蹙。
“江驰他们还在荒滩守着，已经三天。”陆峥随口开口，“环境很差，夜里温度低，荒滩蚊虫多，队员们熬得辛苦。”
沈予安闻言，轻声应道：“野外蹲守最难熬，长时间保持静止，精神高度紧绷。希望能早点有消息，不用让大家继续耗下去。”
陆峥嗯了一声，把手机锁屏放进口袋，目光再次落回沈予安肩头的纱布，目光里带着一点顾虑。
“等你伤势稳定，医生评估过后，才能考虑出院。”他缓缓开口，“现在别试着抬胳膊，换药的时候护士说了，伤口下面的软组织还在长，一旦用力拉扯，很容易二次撕裂，到时候恢复期又要拉长。”
沈予安微微颔首，视线依旧落在窗外。远处楼宇之间掠过几只飞鸟，小小的影子在玻璃上一闪而过。
“我记得。”他声音轻缓，“每次翻身都格外小心，不敢乱动。护士每次过来查房，都会叮嘱一遍。”
他顿了顿，微微偏过头，目光落在陆峥眼底浓重的青黑上。
“你也要抽空歇一歇。连续熬这么久，人扛不住。”
陆峥扯了扯嘴角，算是一个浅淡的笑。连日紧绷，这一点笑意也带着疲惫。
“案子悬着，安心不了。”
陆峥坐在椅子上，脑子里还在反复推演荒滩布控的方案。
老鬼这个人，他们拿到的资料极少。只有黑市零散的口述，没有清晰照片，没有固定联系方式，连真实姓名都无从查证。所有信息，都是不同的线人零碎拼凑出来的碎片。只知道这人常年往返南市与安市两市，经手化工原料中转，行事多疑，出手狠辣。
陆峥心里清楚，这是目前整条制毒链条上，唯一能够摸到的活人节点。只要抓住老鬼，顺着他的社会关系，就能一点点往链条上层挖。可对方仿佛天生就对风险敏感，无论布控多周密，总能提前避开。
他在心里默默复盘上次回收站的抓捕行动。现场留下的痕迹、枪手开枪的角度、林浩毫不犹豫吞毒自尽的决绝。一桩桩一件件在脑海里翻过，所有线索都指向罪犯极强的组织性。
沈予安安静陪着他，没有继续搭话打扰。他的右手随意搭在被子表层，指节放松，看上去闲散平和。只有指腹，极慢地摩挲着纯棉被面细微的纹路，动作轻得几乎难以察觉。
他清楚荒滩那边的布控点位，清楚队员轮换的时间，清楚陆峥定下的合围信号。这些信息，都是方才陆峥翻看简报时，屏幕上短暂闪过的文字，被他不动声色收入眼底。信息不多，却足够触发预案。
墙上挂着的电子时钟，数字静静跳动，一点点向正午靠近。
就在这时，陆峥口袋里的手机猛地震动起来，连续短促的嗡鸣，打破病房里安静的氛围。
陆峥立刻掏出手机，屏幕上弹出江驰的来电。他指尖划开接听，把手机贴到耳边，气息瞬间绷紧。
“我是陆峥。”
听筒那头，江驰压着声音，藏不住压抑的激动，混着旷野里微弱的风声，一并传过来。
“陆队，目标出现。”
陆峥脊背微微一挺，原本松弛的坐姿瞬间收紧，周身的气息一下子冷了下来。
“西侧小路，灰色厢货，泥污覆盖车身，临时套牌。司机戴着宽檐帽，整张脸埋在阴影里，副驾坐着一个黑衣人，身形偏瘦，一直低头，看不清脸，体型特征和回收站伏击我们的枪手高度吻合。车辆正在缓慢驶入荒地，看样子准备就地交割。”江驰的声音压低，“我们已经保持远距离尾随，没有惊动对方，四个点位全部就位，随时可以合围。”
陆峥目光沉凝，快速思索。
“保持距离，不要暴露。通知所有队员，稳住阵型，封锁所有出入口，我现在立刻赶往现场。”
“收到。”
挂断电话，陆峥迅速起身抓过搭在椅背上的外套。原本柔和的神色尽数褪去，眼底只剩下刑侦队长锐利果决的锋芒。他转头看向床上的沈予安，语速急促，却依旧不忘叮嘱。
“荒滩那边发现目标，我要马上过去带队抓捕。你乖乖待在病房，不要起身走动，有事直接按床头呼叫铃联系护士。”
沈予安闻言，瞳孔微微一收，脸上瞬间浮起一层虛假的紧张。他微微坐直一点，下意识想要抬肩，动作刚起，肩下的伤口立刻传来一阵刺痛，他微微蹙起眉，又缓缓放回去。
“是老鬼吗？”他的声音微微抬高一丝，带着牵挂，“那边会不会有危险？上次抓捕就遇袭了，你千万小心。”
他的眼神澄澈，担忧毫无保留地铺在眼底，没有半分伪装的僵硬。
陆峥看着他这副模样，心头一暖，抬手轻轻拍了拍床沿，语气沉稳。
“这次布控周全，多路合围，不会再给对方偷袭的机会。放心。”
“一定要平安回来。”沈予安轻声说道。
陆峥不再多留，转身快步走出病房。厚重的房门合上，咔嗒一声锁舌咬合，隔绝了走廊急促远去的脚步声。
房间里一下子安静下来。
窗外的日光依旧和煦，草木香漂浮在空气里，沈予安维持着倚靠床头的姿势，静静坐了几秒。方才眼底翻涌的紧张与担忧，如同潮水退去，一点点消散干净。
余下的，只有一片沉静如水的漠然。
他缓缓抬起右手，动作放得极慢，避开左肩伤口，探入枕头下方。指尖触碰到冰凉的手机外壳，轻轻把设备取出来。屏幕底色漆黑，亮度调到最低，几乎融进日光。屏幕没有响起任何提示音，后台一条暗码消息静静悬停在界面上。
【誘餌提前發動，計劃提前。】
短短一行字，没有多余情绪。
沈予安的指尖落在屏幕上，缓慢轻点，确认回执。操作界面没有弹窗，没有消息记录留存，每一次点击，都在同步抹除访问痕迹。三秒之后，消息自动销毁，后台登录端口同步关闭，所有操作日志就地清空，不留半点可供追踪的痕迹。
他把手机放回枕下，手臂轻轻落回被褥上。
窗外的风穿过窗缝，掀动米白色窗帘的边角，光影在墙面轻轻晃动。沈予安的视线重新落向远处林立的楼宇，面上没有任何表情起伏。
他安静坐在床上，等着远处荒滩上演的那一场扑空。
两市交界的物流荒滩。
风比晨间强劲了不少，卷着荒草的碎叶，在空旷的地面来回扫动。空气里那股淡淡的工业塑胶气味，愈发清晰，干涩刺鼻，混着泥土和野草的气息，在旷野里铺开。
江驰趴在废弃卡车的阴影里，举着单筒望远镜，视线牢牢锁在那台灰色厢货上。车辆停在荒地中心一块平整的空地上，后车厢门半敞，黑色密封包装袋堆叠在车厢内部，袋身厚重，里面装着经过初步提纯的化工原料。
队员们分散在四周的掩体后方，手按在腰间配枪，呼吸放轻，目光死死锁定厢货周边。
“车辆停稳，暂时没有人员下车。”耳麦里传来观察岗队员的汇报，“视野内，两个人，司机和副驾，还在车上。”
江驰压低声音回应：“继续观察，等他们开始交割再动手，确认人赃并获。”
所有人屏息等待，旷野里只剩下风吹草叶的沙沙声响。
一分钟，两分钟，三分钟。
车厢门口依旧没有动静。
江驰微微皱起眉头，握着望远镜的手指慢慢收紧。
“不对劲。”他低声开口，“如果是交割，到地方之后应该很快下车对接。”
话音落下的瞬间，远处国道方向传来一阵微弱的引擎轰鸣，由近至远，迅速消失在视野尽头。
江驰心里咯噔一下。
“人跑了！”
他几乎是脱口而出，“立刻突进！”
埋伏在四周的队员闻声，低姿冲出掩体，朝着厢货全速冲刺。脚步声踩在干裂的泥土上，急促厚重。短短几十米距离，众人转瞬冲到货车旁边，枪口对准车厢内部。
车厢空空荡荡。
只有堆在角落的黑色密封袋，还有散落的包装碎屑。
人，消失了。
江驰跳上货车车厢，指尖摸了摸密封袋的表面，袋子还有余温，说明刚刚才在这里放置不久。
“他们提前弃车，换了别的交通工具离开。”江驰转头看向围拢过来的队员，声音紧绷，“立刻散开，扩大搜索范围，沿着所有小路追查脚印、轮胎痕迹！”
队员迅速四散，沿着荒地所有岔路向外搜寻。
大片荒草被仔细排查，泥土路面仔细勘验。可地面上干干净净，没有新鲜脚印，没有二轮车、摩托车的胎印。对方撤离的时候，刻意清理掉了所有地面痕迹。
“驰哥，西侧小路找到少量车轮印，但只有很短一段，再往外就是硬化路面，痕迹彻底消失。”一名队员跑回来汇报，“没有目击者，附近连拾荒的人都没有。”
“东边路口监控，刚刚调取，十分钟前有一辆黑色无牌摩托，两个人，高速驶离荒地，驶入城乡结合部小巷，后续监控盲区，跟丢了。”另一名队员拿着对讲机汇报。
江驰站在货车旁，风吹起他额前的碎发，胸腔里堵着一股沉重的无力感。又是这样，眼看着目标就在眼前，转瞬之间凭空脱身，只留下货物作为诱饵。
陆峥快步赶到现场，皮鞋踩过满地草屑，走到厢货旁边。他看向车厢内的原料包装袋，目光扫过空旷荒芜的四周。
“痕迹勘验组到了没有？”
“正在路上，十分钟之内抵达。”
“封锁整片区域，所有物证原地保护。”陆峥沉声安排，“样品提取送检，溯源这批化工原料的来源。通知各路口卡点，重点排查黑色双人摩托。”
“收到。”
队员分头行动，拉起警戒线，等候技术人员到场。风持续吹过荒滩，卷起尘土，掠过废弃铁皮棚，发出呜呜的轻响。
陆峥站在警戒线之内，目光望向四通八达的小路。对手预判能力极强，仿佛提前知晓合围的时间节点，算准了埋伏的位置。他心里只有对罪犯缜密布局的惊叹与恼火，认定对方只是反侦察手段远超普通嫌犯，没有半分念头，将这件事和病房里休养的沈予安联系在一起。
江驰走到陆峥身侧，低声开口，语气里满是挫败。
“又扑空了。对方像是提前收到消息，我们刚准备合围，人已经弃车跑了。”
“是预判，不是巧合。”陆峥缓缓开口，眉头紧锁，“老鬼清楚这片荒地所有逃生路线，提前做好弃货撤离的预案。这批原料，就是用来拖住我们的诱饵。”
“那接下来怎么办？”
“继续蹲守。”陆峥目光望向远处的薄雾，“诱饵放出来，说明他们近期还有交易需求。只要他们还要流转原料，就一定会再次露面。通知各组，调整蹲守轮换方案，增加隐蔽点位，缩小暴露风险。”
江驰点头，转身去传达指令。
荒滩之上，警戒线在风里轻轻晃动。物证袋静静摆在地面，化工原料刺鼻的味道慢慢在风里消散。线索刚刚露头，便再次断裂。
陆峥站在原地，目光望向远方连绵的荒草。挫败感沉甸甸压在肩头，但是他心底依旧抱着希望，只要持续盯守，总有抓到对方的一天。
没有人想到，这一场天衣无缝的撤离，源头安安静静藏在市中心医院温暖的病房之中。
病房内，沈予安微微侧过头，目光落在墙上时钟。分针缓慢转动，算着荒滩那边合围、发现空车、队员搜寻的时间。
他缓缓抬起右手，指尖轻轻搭在被子上，安静地坐着。窗外日光缓缓移动，在地板上慢慢推移。
床头的呼叫铃安安静静，药盒整齐摆放，草木香依旧漫在空气里。一切如常，看上去，这里只是一间普通的病房，躺着一位因伤休养的法医。
他静静等待，等待陆峥忙完现场，返回医院。等待下一轮线索的拉扯，等待下一次警方的追击。棋局缓缓推进，他藏在光明之中，不动声色，看着外面的人在迷雾之中奔走。
手机依旧安安稳稳躺在枕头之下，悄无声息。
en: At five-thirty in the morning, the first blue-gray line of dawn appeared.

Mist lay cool and soft over the wasteland between the two cities, like water-soaked cotton. Wind rubbed against abandoned sheet-metal sheds, producing a faint, hoarse hum that rolled close to the ground. The old logistics site was unnervingly silent. Once a temporary transfer station for short-haul freight, it had emptied after plans for the new district changed and the businesses moved away. Cracked dirt roads crossed between abandoned buildings. Dry, black clods were embedded in the surface, and long grass rose through the fissures, holding heavy drops of dew. A touch sent them sliding soundlessly into the earth. Scrap trucks leaned in the shadows, their flaking skins layered with reddish rust, worn mottled by the wind and merging into the gray morning.
Four groups of plainclothes officers waited in concealment across three hidden positions.

No one spoke. Even breathing was shallow. Damp cold penetrated the thin training clothes, settling into stiff fingers and limbs. Jiang Chi crouched behind a truck chassis, his back pressed to metal that had gathered the night’s chill. His chin rested against his knee. His eyes were densely bloodshot. Seventy-two hours of surveillance, with shifts rotating around the clock, had drained everyone. Beyond him, only drifting mist and swaying weeds moved.
A faint electrical hiss filled his earpiece, making the emptiness seem quieter still.

“Nothing yet, Jiang Chi.” The officer kept his voice low, unable to hide fatigue and irritation. The microphone gave it a slight distortion. “We’ve checked every nearby path on rotation. No suspicious vehicles or strangers. An occasional elderly scavenger comes here by day. Before dawn, even stray dogs barely show up.”
Jiang Chi closed his eyes. Moisture clung lightly to his lashes. When he opened them, only the stubbornness of an investigator remained. He gripped the radio until his knuckles whitened.

“We wait,” he said softly. “People who live off a network like this don’t stay quiet for nothing. He can’t hide forever. Old Ghost has materials to move and people downstream to meet. Transactions follow a cycle. He’ll come out.”

Another officer turned toward him, brow furrowed, lips pressed thin. He had not slept for two nights. “We’ve covered every main access road and reviewed half a month of footage. Only a few blurred figures. Every plate is a temporary clone. The records all lead to scrapped vehicles.”

“That’s normal.” Jiang Chi slowly turned his neck, the joints clicking faintly. “Ordinary offenders get greedy, impatient, lonely. A hint of danger and they panic. Old Ghost is different. Like a snake lying out here: secretive, steady, ruthless. Knows how to stay still, shed a threatened tail and stop exposure before it starts.”
After three days of watching, the wasteland was too clean.

No stray household rubbish, no makeshift shelter. Even the abandoned vehicles had been cleared of wrappers, cigarette ends and bottles. The other side was meticulous enough to remove every trace in advance.
The blue-gray horizon paled. The mist did not lift, but thinned a little. From the distant national highway came the muffled rumble of a truck engine.

Officers took turns watching and eating small bites of cold compressed biscuits. No fire, no bright flashlight; every movement kept minimal. The dry biscuits scraped their throats and needed a little bottled water to swallow. Everyone carried the same stubborn anger. The last arrest had brought an ambush, an injured colleague and a trail destroyed by Lin Hao’s suicide. They were waiting for this one remaining opening.
At the same time, in the city-center hospital’s private room,

the air was warm and steady. Pale cream curtains filtered the gray light into softness. A small bottle of fragrance on the bedside cabinet sent a mild green scent through the room, masking the sharpness of disinfectant. It was light and calm, like a spring breeze across a lake. The room was spacious, with a single visitor’s sofa against the wall and an air purifier humming quietly in one corner.

Shen Yu’an rested against two thick cotton pillows, angled to avoid pulling the wound. White gauze covered his left shoulder from collarbone to shoulder tip, secured firmly with medical tape. During the previous night’s dressing change, the gauze had adhered to new tissue. Removing it sent small pains along the nerves. He had made no sound, only gripped the sheet. The lingering ache was not sharp, but persistent, like tiny needles tapping at the bone.
He dared not move the shoulder far. Even turning to one side was carefully controlled.

Above the blanket, faint blue veins showed through the pale skin of his right hand. The long fingers rested in the slight curve formed by years of holding autopsy instruments. He looked out at the city buildings. Between them, roadside tree crowns shifted gently in the wind.

His profile was quiet and soft, dense lashes lowered into faint shadows. His face held the fragile pallor of someone recovering, lips light, the whole figure almost like delicate porcelain. Warm water and prescribed oral medication stood beside him, the tablets arranged in a white box.
The door opened gently, its latch barely audible.
Lu Zheng entered.

He brought the damp cold with him. Days moving between the hospital and bureau, and nights reviewing files, had left deep fatigue and clear shadows beneath his eyes, though his bearing remained straight. He approached quietly and placed the warm water and tablets steadily on the cabinet.
“Has the pain been worse this morning?”
His voice had lost its working severity. He studied the bandages, checking the edges for bleeding and the tape for movement. Only after confirming they looked stable did he ease a little.

Shen Yu’an turned carefully. His gaze was clear and warm. He shook his head, his voice slightly rough from waking. “Not much. It still hurts, but I can bear it. Sometimes it wakes me at night. If I wait a little, I can sleep again.”

He paused, looking at the fatigue Lu Zheng could not conceal, and offered a small, considerate smile. “Don’t keep running back and forth. The case is difficult enough. You don’t need to watch me every day. Jiang Chi and the others are there, and the nurses will call if anything happens.”
Lu Zheng drew the chair closer and sat at a careful distance. His fingers rubbed unconsciously at the fabric over his knee, a small habit when thinking through a case.

“They’re watching the case.” He looked at the pale face. “I worry about you. A shoulder injury isn’t minor. Damage to the soft tissue could affect the arm later. You’re a forensic physician. You need your arms for autopsies and scene work.”
In a few brief words, he passed over the stalled surveillance outside the city, unwilling to burden an injured man with it.
Shen Yu’an listened, lashes moving lightly. Just the right measure of regret and helplessness entered his eyes: an observer worried about the investigation.

“We reach the chain and get blocked every time,” he sighed softly. “They’re buried so deep, with one trap inside another. No one expected Lin Hao to carry poison and cut every lead by killing himself.”

Looking at his quiet face, Lu Zheng felt much of the frustration accumulated over days ease. The whole team had become restless and oppressed by the stalemate. Each lead appeared, then failed. Each operation seemed to strike cotton—effort with nothing to grip. The office lights had remained on all night for days. Files covered the long table as everyone reviewed arrest footage, autopsy reports and interviews without finding a way through. Only in this quiet room could he briefly put the pressure down.

“Their counter-investigation is too strong,” he said. “Last time an ambush and suicide. This time everyone goes to ground. They’re deliberately wearing us out. We’ve widened the search, requested footage across cities and interviewed illicit-market contacts. Very little.”

Shen Yu’an nodded and asked no more. He returned his gaze to the window, warm light on half his face. Resting quietly against the pillow, breathing evenly, he seemed entirely absorbed in recovery. They sat together in silence, with only the purifier humming. Lu Zheng checked a short surveillance update from Jiang Chi. Still no unusual activity. He scrolled slowly, frowning.
“They’re still out on the wasteland. Three days now,” he remarked. “Poor conditions, cold nights, insects. It’s wearing them down.”
“Outdoor surveillance is the hardest,” Shen Yu’an said. “Staying motionless so long, always alert. I hope something comes soon, so they don’t have to keep enduring it.”
Lu Zheng murmured agreement, locked the phone and put it away. His eyes returned to the shoulder dressing.

“We can only consider discharge once the injury is stable and the doctor has assessed you. Don’t try lifting the arm. The nurse said the tissue beneath the wound is still healing. Pulling it could tear it again and extend the recovery.”
Shen Yu’an nodded, still looking outside. A few birds passed between distant buildings, their small shapes flickering over the glass.
“I remember. I’m careful every time I turn. The nurses remind me whenever they come.”
He paused and angled his face toward the dark shadows beneath Lu Zheng’s eyes.
“You should find time to rest too. No one can keep going like this.”
Lu Zheng’s mouth moved into a slight smile, tired even in that small expression.
“I can’t settle while the case is open.”
Sitting there, he continued running through the surveillance plan.

They knew very little about Old Ghost. Scattered statements from illicit-market contacts, no clear photograph, no fixed means of contact, not even a verified real name. Different informants had supplied fragments. All they knew was that he moved repeatedly between Nanshi and An’an, handled chemical transfers, trusted little and acted ruthlessly.

Lu Zheng understood that this was their only reachable living connection to the production chain. Catch him, and his contacts could lead them upward. Yet the man seemed instinctively sensitive to risk, avoiding even carefully arranged surveillance in advance.
He silently reviewed the recycling-yard operation: the traces left behind, the gunman’s angle, Lin Hao’s immediate readiness to die. Every detail pointed to a highly organized group.

Shen Yu’an sat quietly with him, not interrupting. His right hand rested loosely on the blanket. Only the pads of his fingers moved, slowly brushing the fine cotton weave, almost too lightly to notice.

He knew the positions on the wasteland, the rotation times and the signal Lu Zheng had chosen for the arrest. He had quietly read the brief words on the screen while Lu Zheng viewed the update. It was not much, but enough to activate the contingency plan.
The digital clock on the wall advanced toward noon.
Then the phone in Lu Zheng’s pocket vibrated sharply, breaking the quiet.
He took it out at once. Jiang Chi’s name appeared. He answered, tension returning to his breathing.
“Lu Zheng.”
Jiang Chi’s hushed voice carried contained excitement, mixed with faint wind.
“The target’s here.”
Lu Zheng’s back straightened. His relaxed posture tightened, his presence turning cold.
“Tell me.”

“Western path. Gray box truck, body covered in mud, cloned plate. The driver has a wide-brimmed hat and his face is in shadow. A slim person in black is in the passenger seat, head down. The build closely matches the gunman at the yard. They’re moving slowly into the site. Looks like a handover.” Jiang Chi lowered his voice. “We’re following at a distance. They haven’t noticed. All four positions are ready to close in.”
Lu Zheng considered quickly, his gaze fixed.
“Keep your distance. Don’t expose yourselves. Tell everyone to hold formation and cover the exits. I’m coming now.”
“Understood.”
Lu Zheng ended the call and rose, taking his jacket from the chair. All softness left his face. He turned to Shen Yu’an, speaking quickly but still remembering to reassure him.
“They’ve found the target. I need to lead the arrest. Stay here. Don’t get up and walk around. Use the call bell if you need anything.”
Shen Yu’an’s pupils narrowed slightly. A false anxiety appeared on his face. He tried to sit straighter and lift his shoulder, then winced at the pain and carefully settled it again.
“Old Ghost?” His voice rose a little with concern. “Will it be dangerous? You were attacked last time. Please be careful.”
His eyes were clear, the worry entirely convincing.
Warmth touched Lu Zheng. He lightly patted the edge of the bed.
“We have full coverage this time, several teams closing in. We won’t give them another chance to ambush us. Don’t worry.”
“Come back safely,” Shen Yu’an said softly.
“I will.”
Lu Zheng left quickly. The heavy door closed, its latch clicking into place and cutting off his receding footsteps.
The room became still.
Sunlight remained warm and the green scent hung in the air. Shen Yu’an sat against the pillows for several seconds. The worry in his eyes receded like a tide.
Only a deep, still indifference remained.

Slowly, with his right hand, he reached beneath the pillow, careful of the left shoulder. His fingertips met the cool phone case. He drew it out. The screen was black-backed and dim enough to disappear in daylight. No sound accompanied the coded message waiting there.
[BAIT ACTIVATED EARLY. PLAN MOVED FORWARD.]
One short line. No emotion.

His finger touched the screen to acknowledge it. No pop-up, no retained message history. Each action erased its access traces. Three seconds later, the message destroyed itself, the session closed and the operation records cleared.
He returned the phone beneath the pillow and lowered his arm onto the bedding.
A breeze through the window lifted the corner of the cream curtain, shifting light over the wall. He looked again toward the distant buildings, his expression unchanged.
He sat quietly, waiting for the failure about to unfold on the wasteland.
At the abandoned logistics site between the cities,
the wind had strengthened since morning. It swept fragments of grass over the open ground. A faint industrial-plastic smell had grown clearer, dry and sharp amid earth and weeds.

Jiang Chi lay in the shadow of a discarded truck, a monocular raised to his eye. He watched the gray box truck, now stopped on a level patch at the center. Its rear doors were half open. Heavy black sealed sacks were stacked inside, containing partly refined chemical material.
Officers waited behind cover around it, hands near their weapons, breathing quietly and watching the vehicle.
“The truck has stopped. No one out yet,” the observation officer reported. “Two people visible. Driver and passenger, still in the cab.”
“Keep watching,” Jiang Chi answered softly. “Wait until the handover starts. We need them with the goods.”
Everyone held still. Only grass rustled in the wind.
One minute. Two. Three.
Nothing moved at the rear doors.
Jiang Chi frowned and tightened his grip on the monocular.
“Something’s wrong. If this is a handover, they should be getting out to meet someone.”
As he spoke, a faint engine sounded toward the highway, rapidly fading into the distance.
His heart dropped.
“They’re gone!”
The words burst out. “Move in. Now!”
Officers rose from cover and rushed toward the truck, low and fast. Footsteps struck the cracked earth. In moments they covered the short distance and trained their weapons inside.
The vehicle was empty.
Only sealed black sacks and scattered packaging remained.
The people had disappeared.
Jiang Chi climbed into the rear and touched a sack. It was still slightly warm, recently placed there.
“They abandoned the truck and switched transport.” His voice was tight. “Spread out. Widen the search. Check every path for footprints and tire marks.”
The officers dispersed along all the branching routes.
They searched the grass and examined the dirt. Yet there were no fresh footprints and no clear bicycle or motorcycle tracks. The people leaving had deliberately cleared their traces.
“A short stretch of tire marks on the western path,” one officer reported on returning. “Then hard surfacing, and nothing. No witnesses. Not even scavengers nearby.”

Another spoke into his radio. “We’ve just retrieved footage from the eastern junction. Ten minutes ago, a black motorcycle without plates, two riders, left at speed. It entered the lanes on the urban fringe, then a camera blind spot. We lost it.”
Jiang Chi stood beside the truck, wind lifting his hair, helplessness pressing on his chest. Again. The target in sight, then gone, leaving goods as bait.
Lu Zheng arrived at a fast walk, crossing the scattered grass to the truck. He looked at the sacks and scanned the empty surroundings.
“Trace team here?”
“On the way. Within ten minutes.”
“Seal the whole area. Protect every item where it is,” he ordered. “Take samples and trace the source of the chemicals. Tell the checkpoints to watch for a black motorcycle with two riders.”
“Understood.”
Officers set up the cordon and waited for the technicians. Wind continued over the wasteland, lifting dust and humming through the metal sheds.

Lu Zheng stood inside the tape, looking toward the paths running in every direction. Their opponents seemed to know the timing and positions of the arrest in advance. He felt only anger and reluctant respect for their planning, convinced they possessed exceptional counter-investigation skills. He did not connect any of it to Shen Yu’an resting in a hospital bed.
Jiang Chi came beside him, his voice full of defeat.
“Missed them again. It’s as if they were warned. We were about to move, and they’d already abandoned the truck.”
“Anticipation, not coincidence,” Lu Zheng said slowly, frowning. “Old Ghost knows every escape route here. He had a plan to leave the cargo and withdraw. The materials were bait to hold us.”
“What now?”

“We keep watching.” Lu Zheng looked toward the distant mist. “If they’re putting out bait, they still have transactions to make. As long as materials must move, they’ll appear again. Adjust the rotations, add concealed positions and reduce our exposure.”
Jiang Chi nodded and went to pass on the orders.
The cordon shifted in the wind. Evidence bags sat on the ground as the chemical smell dispersed. A lead had surfaced only to break again.
Lu Zheng watched the weeds stretching into the distance. Failure weighed on him, but he retained hope. Keep watching long enough, and they would catch them.
No one imagined that the source of the flawless withdrawal sat quietly in a warm hospital room at the city’s center.
There, Shen Yu’an turned slightly toward the clock, counting the time for the teams to close in, discover the empty truck and search the grounds.
He raised his right hand and rested his fingertips lightly on the blanket. Sunlight moved slowly across the floor.
The call bell was still, the medication neatly arranged, the green scent unchanged. To anyone looking, this was an ordinary hospital room occupied by an injured forensic physician.
He waited for Lu Zheng to finish and return. For the next pull of a lead, the next police pursuit. The game advanced slowly. Hidden in the light, he watched others move through the mist.
The phone lay silently beneath his pillow.

alt.en: Investigators discover the abandoned gray cargo truck in the misty freight yard.
alt.zh: 刑侦队员在晨雾中的废弃货运场发现被丢下的灰色货车。

zh: 清晨，医院查房结束。
主治医生拿着检查报告，站在病床前简单交代了几句恢复注意事项，告知沈予安创口恢复稳定，没有发炎牵拉的情况，符合出院标准，后续只需要定期回院复查换药即可。
沈予安听完，点头应下。
等医生离开病房，他简单收拾了一下自己的东西。东西不多，只一个随身小包。
没过多久，陆峥推门走进病房。
他进门先看了一眼沈予安的状态，确认对方行动无碍，直接伸手接过沈予安手里的包。
“我去办手续，你在大厅等我。”
沈予安没有推辞，应声起身，跟着他走出病房。
医院大厅人很多，来往行人步履匆忙，各个窗口都排着长队。沈予安找了处空的长椅坐下，安静等候。
陆峥排队办理完所有出院流程，收好单据，很快回到他身边。
“可以走了。”
两人一同走出医院，坐车返回市局。
一路车程平稳，车里很安静，没人说话。回到刑侦大楼，刚走进办公区，队内几个值班的队员都抬眼看了过来，出声打招呼。
“沈法医回来了？”
“恢复得挺快啊。”
“这下总算归队了。”
几句问候，都是队内熟络的常态语气。
沈予安微微点头回应，态度算得上溫和。
江驰从会议室走出来，看到人，停下脚步。
“身体彻底没问题了？”
“没事了，后续只需要静养复查，不影响正常工作。”沈予安回答。
江驰嗯了一声，语气放松不少。
“刚好这几天队里没有紧急案子，荒滩那起河尸案的物证还在送检溯源，结果没这么快出。你刚出院，不用急着上手工作，先调整两天。”
这段时间本来就是办案空档期。
荒滩灭口案结束之后，所有现场物证、尸体样本、纸质证物，全部移交技术科做深度筛查。按照正常侦办流程，高端纸品溯源、加密墨水比对、特殊工艺排查、未知网络域名破译，都需要数天的工作周期，不可能短短一两天出结果。
全队这段时间的工作，基本以复盘旧案、整理卷宗、轮流休整为主。
沈予安回到自己工位，拉开椅子坐下，打开电脑。
办公区氛围松弛，有人整理笔录，有人轮流去食堂吃饭，有人趴在桌上补前一晚的夜班，跟前段時間高压办案的紧绷状态簡直天壤之別。
临近午后，技术科往队内工作群推送了一份数据提取回执。
回执内容很简单，是死者老鬼随身电子设备的初步筛查结果。
技术人员在老鬼的手机、平板和笔记本的深层缓存里，找到了大量重复的访问记录，全部指向同一个加密外文域名。域名是法文结构，层级极高，不属于任何公开网络平台，属于私密加密内部论坛。
队内几个人凑到电脑前查看。
没人认识这串字符，没人接触过这种层级的私密网络。
江驰看着屏幕上的加密域名，眉头微蹙。
“一个做底层原料中转的中间人，频繁登录这种私密暗网论坛，本身就很不正常。”
旁边队员接话。
“常规贩子只会用普通社交软件、匿名聊天工具交易，根本接触不到这种加密圈层论坛。而且三台设备全部有长期登录痕迹，不是误触，是固定访问。”
几人简单讨论了几句。
警員能审出来老鬼生前完整的交易轨迹、交接时间、出货地点、联络方式，口供清晰，细节完整。
但只要话题触及这个未知网络、背后关联人员、上级信息，所有线索直接卡死。
无论审讯人员如何询问，老鬼生前留存的所有审讯记录里，只要提到相关组织、网络背后的势力、上线身份，对方态度瞬间变得极度偏执狂热，闭口不谈半个字。
审讯人员反复试探多次，得到的反应一模一样。
是发自内心的盲从与崇拜，对背后未知的存在抱有近乎虔诚的信仰，宁死不肯泄露任何一丝相关信息。
队员看着屏幕，低声感慨。
“这种忠诚度，根本不是普通黑市团伙能培养出来的。”
“这群人的纪律性和洗脑手段，太夸张了。”
办公室里的讨论止于此处。
所有人的判断都只停留在外部。
对手是一支训练度极高、纪律极强、拥有成熟洗脑体系的高端犯罪组织，反侦察、清痕布局、人员管控全部专业到极致。
沈予安坐在工位上，看着群里的回执信息，神色平淡，和在场所有人的反应别无二致。
他安静看着屏幕，没有插话，正常跟进工作信息的状态。
午后时间缓缓过去。
队内工作节奏依旧松弛，没有紧急任务，突发警情。队员们轮班休息、吃饭、整理手头的卷宗材料，办公区维持着祥和的状态。
傍晚时分，天色慢慢暗下来。
办公室陆续有人下班离岗，人流渐渐变少。
陆峥处理完手里的工作，起身走到沈予安工位旁。
“今天不用加班，早点回去休息。伤口刚愈合，别劳累。”
沈予安抬眼看他。
“你也是，别熬得太晚。”
陆峥轻轻点头，没有立刻离开，站在桌边停了两秒。
办公区还有不少队员在，人多眼杂，他没有多余动作，只是语气里带着自然的偏袒，刻意给沈予安减负。
“接下来几天都轻松调整，案子等物证结果出来再说。”
说完，他才转身收拾东西，准备下班。
办公区的灯光亮着，暖白光铺满桌面。
剩下的人各自忙着自己的收尾工作，没人察觉任何异常。
整支队伍依旧沉浸在短暂的休整期里，所有人的注意力，全部放在等待物证溯源、等待网络破译、等待外部线索突破上。
安市的初秋总是裹着一层温和的暖意，褪去了盛夏的燥热，也未染深冬的寒凉，整座城市的节奏都趋于平缓。连续三日，全市治安状况稳定，没有突发恶性警情，街头巷尾的巡防记录清一色平稳如常，市局刑侦大队终于从连轴转的紧绷状态里抽离出来，进入了难得的休整复盘空档期。
经历过荒滩废弃货厢交易、河道灭口弃尸、黑金信封留字的连环诡异事件后，整支专案组的神经始终悬在半空，哪怕暂时无案可查，所有人也都下意识保持着警惕，没有任何人彻底松懈。只是受制于刑侦工作的客观规律，高端私密纸品溯源、加密法文暗网域名破译、特殊墨水成分比对、尸体毒物精细化筛查，這些只有後面兩個有了突破
沈予安彻底归队的这三天，作息尚且規律，枪伤带来的创口损伤还处在恢复期，哪怕医生明确告知不影响正常内勤工作，队内所有人也都下意识对他多了几分包容与照顾，没人安排高强度外勤，让他熬夜加班，所有繁重琐碎的工作都被其余队员默默分担。
这份特殊的优待里，尤以陆峥的偏袒最为直白，不加遮掩，明目张胆，落在朝夕相处的细碎日常里，人人看在眼里，還時常被小警員在角落偷笑。
清晨八点整，刑侦大队办公区准时到岗。阳光透过双层隔音玻璃窗平铺而入，均匀洒在整齐排列的办公桌面上，驱散了室内晨间残留的微凉，将整片办公区衬得明亮通透。队员们陆续打卡到岗，换好制式工作服，整理桌面文件、开启办公设备、对接昨日遗留工作，细碎的脚步声、键盘敲击声、低声交流的说话声交织在一起，构成了刑侦队独有的安稳日常。
沈予安准时走入办公区，一身干净规整的制服穿戴整齐，领口纽扣扣合妥当，袖口平整贴合手腕，没有丝毫凌乱。因为左肩枪伤尚未完全愈合，他穿戴衣物的动作会刻意放缓，避开左臂大幅度发力，细微的克制动作不显眼，却始终贯穿在他所有的行为里。他的面色依旧带着一丝大病初愈的清浅苍白，眉眼温顺沉静，行走间身姿挺拔端正，没有孱弱颓靡的姿态，只是周身气质温软平和，自带一种让人下意识想要呵护的柔软感。
他径直走到自己的法医专属工位前，单手拉开座椅，动作轻稳，全程依靠右手发力，左肩始终保持放松固定的状态。落座后，他有条不紊地开启电脑、整理昨日归档的勘验记录、核对留存的物证登记台账
陆峥几乎是和他前后脚到岗。
作为刑侦队队长，他常年保持着提前到岗的习惯，今日也依旧提早十分钟抵达，提前梳理好了当日的工作安排。他刚把随身的工作笔记本放在桌面，目光便下意识越过办公桌群，精准落在沈予安的身影上。
视线停留的片刻，他仔细观察着对方的状态，确认沈予安行动自如、神色安稳，没有创口不适的疲惫姿态，心底悄然悬着的那一丝担忧，才缓缓落定。
连日以来的牵挂与顾虑，早已在日复一日的陪护与相处中，变成了刻在本能里的在意。陆峥自己也清晰察觉，对沈予安的关照早已超出了队内同事、上下级的范畴，是独一份的偏爱与特殊对待
办公区人多繁杂，队员们各司其职、忙碌不休，没人刻意关注两人之间的细微互动，但这份明目张胆的偏袒，早已是队内公开的默契。
上午的工作平淡有序，没有突发状况，没有紧急任务。
一部分人集中复盘荒滩河道藏尸案的所有现场细节，一遍遍回看执法记录仪录像、核对现场照片、梳理死者生前的行动轨迹与交易脉络；一部分人整理近三年安市及周边城市发生的仪式化、高智商无痕犯罪卷宗，试图寻找可以并案的相似线索；剩余内勤人员则专注于台账更新、物证对接、报告汇总，各司其职，井然有序。
沈予安的工作重心放在法医勘验资料的梳理与归档上。
荒滩死者老鬼的尸检报告已经初步成型，基础死因、毒物种类、体表特征、体内损伤数据全部核验完毕，只差技术科最终的微量毒物溯源结果，即可正式定稿归档。他坐在工位上，逐字逐句核对报告数据，修正细节偏差，调整专业表述，神情专注认真，眉眼沉静温柔。
长时间久坐让身体难免僵硬，临近上午十点，沈予安微微挺直脊背，想要抬手舒展肩颈，缓解久坐带来的酸胀感。
他下意识抬起左臂，肩头肌肉刚刚轻微牵拉，胸腔侧边的创口位置立刻传来一阵细密的酸胀钝痛，不算剧烈，却足够清晰，瞬间牵制住了他所有的动作。
沈予安的动作骤然顿住，指尖悬在半空，微微蹙了蹙眉，极其细微的不适感掠过眼底。他没有出声，只是缓缓收回左臂，重新放平坐姿，打算靠轻微转动脖颈缓解僵硬。
可这转瞬即逝的细微动作，還是被不远处的陆峥精准捕捉。
陆峥原本正低头核对手中的卷宗台账，视线余光扫到他停滞的动作与微蹙的眉眼，几乎没有半秒犹豫，当即放下手中的文件，起身迈步走了过去。
沉稳的脚步声由远及近，落在安静的办公区里，清晰却不突兀。
周遭忙碌的队员各自专注手头工作，无人留意这一幕，唯有沈予安察觉到身前落下的阴影，抬眸的瞬间，刚好对上陆峥沉敛温柔的眼眸。
“伤口不舒服？”陆峥站在他身侧，俯身压低声音询问，语气里带着独有的细致与关切，音量控制在两人可闻的范围，不打扰旁人工作，却极尽温柔稳妥。
沈予安微微摇头，眉眼舒展，恢复了温顺柔和的模样，语气轻浅温和：“还好，就是坐太久僵住了，刚刚抬手忘了伤口还没完全好。”
他的解释坦然真诚，带着一点恰到好处的笨拙与无奈，却自然而然流露出身体未愈的不便，分寸拿捏得恰到好处。
陆峥垂眸看着他依旧不敢大幅发力的左肩，眼底的温柔又沉了几分，不容置喙的语气带着专属的纵容：“别勉强自己，刚出院三天，软组织还在恢复期，不能久坐更不能逞强。”
话音落下，他目光扫过沈予安桌面堆积的厚重卷宗与待核对报告，伸手直接将最上方一摞厚重的档案资料挪到自己手边。
“这些重活、整理归档的粗活不用你碰，我让其他人过来处理。你起来走动两分钟，活动一下腰背，别一直坐着。”
沈予安抬头望着他，眼底漾着浅浅的歉意，温顺又礼貌：“不用这么麻烦的陆队，我稍微注意一点就可以，不用特意让别人替我干活。”
“听话。”
陆峥只淡淡两个字，温柔却有力，没有给对方推辞的余地。
这两个字带着长久相处养成的默契与纵容，像无形的温水，轻轻裹住所有的距离感与疏离感。
沈予安看着他认真坚持的模样，没有再继续推辞，顺从地点了点头，唇角带着浅淡温顺的笑意：“那辛苦你了。”
他的顺从，恰到好处的柔软，却总能精准戳中陆峥心底最软的地方。
他缓缓起身，按照陆峥的叮嘱，在工位旁轻轻走动，动作舒缓轻柔，避开左肩所有发力动作，姿态温顺乖巧。
陆峥转头抬手，对着不远处整理卷宗的年轻队员招了招手，简单交代两句，将沈予安桌面上的厚重归档工作全数移交出去，彻底替他减负。
年轻队员早已习以为常，八卦的笑了笑轉身去默默完成交接。在所有人心里，沈予安体弱温柔、刚从重伤里恢复，陆队长偏爱照顾本就是理所应当的事情，早已成为队内无需言说的共识。
沈予安缓步走在办公区的过道里，慢慢舒展腰背，目光随意扫过窗外的街景，神色平和淡然。
眼底温顺柔和的表象之下，是一片毫无波澜的沉静。
队内所有人都沉浸在日常的安稳里，所有人都将所有疑点、所有警惕、所有戒备，全部对准外部那个神秘的高端犯罪组织。
大家忌惮对方极致专业的反侦察手段、恐惧对方冷血果断的灭口方式、惊叹对方高端精致的犯罪载体、忌惮对方近乎变态的人员洗脑管控体系。
两分钟后，沈予安缓步走回工位，重新落座。
陆峥依旧站在他身侧，低声叮嘱：“以后觉得累了、不舒服了，直接休息，不用硬撑工作。队里不缺你这一时半会的工作进度，你的身体最重要。”
“我知道了。”沈予安抬眸看他，眼神澄澈温顺，乖乖应声，“我会注意的。”
简单的对话落幕，陆峥才转身回到自己的办公桌前。
只是落座之后，他的目光依旧会时不时不经意地扫向斜前方的身影，视线停留的频率远超对待任何一位队员。心底的牵挂、偏爱、心疼层层堆叠，愈发深重，在无人察觉的角落肆意蔓延。
一整个上午，办公区的工作始终平稳推进，没有任何波澜。
技术科每隔两个小时，就会在队内专属工作群推送一次物证溯源的进度更新，内容大多是数据拆解、成分筛查、域名破译的阶段性进展，没有实质性的线索突破。
队内队员闲暇之余，会低声讨论几句案件的诡异之处，所有讨论的方向，全部围绕外部组织展开。
有人感慨对方的清痕手段太过完美，几乎做到了现场无痕；有人疑惑对方的圈层门槛极高，底层贩子根本无从接触；有人畏惧对方的洗脑能力，能让普通底层人员拥有宁死不叛的绝对忠诚。
临近正午十二点，下班打卡的提示音准时响起，忙碌一上午的队员们陆续放下手头工作，结伴收拾东西，准备前往食堂就餐。
队内的氛围彻底放松下来，喧闹的谈笑声慢慢响起，驱散了一上午的工作沉静。
江驰合上手里厚厚的卷宗，伸了个懒腰，转头看向收拾东西的陆峥和沈予安，随口出声邀约：“一起去食堂？今天食堂加了菜，清淡菜品不少，刚好适合沈法医养身体。”
陆峥看向身侧的沈予安，下意识征询他的意愿。
沈予安轻轻点头：“可以，一起吧。”
三人并肩跟着大部队走出办公区，顺着楼梯下楼，朝着市局食堂的方向走去。
楼道里人流密集，队员们三三两两结伴而行，聊着日常琐事、排班休息、近期天气，氛围轻松热闹，彻底褪去了办案时的紧绷肃穆。
食堂大厅宽敞明亮，窗口菜品摆放整齐，荤素搭配齐全，热气腾腾的饭菜香气弥漫在整片空间里。就餐的民警、辅警、后勤人员来来往往，人声嘈杂，烟火气十足。
沈予安端着餐盘，刻意挑选了几样清淡软烂、少油少盐的菜品，贴合术后恢复期的饮食要求，没有辛辣、没有油腻，简单规整。
陆峥跟在他身侧，目光扫过他餐盘里的菜式，确认都是易消化的清淡口味，心底的顾虑悄然放下。他下意识走在沈予安外侧，替他隔开往来拥挤的人流，避免有人走动磕碰。
几人找了一处靠窗的长条餐桌落座，宽敞通风，视野开阔。
刚坐下，旁边几名年轻队员便顺势凑过来，围坐在一起，边吃饭边闲聊，话题自然而然绕回了悬而未决的荒滩灭口案。
“技术科那边的破译还是卡住了，那串法文暗网域名太难啃了，根本找不到突破口。”
“正常，这种私人高端圈层的私密论坛，本身就不对外公开，加密等级是顶级的，哪有那么容易攻破。”
“最让人摸不透的还是那群执行者，审讯的时候太反常了，作案过程、时间、地点、手法、交易细节，问什么答什么，清清楚楚、一丝不漏，可只要沾到组织相关的东西，立刻闭口不谈，态度偏执到吓人。”
一名年轻队员放下筷子，语气满是费解与凝重：“我审过不少团伙罪犯，贪财的、怕死的、抱团的、内讧的什么样的都有，就是很少見这种。是明知道一切，却心甘情愿死守秘密，把那个组织当成信仰一样供奉，宁死不卖、宁死不叛。”
这话一出，桌边几人纷纷点头附和。
“这种忠诚度绝对是系统性洗脑、长期管控、严格驯化出来的，普通黑市松散团伙根本做不到。”
“而且对方审美、格局、布局、手段全部在线，留的那张黑金信封、手写英文卡片，精致，完全不像凶徒会有的东西。”
“感觉我们面对的根本不是普通罪犯，是一群受过高等教育、高端训练、有审美、有纪律、有信仰的专业犯罪人员。”
众人你一言我一语，层层剖析对手的恐怖之处。
陆峥安静听着众人的讨论，低头慢条斯理吃着饭菜，神色沉静，没有多言，心底的凝重却一点点沉淀加深。
他比任何人都清楚这起案件的诡异与棘手。
从最初的精准预判警方行动、完美弃货脱身，到冷血果断灭口弃尸、不留活口，再到极致优雅的仪式化留讯，每一步布局都精准、冷静、长远，完全碾压安市以往所有刑事案件的层级。
这绝对是一个成熟、庞大、精密、恐怖的高端犯罪组织。
全程安静就餐的沈予安，始终默默听着众人的分析，眉眼温顺，神色淡然，偶尔会轻轻点头附和，姿态和在场所有队员别无二致，一样的警惕、一样的凝重、一样的探究。
他沒有主动搭话，完美融入团队。
餐桌间的闲谈持续了半个多小时，众人吃完午饭，收拾好餐盘，结伴走出食堂。
午后的阳光更加温暖柔和，晒在身上暖意融融，驱散了初秋的微凉。
大部分队员吃完饭后，都会回到办公区短暂午休，缓解一上午的疲惫，为下午的工作储备精力。
回到刑侦办公区，大半队员纷纷趴在工位上小憩，原本热闹的办公区迅速安静下来，只剩下微弱的呼吸声与窗外轻柔的风声。
沈予安没有午休的习惯，回到工位后，他继续翻看尸检报告的细节资料。
陆峥也没有休息，坐在办公桌前，指尖轻点桌面，脑海里反复复盘荒滩案件的所有细节，试图从密密麻麻的线索里找到被忽略的突破口。
他的目光总会不由自主飘向斜前方安静伏案的身影，视线落下时，眼底所有的凝重与警惕，都会悄然化作温柔的柔软。
看着沈予安安静认真、温顺乖巧的模样，陆峥心底的偏爱与心疼愈发深重。
对方舍身替自己挡枪的画面，无数次在脑海里回放，那一瞬间的果敢与决绝，让他这辈子都无法释怀，也让他心甘情愿，一次次打破自己的原则与底线，给予对方独一无二、不加遮掩的偏爱。
整整一个午后，办公区始终维持着安静松弛的休整状态，无警情、无外勤、无突发线索突破，一切都平稳如常。
下午三点左右，午休结束，队员们陆续苏醒，揉着眉眼恢复工作状态，办公区重新响起错落的键盘声与低声交流声。
技术科再次推送最新进度，依旧是常规数据筛查进展，没有任何实质性突破，暗网域名依旧无法破译，纸品溯源暂时没有匹配结果，毒物筛查还在精细化比对阶段。
漫长的等待，是刑侦工作的常态。
临近傍晚六点，夕阳西垂，暖橙色的霞光铺满整片玻璃窗，将办公区染成一层温柔的橘色。
一天的工作即将收尾，队内依旧无任何突发警情，所有人都以为，今日依旧会是安稳休整、静待线索突破的平静一日。
就在队员们陆续收拾东西、准备准时下班休整的时候，刑侦大队的接警座机，骤然尖锐地响了起来。
急促的铃声划破办公区的宁静，穿透力极强，瞬间让所有人心头一紧，瞬间驱散了一日的松弛。
正在整理卷宗的队员动作一顿，准备起身离岗的脚步纷纷停下，所有人的目光同时落在值班室的座机上。
值班队员立刻快步上前，迅速接起电话，神色从放松快速转为凝重。
电话听筒贴在耳边，他安静听着对面急促的报案叙述，眉心一点点拧紧，面色愈发严肃，指尖无意识攥紧了听筒。
短短数十秒，他快速记录下地址、案情、现场特征，挂断电话的瞬间，立刻抬头面向全队，高声通报紧急警情。
“紧急出警！城郊艺术雕塑公园！园区中心大型城市雕塑内部，被保洁人员发现藏匿人体残骸，疑似恶性藏尸命案！现场形态诡异，疑似刻意摆放的仪式化现场！”
话音落下的瞬间，原本趋于平静的办公区，瞬间紧绷到极致。
所有队员瞬间收敛所有松懈姿态，神色肃穆，动作迅速，立刻转身奔赴装备区，领取警帽、执法记录仪、勘验设备、抓捕器械。
连日休整的平静被骤然打破，新的、属于神秘组织的艺术凶案，毫无预兆地拉开了序幕。
陆峥身形瞬间站起，周身温柔松弛的气场尽数褪去，取而代之的是刑侦队长独有的凌厉与冷肃。
他目光快速扫过全队，语速沉稳有力，快速下达出警指令：“全员紧急集结！勘验组、外勤组、走访组分组行动！穿戴装备，立刻出发！”
指令落地，全队行动整齐划一，没有半分拖沓。
话音落下的瞬间，陆峥的目光第一时间精准锁定沈予安，凌厉的眼底瞬间掺进一丝克制的担忧，语气也下意识放缓：“你伤势未愈，不用跟进本次外勤，留守队里待命，等待我们现场反馈。”
他第一时间下意识将最安稳、最轻松的位置留给沈予安。
全队紧急出警，外勤路途遥远、现场未知、环境复杂、需要长时间站立勘验、随时可能出现突发状况，他绝不允许刚刚恢复的沈予安勉强逞强，再次牵扯伤口。
周围队员都默认这个安排，在大家眼里，沈予安的身体状态，确实不适合奔赴未知的凶案现场。
可话音落下，沈予安却轻轻摇了摇头，主动拿起工位旁的法医专属勘验包，单手背在肩上，动作稳妥从容。
他抬眸看向陆峥，眉眼温顺柔和，眼底带着浅浅的坚持，语气顺从却坚定，只是温柔地想要并肩同行。
“陆队，我可以跟进现场。伤口只是不能剧烈发力、不能负重，常规的现场勘验、痕迹排查完全不受影响。队里勘验人手刚好齐全，我跟着过去，现场研判会更精准，不会耽误工作，也不会牵扯伤口。”
他语气平和真诚，只是温柔地阐述事实，给出合理稳妥的理由。
温顺的姿态，恰到好处的懂事，恰到好处的坚持，恰到好处的并肩心意。
陆峥看着他澄澈温柔的眼眸，看着他认真恳切的模样，拒绝的话卡在喉间，迟迟无法说出口。
他太了解沈予安的性子，温顺却有韧性，温柔却不怯懦，对待工作始终认真负责，从不会因为私人身体原因推脱本职工作。
心底的担忧与顾虑，最终败给了心底的纵容与偏爱。
几秒的沉默后，陆峥微微松口，语气带着极致的妥协与叮嘱：“可以跟着，但全程寸步不离我身边。不许弯腰、不许抬手发力、不许独自走动勘验、不许勉强自己。一旦有任何不舒服，立刻告诉我。”
字字句句，皆是专属的呵护与牵挂。
“好。”沈予安弯眸应声，眼底漾开浅淡温柔，乖乖点头应下，“我都听你的。”
简单的四个字，温顺乖巧，彻底抚平了陆峥心底最后的顾虑。
两人一前一后，跟着大部队快步走出办公区，奔赴楼下警车停放区域。
三辆警用车辆快速启动，车灯亮起，警笛低鸣，依次驶出市局大院，朝着城郊艺术雕塑公园的方向疾驰而去。
傍晚的城市车流渐缓，晚高峰临近尾声，路面通行顺畅。警车一路拉着警笛，匀速穿梭在城市主干道上，快速远离市区繁华地带，朝着城郊空旷的生态园区疾驰。
四十分钟的车程，车内氛围肃穆安静。
外勤队员坐在前排，低声梳理着已知的现场信息，提前预判案情走向、规划抵达后的排查分工、预想可能出现的现场状况。
后排位置，陆峥与沈予安并肩而坐，空间安静狭小。
车厢轻微颠簸，风声与警笛声隔着车窗隐约传来，隔绝了外界所有的嘈杂。
路途过半，车辆途经一处路面减速带，车身骤然剧烈颠簸了一下，整台车体顺势轻微晃动。
沈予安没有抓扶手，身体随着车身惯性轻轻一晃，重心偏移，肩头毫无防备地轻轻靠上了陆峥
温热的衣料相贴，触感轻柔，距离瞬间拉近到极致。
只是极短暂的一瞬，失衡的身体很快被沈予安稳住，他立刻端正坐姿，微微侧头，对着身侧的陆峥轻声致歉，语气温顺有礼：“不好意思，刚刚没坐稳。”
可就是这一瞬不经意的近身触碰，却让车厢内的氛围悄然柔软下来。
陆峥侧头看着他温顺致歉的模样，眼底的冷肃彻底褪去，只剩下温柔的纵容。
他声音压得极低，只有两人能够听见，语气温柔缱绻：“没事，路途远，颠簸难免。累了就靠着歇一会，不用硬撑。”
沈予安抬眸看了他一眼，轻轻点头，没有推辞，安静靠在椅背上，眼帘轻轻垂下，姿态温顺安然。
眼底一片漠然沉静。
他清晰知晓，这场突如其来的雕塑藏尸案，只是遊戲的開始。
La Rose Éternelle组织正式开启的第一桩完整艺术仪式化凶案，是十二部门连环大案的正式开篇，是棋局铺开的第一枚落子。
现场会有精心雕琢的仪式布局、极致规整的艺术美感、被彻底驯化洗脑、对组织与顶层神明极致狂热崇拜的执行者。
警方耗费数日时间，走访排查、现场勘验、物证筛查、监控溯源，一步步艰难锁定执行者、抓捕归案、审讯复盘，历经三四天的漫长侦办，彻底破获此案。
最终只能从执行者的电子设备里，抓取到更多零碎的暗网访问痕迹，一点点拼凑出那个庞大神秘组织的冰山一角。
前路迷雾层层堆叠，风浪缓缓翻涌。
整车警力满心警惕、满心探究、满心凝重，奔赴一场精心布置的黑暗棋局。
而执棋之人，就安稳坐在人群之中，温顺沉静，温柔无害，陪着他们一同奔赴自己布下的棋局。
警车持续疾驰，晚风透过车窗缝隙吹入车内，拂动细碎的发丝。
明暗对峙的棋局，新的篇章，已然稳稳落定。
en: Morning rounds had ended.

The attending doctor stood beside the bed with the examination results and briefly explained the remaining precautions. Shen Yu’an’s wound was stable, without inflammation or strain. He met the discharge criteria and would only need regular follow-up visits and dressing changes.
Shen Yu’an listened and nodded.
Once the doctor left, he gathered his belongings. There was little to pack, only a small personal bag.
Soon afterward, Lu Zheng entered.
He first checked Shen Yu’an’s condition. Seeing that he could move without difficulty, he took the bag directly from his hand.
“I’ll handle the paperwork. Wait in the lobby.”
Shen Yu’an did not object. He rose and followed him out.
The hospital lobby was busy, people hurrying past and long lines at every counter. Shen Yu’an found an empty bench and waited quietly.
Lu Zheng completed the discharge procedures, put away the documents and returned quickly.
“We can go.”
They left together and drove back to the municipal bureau.
The journey was smooth and silent. When they entered the criminal investigation offices, several officers on duty looked up and greeted them.
“Dr. Shen, you’re back?”
“That was a quick recovery.”
“Good to have you with us again.”
A few familiar greetings, in the team’s usual manner.
Shen Yu’an nodded in response, his attitude mild.
Jiang Chi came out of the meeting room and stopped when he saw him.
“Everything all right now?”
“Yes. Rest and follow-up checks from here. It won’t affect ordinary work,” Shen Yu’an replied.
Jiang Chi nodded, noticeably relieved.

“Good timing. No urgent new cases these past few days. The evidence from the river-body case on the wasteland is still being tested and traced. That won’t come back quickly. You’ve just left hospital. Take a couple of days to settle in before getting buried in work.”
This was a natural pause in the investigation.

After the killing and disposal on the wasteland, all scene evidence, body samples and paper exhibits had gone to the technical section for deeper examination. Tracing specialty paper, comparing encrypted ink, examining unusual manufacturing techniques and deciphering an unknown online domain all took days. Results could not appear in one or two.
For now, the team mainly reviewed earlier cases, organized files and rotated periods of rest.
Shen Yu’an returned to his workstation, pulled out the chair and started his computer.
The office was relaxed. Some officers sorted interview records, some took turns going to the canteen, and others slept at their desks after night duty. It was a world apart from the recent pressure.
Around early afternoon, the technical section posted a data-recovery receipt to the team’s work group.
It was brief: preliminary findings from the late Old Ghost’s electronic devices.

Deep in the caches of his phone, tablet and laptop, technicians had found many repeated visits to the same encrypted foreign-language domain. Its structure was French and its access level extremely restricted. It belonged to no public platform, but to a private encrypted forum.
Several officers gathered at a computer.
None recognized the string or had encountered a private network at this level.
Jiang Chi frowned at the domain on the screen.
“A low-level materials intermediary regularly visiting a private dark-web forum like this is abnormal in itself.”
An officer beside him agreed.
“Ordinary dealers use common social apps or anonymous messaging. They don’t get into closed circles like this. And all three devices show long-term access. Not an accidental click. Regular visits.”
They discussed it briefly.
Investigators had been able to obtain Old Ghost’s complete trading history, handover times, delivery sites and contact methods while he was alive. His account was clear and detailed.
But any question touching the unknown network, its associates or those above him brought everything to a halt.
In every surviving interview, mention of the organization, the power behind the network or the identity of his superiors made him intensely obsessive and fervent. He would say nothing.
Repeated attempts produced exactly the same response.
It was genuine submission and worship, an almost devout faith in something unknown behind him. He would die rather than reveal it.
Looking at the screen, an officer spoke quietly.
“No ordinary illicit-market group produces loyalty like that.”
“Their discipline and conditioning are extraordinary.”
The office discussion stopped there.
Everyone’s judgment remained directed outward.

They faced a sophisticated criminal organization: highly trained, rigorously disciplined, with an established system of indoctrination. Its evasion, removal of evidence and control of personnel were all exceptionally professional.
At his desk, Shen Yu’an read the receipt in the group chat. His expression was unremarkable, no different from anyone else’s.
He watched without joining the discussion, simply following a work update.
The afternoon passed slowly.
The team’s pace remained easy. No urgent assignment, no unexpected call. Officers rested in rotation, ate and organized their files. The office stayed peaceful.
Toward evening, the sky darkened.
People began leaving, and the room gradually emptied.
Lu Zheng finished his work and went to Shen Yu’an’s desk.
“No overtime today. Go home early. The wound has only just healed. Don’t exhaust yourself.”
Shen Yu’an looked up.
“You too. Don’t stay too late.”
Lu Zheng nodded but remained for another two seconds.
There were still plenty of colleagues around. He made no unnecessary gesture, but the preference in his voice was natural as he deliberately eased Shen Yu’an’s workload.
“Take the next few days lightly. We’ll deal with the case when the evidence results arrive.”
Only then did he turn away to collect his things.
Warm-white office light spread across the desks.
Those remaining finished their own tasks. No one noticed anything unusual.
The team stayed absorbed in its brief respite, attention fixed on tracing evidence, deciphering the network and waiting for an external breakthrough.

Early autumn in An’an held a mild warmth, without summer’s heat or winter’s chill. The city’s pace seemed slower. For three days, public order remained stable. No sudden violent incidents; patrol reports from every street were routine. The municipal criminal investigation team finally stepped out of its relentless schedule into a rare interval of rest and review.

After the strange sequence of the abandoned truck transaction, the river disposal and the message in a black-and-gold envelope, their nerves had never fully settled. Even without an immediate case to pursue, everyone remained alert. But the work had its own pace: tracing exclusive paper, deciphering a French dark-web domain, comparing unusual ink and conducting fine toxicology screens. Only the latter two had yielded progress.

For the three days since his return, Shen Yu’an kept fairly regular hours. The gunshot wound was still healing. Though cleared for ordinary office duties, he received extra consideration from everyone. No demanding fieldwork or late nights; others quietly shared the heavy and tedious tasks.
Lu Zheng’s preference was the clearest. Open and undisguised, it appeared in small daily moments everyone saw, prompting the younger officers to laugh privately in corners.

At eight each morning, the office came to work. Sunlight entered through double-glazed windows and spread evenly across the rows of desks, dispelling the last morning chill. Officers arrived, changed into uniform, arranged papers, started equipment and picked up unfinished work. Footsteps, typing and low conversation formed the steady rhythm peculiar to the team.

Shen Yu’an arrived on time, his uniform neat, collar fastened and cuffs smooth against his wrists. With his left shoulder not fully healed, he dressed slowly and avoided force through that arm. The restraint was unobtrusive but present in every movement. His face retained a faint recovering pallor. He walked upright, without a defeated or frail bearing, yet his quiet gentleness invited care.

He went straight to his forensic workstation and pulled out the chair with his right hand, keeping the left shoulder relaxed and still. Once seated, he started the computer, organized the previous day’s examination records and checked the evidence register.
Lu Zheng arrived almost alongside him.

He habitually came early and had reached the bureau ten minutes before the official start, with the day’s work already organized. As soon as he set down his notebook, his eyes found Shen Yu’an across the desks.
He watched long enough to confirm easy movement, a settled expression and no sign of wound-related distress. Only then did his quiet worry ease.
Days of care and companionship had made the concern instinctive. Lu Zheng knew it had gone beyond colleagues or hierarchy. This was a particular affection, a special treatment.
The busy office gave no one much reason to watch their small exchanges, but the open preference had long become an unspoken understanding.
The morning was orderly and uneventful. No sudden incident, no urgent task.

Some officers repeatedly reviewed the wasteland and river-body scenes, watching body-camera footage, checking photographs and reconstructing the dead man’s movements and transactions. Others examined three years of ritualized, sophisticated crimes with few traces in An’an and neighboring cities, seeking similarities that might connect cases. Administrative staff updated registers, coordinated evidence and compiled reports.
Shen Yu’an concentrated on organizing and archiving forensic material.

Old Ghost’s preliminary autopsy report was complete. Cause of death, toxin type, external features and internal injuries had all been checked. Only the technical section’s final trace-toxicology findings remained before formal filing. Shen Yu’an reviewed every word and figure, correcting small discrepancies and refining the professional language with quiet attention.
By nearly ten, prolonged sitting had stiffened him. He straightened slightly and tried to stretch his shoulder and neck.
Instinctively, he lifted the left arm. The first pull of muscle sent a dull ache through the wound near the side of his chest. Not severe, but clear enough to stop the movement.

His fingers paused in the air. He frowned faintly, discomfort passing through his eyes. Without a sound, he lowered the arm and settled again, intending to ease the stiffness by gently turning his neck.
Lu Zheng noticed even that brief movement.
He had been checking files, but caught the pause and tightened brow at the edge of his vision. Without hesitation, he set down the papers and stood.
His steady footsteps approached, clear but unobtrusive in the quiet office.
The others remained occupied. Shen Yu’an noticed the shadow fall beside him and looked up into Lu Zheng’s restrained, gentle gaze.
“The wound bothering you?” Lu Zheng leaned slightly closer and kept his voice between them, attentive without disturbing anyone else.
Shen Yu’an shook his head, his face smoothing. “Not really. Just stiff from sitting too long. I forgot it hadn’t healed when I lifted my arm.”
The explanation was open and sincere, with just enough awkwardness and helplessness to reveal the inconvenience of recovery naturally.

Lu Zheng looked at the shoulder he still could not use freely. His voice was firm but indulgent. “Don’t push yourself. You’ve only been out three days. The tissue is still healing. No sitting for hours, and no pretending you’re fine.”
He glanced over the heavy files and reports on the desk, then moved the top stack toward himself.
“You don’t need to handle the heavy sorting and filing. I’ll have someone take it. Get up for two minutes. Ease your back. Don’t stay in the chair.”
Shen Yu’an looked at him apologetically. “You don’t need to go to so much trouble. I can be careful. There’s no need to make someone else do my work.”
“Listen to me.”
Quiet words, gentle but firm, leaving no room for refusal.
They carried the familiarity and indulgence built over time, softening the distance between them.
Seeing his insistence, Shen Yu’an stopped objecting. He nodded, a faint smile on his lips. “Then thank you.”
His compliance, that precisely measured softness, always reached the most vulnerable place in Lu Zheng.
He rose slowly and walked beside the desks as instructed, avoiding any strain on the left shoulder.
Lu Zheng called over a younger officer organizing files and briefly arranged the transfer of the heavy archiving work, removing it entirely from Shen Yu’an’s desk.

The officer was accustomed to this. He gave a knowing smile and quietly handled the handover. Everyone regarded Shen Yu’an as gentle and still recovering from serious injury. Lu Zheng’s care seemed natural, requiring no explanation.
Shen Yu’an walked slowly along the office aisle, easing his back and glancing at the street outside, his face peaceful.
Beneath that mild expression lay an undisturbed stillness.
Everyone remained absorbed in the steadiness of daily work. All doubt, vigilance and suspicion pointed outward, toward the mysterious, sophisticated criminal organization.
They feared its professional evasion and decisive silencing of people, marveled at the refined objects it used, and worried over its extreme conditioning and control of members.
Two minutes later, Shen Yu’an returned to his desk.
Lu Zheng still stood beside it. “If you’re tired or uncomfortable, rest. Don’t force yourself to work. The team can manage without a little extra progress from you. Your health comes first.”
“I understand.” Shen Yu’an looked up with clear, mild eyes. “I’ll be careful.”
Only then did Lu Zheng return to his own desk.
Once seated, he still glanced toward the figure diagonally ahead far more often than toward anyone else. Concern, preference and tenderness deepened, spreading through the places he left unexamined.
The whole morning proceeded without disturbance.
Every two hours, the technical section sent an update to the team’s group. Mostly stages of data analysis, composition tests and work on the domain. No substantive breakthrough.
In spare moments, officers discussed the case’s strange features. Every conversation centered on the external organization.

Some marveled at nearly traceless scenes. Others wondered at the closed circle ordinary dealers could not reach. Others feared a conditioning system that made low-level members willing to die rather than betray it.
Near noon, the shift-break alert sounded. Officers put down their work and prepared to go to the canteen together.
Conversation and laughter returned, breaking the morning’s quiet.
Jiang Chi closed a thick file and stretched. He looked toward Lu Zheng and Shen Yu’an. “Canteen? They’ve added dishes today. Plenty of light options. Good for Dr. Shen’s recovery.”
Lu Zheng instinctively looked to Shen Yu’an for his preference.
Shen Yu’an nodded. “Yes. Let’s go.”
The three joined the others, walking downstairs toward the bureau canteen.
The corridor was crowded with small groups discussing routines, shifts and weather. The severity of casework had given way to easy conversation.

The dining hall was spacious and bright, its counters neatly stocked with meat and vegetables. Steam and the smell of hot food filled the room. Police officers, auxiliary staff and support workers moved through the lively noise.
Shen Yu’an deliberately chose soft, mild dishes with little oil or salt, suited to recovery. Nothing spicy or greasy. A simple, orderly selection.
Lu Zheng stayed beside him, checking the tray and relaxing when he saw the light food. Without thinking, he walked on the outside, shielding him from the crowd and accidental bumps.
They found a long table by the window, with room and fresh air.
A few younger officers joined them, eating and talking. The conversation naturally returned to the unresolved wasteland killing.
“The technical section is still stuck. That French dark-web domain is hard to crack. No opening.”
“Of course. A private forum for an exclusive circle isn’t public in the first place. The encryption’s at the highest level. It won’t be easy.”

“What I can’t understand is the operatives. In interviews they’ll answer everything about the crimes—times, places, methods, transactions. Clear and complete. But mention the organization and they close down. Terrifyingly obsessive.”

One young officer set down his chopsticks. “I’ve questioned plenty of group offenders. Greedy ones, frightened ones, loyal ones, people turning on each other. Hardly ever this. They know everything and willingly guard it. They worship the organization like a faith. Die rather than sell it out, die rather than betray it.”
Several heads nodded.
“That takes systematic indoctrination, long-term control and strict conditioning. A loose illicit-market group couldn’t do it.”
“And everything about them—the taste, scale, planning, methods. That black-and-gold envelope, the handwritten English card. Refined. Not what you expect from violent criminals.”
“It feels like we’re facing highly educated, trained professionals with taste, discipline and belief.”
One after another, they examined what made the adversary frightening.
Lu Zheng listened and ate slowly, saying little. His concern deepened.
He understood the difficulty better than anyone.

From anticipating the police and abandoning goods at the perfect moment, to killing and disposing of witnesses, to leaving an elegant ritual message, each move was precise, calm and far-sighted. It stood above anything An’an had faced before.
This was a mature, extensive, intricate and dangerous organization.
Shen Yu’an ate quietly, listening throughout. Mild and composed, he occasionally nodded. His manner matched the others: watchful, serious and curious.
He did not lead the conversation. He fitted into the group perfectly.
They talked for more than half an hour, finished lunch, cleared their trays and left together.
Afternoon sunlight was warmer, easing the early-autumn cool.
Most officers returned to the office for a short rest before afternoon work.
Soon, more than half were sleeping at their desks. The lively room fell quiet, with only soft breathing and wind outside.
Shen Yu’an did not habitually nap. He resumed reviewing the autopsy details.
Lu Zheng also stayed awake, tapping the desk as he reconsidered every part of the wasteland case, searching the mass of information for an overlooked opening.
His gaze kept drifting toward the quiet figure ahead. Whenever it settled there, concern about the case gave way to tenderness.
Watching Shen Yu’an’s quiet concentration deepened his affection.

The image of him taking the bullet returned countless times. The decisiveness of that instant was something Lu Zheng would never put aside. It made him willing to bend his own rules repeatedly and offer an undisguised care reserved for one person.
The afternoon remained quiet. No call, no field assignment, no sudden lead. Everything was routine.
Around three, the officers woke, rubbed their eyes and returned to work. Typing and low voices resumed.
Another technical update brought only routine progress. The domain remained unresolved, the paper had no matching source, and the toxicology work was still at the detailed comparison stage.
Long waits were part of criminal investigation.
Near six, the lowering sun filled the windows with warm orange light.
The day was almost over. With no unexpected call, everyone assumed it would remain one more quiet day of recovery and waiting.
As they began packing to leave on time, the team’s emergency landline rang sharply.
The urgent sound cut through the stillness and swept away the day’s ease.
Hands paused over files. People about to stand stopped. Every eye turned toward the duty-room phone.
The duty officer hurried over and answered, his expression changing at once.
He listened to the urgent account, brow tightening and fingers closing around the receiver.
Within seconds, he recorded the address, circumstances and scene features. As soon as he hung up, he turned and called out to the team.

“Urgent response. The sculpture park on the outskirts. Cleaning staff have found human remains inside the large central sculpture. Suspected concealed-body homicide. The arrangement is unusual, possibly deliberately ritualized.”
The office tightened instantly.
Every officer shed the relaxed posture and moved toward the equipment area for caps, body cameras, examination gear and arrest equipment.
The brief calm ended. Without warning, the mysterious organization’s new art-themed crime had begun.
Lu Zheng rose, all warmth and ease replaced by the sharp composure of command.
He scanned the team and gave clear orders. “Immediate assembly. Examination, field and interview teams split by assignment. Equipment on. We leave now.”
Everyone moved without delay.
His eyes found Shen Yu’an first. A restrained worry entered them, and his voice slowed. “You’re still recovering. Stay here on standby. Wait for our scene report.”
Instinctively, he reserved the safest, least demanding place for him.
A long drive, an unknown scene, difficult conditions, extended standing and possible surprises—he would not allow Shen Yu’an to strain the wound again.
The others accepted it. In their view, he was not ready for an unknown homicide scene.
But Shen Yu’an gently shook his head and picked up his forensic bag, lifting it onto one shoulder with a steady movement.
He looked at Lu Zheng with quiet persistence, gentle but firm, simply asking to go beside him.

“I can attend. I can’t strain the shoulder or carry weight, but routine examination and trace assessment are unaffected. With the full examination team there, I can help make the initial assessment more precise. I won’t delay the work or pull the wound.”
His explanation was calm and sincere, offering reasonable grounds.
A mild manner. Just enough consideration, just enough insistence, just enough desire to stand beside him.
Lu Zheng looked into those clear eyes, at the earnest expression, and could not bring himself to refuse.
He knew Shen Yu’an’s temperament: gentle but resilient, kind but never timid, conscientious about work and unwilling to avoid duty for personal reasons.
His concern finally yielded to affection.

After a few seconds, he relented. “You can come. But you stay beside me. No bending, no lifting or strain, no wandering off to examine things alone, no forcing yourself. Tell me immediately if anything hurts.”
Every instruction carried his particular care.
“All right.” Shen Yu’an’s eyes softened as he nodded. “I’ll do as you say.”
The simple answer eased Lu Zheng’s last concern.
They followed the team out, one behind the other, toward the police vehicles downstairs.
Three vehicles started, lights on and sirens low, and left the bureau for the sculpture park.
Evening traffic was easing as rush hour drew to a close. The cars moved steadily along the main roads, leaving the busy center for the open parkland beyond.
The forty-minute drive was solemn and quiet.
In front, field officers reviewed the known facts, anticipated the case’s direction and planned the initial assignments and possible conditions.
In the back, Lu Zheng and Shen Yu’an sat side by side in the small, quiet space.
The car moved gently. Wind and sirens came faintly through the windows, with the rest of the city shut out.
Halfway there, it crossed a speed bump with a sudden jolt.
Shen Yu’an had not taken the handhold. The movement shifted his balance, and his shoulder rested briefly against Lu Zheng.
Warm fabric touched warm fabric. The distance between them disappeared.
Only for an instant. Shen Yu’an steadied himself, sat upright and turned slightly. “Sorry. I lost my balance.”
Yet that fleeting contact softened the atmosphere.
Lu Zheng looked at the quiet apology, his severity giving way to indulgence.
He spoke low enough for only Shen Yu’an to hear. “It’s all right. It’s a long drive. There’ll be bumps. Lean back and rest if you’re tired. No need to hold yourself up.”
Shen Yu’an glanced at him, nodded and settled against the seat, eyelids lowered.
Behind them lay a still indifference.
He knew clearly that the sudden sculpture case was only the beginning of the game.
It was La Rose Éternelle’s first complete artistic, ritualized murder: the opening of the linked cases across twelve departments, the first piece placed on the board.
The scene would contain a meticulously shaped ritual, exacting artistic order, and an operative thoroughly conditioned to worship the organization and the divinity at its summit.

The police would spend days interviewing, examining the scene, screening evidence and tracing footage. Slowly, they would identify and arrest the operative, question them and reconstruct the case. After three or four days of painstaking investigation, they would solve it.
And in the end, they would recover only more fragments of dark-web access from the operative’s devices, gradually assembling a small edge of the vast organization.
The road ahead was layered in mist. Trouble gathered slowly.
The officers, full of vigilance, curiosity and concern, drove toward a carefully arranged game.
The person moving its pieces sat safely among them, quiet, gentle and harmless, accompanying them into the trap he had set.
The police cars sped on. Evening wind entered through a gap in the window and stirred loose hair.
A new chapter in the contest between light and shadow had taken its place.

alt.en: Lu Zheng helps move heavy case files from Shen Yu’an’s desk after his return to work.
alt.zh: 沈予安归队后，陆峥帮他移走桌上厚重的卷宗。

zh: 探照灯的冷光钉在雕塑广场的花岗岩表面，光线切割开浓稠的夜色，石材表面凹凸的纹路被照得清清楚楚。现场物证的封装工作持续推进，透明证物袋挨个收纳花瓣残片、石缝残留粉尘，每只袋子都标记采集点位与时间码，整齐码放在金属物证推车上。外勤队员架设第三道警戒封锁，把雕塑主体周边三米划为核心保护区域，隔绝一切外来触碰。
夜里郊野的风穿过树冠，裹挟着泥土与草木的寒气扫过整片广场。
沈予安退到警戒围挡外侧，手攥那瓶还没启封的矿泉水。他后背绷直，目光落向正在作业的勘验现场，肩头旧伤随着长时间站立不断传来酸胀，痛感顺着肩颈蔓延开来。制服布料遮盖住皮下的不适感，只有手指几次收拢瓶身，泄露身体承受的负荷。
陆峥签完现场临时勘验报备单据，把记录板递交给身旁队员，摘下耳麦握在手心，穿过忙碌的作业人员走向围挡外侧。现场所有人各有分工，蹲伏采集足迹的技术员、调试取证设备的外勤、对接检验科同步数据的联络员，没人分心留意队长的动向。
